title: SMD display type constants 1 and 2 are named the wrong way round
description: smd/smd_internal.h defines SMD_DISP_TYPE_MONO_LANDSCAPE=1 and SMD_DISP_TYPE_MONO_PORTRAIT=2, but SMD_$INIT (0x00E34E00/0x00E34E0E) gives type 1 max_x=0x31F, max_y=0x3FF (800x1024, portrait) and type 2 max_x=0x3FF, max_y=0x31F (1024x800, landscape).  The macro *values* are used in comparisons in alloc_hdm.c, copy_font_to_md_hdm.c, free_hdm.c, init.c and inq_disp_info.c, so a rename must swap the names only, never the values.
close_reason: Names swapped, values untouched: SMD_DISP_TYPE_MONO_PORTRAIT is now 1 and SMD_DISP_TYPE_MONO_LANDSCAPE is now 2 in smd/smd_internal.h.  Evidence: SMD_$INIT 0x00E34E00 gives type 1 max_x 0x31F / max_y 0x3FF (800x1024, portrait) and 0x00E34E0E gives type 2 max_x 0x3FF / max_y 0x31F (1024x800, landscape); both addresses now carry a gsk disassembly comment.  Every comparison that used the names was re-checked against its own assembly and its arms swapped where the *name* was load-bearing: alloc_hdm.c (0x00E6D9AC type 1 -> column 800, 0x00E6D9BA type 2 -> the 224-line band), free_hdm.c (0x00E6DA98 / 0x00E6DAB0), copy_font_to_md_hdm.c (0x00E1D7C2 type 1 -> scan line 1, 0x00E1D826 type 2 -> scan line 0x3D8), inq_disp_info.c (jump table arms).  init.c and free_hdm.c/alloc_hdm.c compile clean and smd/test/test_inq_disp_info.c asserts the two constants still hold 1 and 2 and that type 1 reports 800x1024.

title: sio/i_tstart.c passes NULL as TIME_$Q_ADD_CALLBACK's `when`, which the callee dereferences
description:
TIME_$Q_ADD_CALLBACK's second argument is the expiry time, and 0x00E16DF4/0x00E16DF8 dereference it unconditionally ('movea.l (0xc,A6),A0 / move.l (A0),(0xc,A2)').  time/time.h used to type it 'void *elem' so a NULL type-checked; it is now 'clock_t *when'.

sio/i_tstart.c:165 passes NULL there and '&now' as the fourth argument.  SIO_$I_TSTART's own call site pushes a real 6-byte local for the expiry: 0x00E1C8DC 'pea (-0x14,A6)' is the `when`, and 0x00E1C8D6 'pea (-0xc,A6)' - the buffer TIME_$ABS_CLOCK filled at 0x00E1C8B4 - is the `now`.  So the C should pass the address of a local delay value, not NULL.

Found while re-emitting time/q_add_callback.c (bead source-6r3m).  sio/ is not owned by any agent in the 2026-09-07 split, so this was left alone.
close_reason: Re-emitted sio/i_tstart.c (0xE1C7A8) and SIO_DELAY_RESTART (0xE1C690) block by block. The `when` argument is now the real 48-bit local at A6-0x14 that 0xE1C8DC pushes: the delay loop at 0xE1C864-0xE1C874 accumulates the two escape bytes into the LONGWORD at A6-0x12 (which straddles that value's high longword and low word) and 0xE1C88C multiplies by 250. Also corrected in the same pass, each from the listing: (1) the qelem is desc+0x08 (0xE1C8C4 'pea (0x8,A0)'), not a global, so sio_desc_t now carries a time_queue_elem_t delay_qelem at 0x08 and the fabricated SIO_DELAY_RESTART_QUEUE_ELEM at '0xE2DDDC' is gone from sio_data.c/sio_internal.h; (2) the interval is the zero clock at 0xE2DDDC that 0xE1C8C8 'pea (A5)' passes, now a named file-static constant cell; (3) 0xE1C808 'andi.w #-0xa1' clears 0x00A0, not 0x60; (4) SIO_DELAY_RESTART takes the two-level time_$callback_arg_t (0xE1C69C/0xE1C69E) and its 0xE1C6A2 mask 0xFFEE clears 0x10 AND 0x01; (5) SIO_$I_TSTART is a Pascal procedure - no call site reserves a result slot - so the invented uint16_t return is gone; (6) the byte-pointer casts of the 0x74 state word are replaced by word masks. New sio/test/test_i_tstart.c #includes the real .c: 11 tests, 0 failed. Ghidra: 0xE1C690 renamed SIO_DELAY_RESTART, prototypes and comments set on both.

description: asknode/internet_info.c passes NULL as PKT_$SAR_INTERNET's 10th argument (resp_buf). close_reason: asknode/internet_info.c now passes a real 32-byte local (sar_resp_info, A6-0xD8) as PKT_$SAR_INTERNET's tenth argument instead of NULL, matching 'pea (-0xd8,A6)' at 0x00E65716 in the 0x00E656FC-0x00E6573C argument block (seventeen arguments, 0x38 bytes of caller cleanup). title: ec: ADVANCE (0xE20728), the 4-byte C-callable entry that falls through into ADVANCE_INT, is missing from the tree
description:
SAU2 map domain_os.10.2.map, PROC1_ASM segment:

     E20718  EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH     MARKED
     E20728  ADVANCE                          MARKED
     E207D4  PROC1_$REORDER_READY

Image bytes at 0xE20728 are '20 6f 00 04' - movea.l (4,%sp),%a0 - and then
control falls straight through into ADVANCE_INT at 0xE2072C.  It is the
C-callable wrapper for the register-argument ADVANCE_INT and has four callers
in the image (0xE14760, 0xE7566E, 0xE26FE6, 0xE27060).

The tree has no ADVANCE at all: ec/advance_int.c defines only ADVANCE_INT, and
its object's .text starts at ADVANCE_INT.  Consequences:

1. The four call sites above call ADVANCE_INT directly in the C tree, losing
   the image's two-entry structure.
2. The bsr.b displacements in ec/sau2/advance.s and
   ec/sau2/advance_without_dispatch.s link 4 bytes short of the image
   (61 32 / 61 04 vs the image's 61 34 / 61 08) - see source-mc3k.

Fix: emit ADVANCE as ec/sau2/advance_entry.s (4 bytes, fall-through), list it
in sau2.ld between ec/sau2/advance_without_dispatch.o and ec/advance_int.o,
and retarget the four callers.  Owner: ec.
close_reason:
Fixed. ADVANCE_INT and ADVANCE_ALL_INT are hand-written assembly, not compiled Pascal: register argument in %a0, no link/unlk, two separate move.l saves instead of a compiler movem prologue, a hand-picked movem.l %d7/%a0-%a1/%a3 save/restore bracketing the PROC1_$SET_TS call, and ADVANCE_ALL_INT branching into the MIDDLE of ADVANCE_INT (0xE20736, past its 'move.l (%a0),%d7').  The SAU2 map has one object here - ADVANCE at 0xE20728, next symbol PROC1_$REORDER_READY at 0xE207D4, 0xAC bytes - holding all three entries.

So: ec/advance_int.c and ec/advance_all_int.c deleted, replaced by ec/sau2/advance_int.s (ADVANCE + ADVANCE_INT + ADVANCE_ALL_INT, 0xAC bytes).  ec/ec.h keeps all three prototypes and now declares ADVANCE.  Local cmp_l_imm macro for the two 'cmp.l #imm,%d0' the image spells 0xB0BC (gas only emits CMPI 0x0C80).

Section fix: gas pins the pre-created .text at 2**2 with no directive to lower it, which padded advance_all.o (0x16, ending 2-mod-4) to 0x18.  The four ec/sau2 files now open with '.section .text.ec_<name>,"ax",@progbits' + '.balign 2' (a .section-created section starts at 2**0); sau2.ld's ec lines gather by section name instead of object file.

Verification.  Object bytes (objcopy -O binary -j .text.ec_advance_int) vs 'gsk read 0xE20728 0xAC': 0xAC/0xAC bytes, differing only in the four relocated fields (0xE20757-9 TIME_$CLOCKH, 0xE2078E-F the PROC1_$TSVV lea, 0xE20799-B PROC1_$SET_TS, 0xE207B5 the bsr.w to proc1_$insert_into_ready_list).  Scratch link of all four ec/sau2 objects with -T at 0xE206EE and the externals --defsym'd at their image addresses: 0xE6 bytes, ZERO differing bytes against the image 0xE206EE..0xE207D3 - the two 'bsr.b ADVANCE_INT' now link as the image's 61 34 / 61 08, closing source-mc3k's leftover -4/+2.

Linked addresses (m68k-elf-nm on the scratch link / -Map of the real link):

  symbol                        image      scratch    real link   offset
  EC_$ADVANCE                   0xE206EE   0xE206EE   0xE00EDE    +0x00
  EC_$ADVANCE_ALL               0xE20702   0xE20702   0xE00EF2    +0x14
  EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH  0xE20718   0xE20718   0xE00F08    +0x2A
  ADVANCE                       0xE20728   0xE20728   0xE00F18    +0x3A
  ADVANCE_INT                   0xE2072C   0xE2072C   0xE00F1C    +0x3E
  ADVANCE_ALL_INT               0xE207C6   0xE207C6   0xE00FB6    +0xD8
  (next input section)          0xE207D4   -          0xE00FC4    +0xE6

Same gaps as the image, and the real link's map shows no *fill* anywhere inside the run.

Ghidra: function at 0xE207C6 renamed ADVANCE_ALL -> ADVANCE_ALL_INT; label PROC1_$TSVV added at 0xE205D2; decompiler comments on 0xE20728 / 0xE2072C / 0xE207C6 and disassembly comments on 0xE2078C / 0xE20796 / 0xE207D0.

Follow-ups filed: source-vi3h (proc1: rename TIMESLICE_TABLE to PROC1_$TSVV and move it into PROC1_ASM_DATA_SECTION - the only new undefined reference the link reports) and source-nbf? (smd: retarget disp1_int.s's two 'jsr (ADVANCE_INT).l' to ADVANCE).

Gates: make clean && make -k -j8 -> no error:/warning: lines, 0 relocation truncations; make test -> 182 tests, 0 failed; duplicate-global scan over 1431 objects empty.

title: Complete SVC_$ TRAP dispatcher implementations (TRAP 1-4, 6-8)
description:
## Overview

The SVC_$ subsystem implements Domain/OS syscall dispatching via M68K TRAP instructions.
Each TRAP number corresponds to a different argument count for syscall validation.

## Completed Work

- **TRAP #0** (0 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap0.s` - Simple syscalls, no argument validation
- **TRAP #1** (1 arg): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap1.s` - Validates USP + 1 arg, 66 entries at 0xe7b05c
- **TRAP #2** (2 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap2.s` - Validates USP + 2 args, 133 entries at 0xe7b094
- **TRAP #3** (3 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap3.s` - Validates USP + 3 args, 155 entries at 0xe7b0d8
- **TRAP #4** (4 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap4.s` - Validates USP + 4 args, 131 entries at 0xe7b120
- **TRAP #5** (5 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap5.s` - Complex syscalls, validates USP + 5 args, 99 entries
- **TRAP #6** - Not used for SVC calls (points to FIM_$UNDEF_TRAP)
- **TRAP #7** (6 args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap7.s` - Validates USP + 6 args, 59 entries at 0xe7b1d8
- **TRAP #8** (variable args): `domain_os/svc/sau2/trap8.s` - Variable-argument dispatcher, uses argcount lookup table, 56 entries at 0xe7b240
- **Shared tables**: `domain_os/svc/svc_tables.c` - C code, shared across SAUs
- **Header**: `domain_os/svc/svc.h` - Constants, syscall numbers, table declarations

## TRAP Numbering Note

TRAP #6 is NOT used for SVC dispatching - it points to FIM_$UNDEF_TRAP which generates a fault. The naming convention follows the actual M68K TRAP instruction numbers:
- SVC_$TRAP0-5: Handle M68K TRAP #0-5
- SVC_$TRAP7: Handles M68K TRAP #7 (6-arg syscalls)
- SVC_$TRAP8: Handles M68K TRAP #8 (variable-arg syscalls)

All SVC TRAP dispatchers are now complete.
close_reason: All SVC TRAP dispatchers (0-5, 7-8) implemented. Corrected naming: TRAP #6 is unused, TRAP #7 handles 6-arg syscalls, TRAP #8 handles variable-arg syscalls.

title: sio/sio.h _Static_assert(sizeof(sio_desc_t) == 0x78) is not guarded by ARCH_M68K and breaks host tests
description:
sio/sio.h:169 asserts sizeof(sio_desc_t) == 0x78 unconditionally.  sio_desc_t contains an ec_$eventcount_t and a params block that hold native pointers, so on a 64-bit host the record is wider and the assertion fails, e.g.

  suma/test/test_suma_data.c -> suma/suma_internal.h -> term/term.h is fine,
  but any host test that reaches term/term_internal.h -> sio/sio.h fails with
  'static assertion failed ... sio_desc_t must be 120 bytes'.

Every other layout assertion in the tree is written '#if defined(ARCH_M68K) ... #endif' for exactly this reason (see smd/smd_internal.h, dxm/dxm.h, ast/ast.h).  Guard this one the same way, and audit sio/sio.h and sio/sio_internal.h for other unguarded size/offset assertions.  Consequence today: suma/test/test_suma_data.c cannot #include term/enqueue_tpad.c, so it stubs TERM_$ENQUEUE_TPAD instead of exercising the real drain loop, and term/ has no host tests at all.
close_reason: sio_desc_t size assert guarded under ARCH_M68K (pointer-bearing record); term_internal.h now compiles on the host

ring: name the TRANSMIT half of ring_$stats_t (0x00..0x1B)
description:
The receive half was named from /etc/netmain while closing source-1a5o (see the comment on ring_$stats_t in ring/ring.h).  The same netmain display names the transmit half too:

  xmit_call  xmitcnt  xmit_nack  xmit_wack  xmit_orun
  xmit_apar  xmit_bus xmit_nortn xmit_modem xmit_error
  xmit_tim

That is two longs and nine words, which is exactly the shape of ring_$stats_t 0x00..0x1B (a word at +0x00, longs at +0x02 and +0x06, then nine words at 0x0A..0x1A) - xmit_call and xmitcnt are the two %7ld fields in netmain's display, so they are the longs at +0x02/+0x06.

What is missing is the ORDER of the nine words.  The receive half could be pinned because three of its counters are logged with named status codes (0x00110010 'bad checksum', 0x00110013 'receive bus error') and because the RING_$SWDIAG_DATA mirror repeats the same block at a uniform -0x1A.  Nothing similar has been found for the transmit side yet.  Look at RING_$SENDP / RING_$INT / the transmit-completion status decode: 0x00110014 'transmit bus error' and 0x00110016 'memory parity error during transmit' are the obvious anchors if either is logged next to a counter bump.

The fields at 0x00..0x1B currently carry guessed names (xmit_count, success_count, no_response_count, collision_count, abort_count, noresp_count, parity_count, delayed_count, biphase_count, unexpected_count, retry_count).

Evidence: strings -a sr10.4-install/install/ri.apollo.os.v.10.4/etc/netmain, the 'Error counts for !+rx:' format block.
close_reason: Closed

title: dir/test/test_alloc_split_page.c and test_finalize_split.c carry private copies of dir_insert_ctx_t
description: Both files '#define DIR_INTERNAL_H' to keep the real header out and then declare their own dir_insert_ctx_t, uid_t and status_$t. The private ctx types the directory handle as uintptr_t, so it silently disagrees with the real one (uint32_t plus NAME_$HANDLE_TO_PTR), and every layout change to the real struct has to be mirrored by hand - the NAME_$HANDLE_TO_PTR work for source-qu3v had to add a local #define to each of them. They should include dir/dir_internal.h like dir/test/test_insert_entry.c does and mock only the callees. Also note the audit's finding that a test which re-implements its subject proves nothing.
close_reason: dir/test/test_alloc_split_page.c and dir/test/test_finalize_split.c now '#include "dir/dir_internal.h"' and mock only their callees (dir_$map_page, dir_$purify_split_pages, dir_$truncate_pages, AST_$GET_SEG_MAP, AST_$PURIFY, UID_$GEN, CRASH_SYSTEM). Removed from both: the '#define DIR_INTERNAL_H' that kept the real header out, the private dir_insert_ctx_t (whose handle was uintptr_t where the real one is uint32_t), the private 'typedef uint32_t status_$t' (the real one is int32_t) and the '#define uid_t dir_uid_t' shim, plus the local '#define NAME_$HANDLE_TO_PTR' identity macro. Both now compile in name/handle_map.c and build their handles with NAME_$PTR_TO_HANDLE, exactly as dir/test/test_insert_entry.c does. '#include <stdlib.h>' was dropped from both (neither used it) because on macOS it drags in sys/types.h's uid_t and collides with base.h. test_alloc_split_page: 8 passed, 0 failed; test_finalize_split: 7 passed, 0 failed.

title: ring: name the receive error counters in ring_$stats_t / ring_$swdiag_t
description:
ring/ring.h: the per-unit receive error counters at ring_$stats_t+0x20..0x32 and the RING_$SWDIAG_DATA mirror words at +0x06..0x16 are still named after the rcv_csr bit that drives them (rcv_stat_20_cnt etc).  RING_$GET_STATS (0x00E76950) copies the block out verbatim and reports its size as 0x3C, so the kernel never names the fields; they are not in the SR10.4 status-code database or in the headers in this tree either.  The real names would have to come from a user-space consumer of RING_$GET_STATS (netstat / lcnet) or from Apollo documentation.

The bit-to-counter decode order and the swdiag pairing are now documented on ring_$stats_t and in the Ghidra decompiler comment at 0x00E75F60.

RESOLVED (2026-09-06): ring_channel_t.open_word is the driver interface version the channel was opened with - ring_$open_internal rejects anything above 1 at 0x00E76BAE with 0x00310010, 'driver version mismatch'.  Renamed to open_version.
close_reason:
The names WERE recoverable - not from a header in this tree, but from the user-space consumer the bead pointed at.  'strings -a' on sr10.4-install/install/ri.apollo.os.v.10.4/etc/netmain yields its 'Error counts for <node>:' display, which formats the ASKNODE ring statistics record field by field and names exactly eleven receive fields - one printed %7ld (rcvcnt) and ten %7wd (rcveor, rcvcrc, rcvtim, rcvbus, rcvmodem, rcvpkt, rcvovr, rcvapar, rcvxerr, rcvhcsum).  That is exactly the shape of ring_$stats_t 0x1C..0x33: one long plus ten words.  (sau2-headers/ has only asknode.h and netman.h and neither carries counter names; sys/ins has no ring insert.)

Three offsets are pinned directly by the image, so the ordering is not a guess:
- +0x1C rcvcnt: the only long in the receive half, 'addq.l #1,(0x1c,A3)' once per accepted packet at 0x00E75EEC.
- +0x26 rcvbus: the rcv_csr bit-6 arm logs the constant at 0x00E76044 = 0x00110013, which the 10.4 database names 'receive bus error', and CRASH_SYSTEMs before the bump (0x00E75FB4-0x00E75FBE).
- +0x32 rcvhcsum: the header-checksum arm logs 0x00E76040 = 0x00110010, 'bad checksum' (0x00E75ED8-0x00E75EE2).

Reading netmain's rows in the order (rcvcnt, rcveor, rcvcrc, rcvtim), (rcvbus, rcvmodem, rcvpkt, rcvovr, rcvapar), (rcvxerr, rcvhcsum) puts rcvbus on +0x26 and rcvhcsum on +0x32 - both anchors at once - and leaves +0x2C, the one word the CSR decode never touches, as rcvovr, a DMA overrun rather than a CSR condition.

Final mapping (stats offset, rcv_csr bit from ring_$validate_receive 0x00E75F60-0x00E76032, swdiag mirror):
  0x20 rcveor   bit 5      swdiag +0x06
  0x22 rcvcrc   bit 8      swdiag +0x08
  0x24 rcvtim   bit 9      swdiag +0x0A
  0x26 rcvbus   bit 6      swdiag +0x0C, never written (it crashes first)
  0x28 rcvmodem bit 3      swdiag +0x0E
  0x2A rcvpkt   bit 10/11  swdiag +0x10; the split is counted in RING_$RCV_ESB (bit 10, 0xE261BA) and RING_$RCV_BIPHASE (bit 11, 0xE261B8)
  0x2C rcvovr   none       swdiag +0x12, never written
  0x2E rcvapar  bit 0      swdiag +0x14
  0x30 rcvxerr  bit 7      swdiag +0x16
  0x32 rcvhcsum -          no mirror

Every swdiag mirror is its stats counter minus exactly 0x1A, so RING_$SWDIAG_DATA+0x06 is the same ten-word block in the same order, and the two mirrors the receive path never writes are precisely the two counters that have no CSR arm - which independently confirms the slot numbering.  ring_$swdiag_t's _r0c and _r12 are named rcvbus and rcvovr accordingly.

Renamed across ring/ring.h, ring/rcv.c, ring/int.c and ring/test/test_rcv.c; good_rcv_count -> rcvcnt as well, since the same evidence names it and it anchors the layout.  New _Static_asserts on ring_$stats_t.rcveor/rcvbus/rcvovr/rcvpkt/rcvhcsum and ring_$swdiag_t.rcveor/rcvpkt/rcvxerr.  ring builds clean; ring/test/test_rcv.c passes 25 assertions.

The TRANSMIT half at 0x00..0x1B is still guessed - netmain names it xmit_call/xmitcnt (the two longs at +0x02/+0x06) plus nine words, but nothing in the image pins their order yet.  Filed as source-11rf.

Ghidra: decompiler comment with the whole table on 0x00E75F60; disassembly comments on 0x00E75ED8, 0x00E75EEC and 0x00E75FB4.

title: ASKNODE_$INTERNET_INFO copies 42 bytes of MEM_$MEM_REC, image copies 86
description:
asknode/internet_info.c:97 copies 21 *words* from MEM_$MEM_REC into the reply at result+0x72.  The image copies 21 longwords plus one word:

  00e6481c  moveq #0x14,D3
  00e6481e  lea (0x72,A1),A3
  00e64824  move.l (A0)+,(A3)+
  00e64826  dbf D3w,0x00e64824
  00e6482a  move.w (A0)+,(A3)+

that is 0x56 = 86 bytes, which is exactly sizeof(mem_$mem_rec_t) (mem/mem.h) and reaches the end of MEM_$PAGE_ERRORS at 0xE2298A.  The tree therefore drops the whole per-page error table from the reply.  Note the destination also overlaps the MMAP_$REAL_PAGES word the very next statement writes at result+0x76, so the fix must keep the store order.  Found while doing source-eqom; asknode/ not owned by that pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: smd_cursor_pos_t field order does not match the packed position
description: The kernel carries a cursor position as one longword with X in the LOW half and Y in the HIGH half (proved in smd_$write_str_clip_impl 0x00E703F6: the low half is clipped against +0x56/+0x58 and shifted right by 4 to index words within a scan line, the high half against +0x5A/+0x5C).  In big-endian terms that makes offset 0x00 the Y and 0x02 the X, but smd/smd.h's smd_cursor_pos_t declares {int16_t x; int16_t y}.  smd/smd_internal.h now provides SMD_POS_X/SMD_POS_Y/SMD_POS_MAKE and the hot paths (hw->cursor_pos, SMD_GLOBALS.default_cursor_pos, saved_cursor_pos, smd_event_entry_t.pos) use a plain uint32_t.  smd_cursor_pos_t is still exported to other subsystems (SMD_$DISPLAY_CURSOR, SMD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR_POS, TPAD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR), so fixing it needs those callers checked too.
close_reason: smd_cursor_pos_t is now 'typedef uint32_t' - the packed longword the kernel actually manipulates - and SMD_POS_X/SMD_POS_Y/SMD_POS_MAKE moved from smd_internal.h to smd.h so external callers get them too.  This is the endian-safe fix: a {int16_t;int16_t} struct can only be right on one byte order, whereas every SMD entry point loads the position with a single move.l (SMD_$DISPLAY_CURSOR 0x00E6E096, SMD_$CLEAR_CURSOR 0x00E6E0C0, SMD_$SET_TP_CURSOR 0x00E6E976, SMD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR_POS 0x00E6E7EC) and smd_$write_str_clip_impl 0x00E703F6 takes the LOW half as X and the high half as Y.  All seven in-tree users already cast to uint32_t*, so the casts simply went away; the one cross-subsystem call, TPAD_$SET_UNIT_CURSOR, now takes an explicit (smd_$pos_t *) cast with a comment - tpad/tpad.h's union smd_$pos_t already declares {int16_t y; int16_t x}, which is the m68k memory image of the same value and independent corroboration.  _Static_assert on sizeof == 4.  The same row-first convention was found in smd_hdm_pos_t and fixed there too (see source-nhzy): SMD_$COPY_FONT_TO_HDM 0x00E70328/0x00E70330 uses +0x00 as the scan line and 0x00E70340 uses +0x02 as the column.

title: Emit acl_$eval_acl_entries (0x00E46172), the ACL entry walk
description: 626 bytes.  Called by acl_$eval_rights (0x00E46878) as (cache_slot, sids, proj_uids, prot).  Walks slot->entries (0x34, stride 0x20, slot->entry_count at +0x0E) matching a three-part SID against each entry's person/group/org UIDs with UID_$NIL acting as a wildcard, ANDs the entry's rights word at entry+0x1A with prot->subsys_rights, and has a second pass from 0x00E46250 that accumulates rights across matching entries.  Returns a 16-bit rights word.  Prototype and TODO are in acl/acl_internal.h.
close_reason: Emitted acl/eval_acl_entries.c, every basic block of 0x00E46172-0x00E463E2 traced.  Structure recovered: acl_$acl_entry_t is 0x20 bytes (person 0, group 8, org 0x10, rights word 0x1A) and entries are numbered from 1 - the direct form lea (0x14,slot,i*0x20) at 0x00E462DE proves entry i is at slot+0x14+i*0x20, i.e. slot+0x34 is entry 1.  Three phases, all of them present: (1) 0x00E461A2 person scan running while entry->person != UID_$NIL with NIL group/org acting as wildcards, returning prot->subsys_rights & entry->rights (0x00E4621E); (2) 0x00E46250 nine passes - the dbf count is moveq #0x8 and pass 0 is selected by the Z flag that move.w D1w,D3w leaves at 0x00E46260 - copying the caller's full 36-byte SID block on pass 0 and substituting proj_uids[k-1] for the group SID on passes 1..8 (lea (-0x8,A2) at 0x00E46280, A2 advanced once per pass), OR-ing rights from prot->group_rights or from every matching entry and stopping at the first NIL project (0x00E4628E); (3) 0x00E46364, only when nothing matched, the org record then an org-only entry scan that branches back into phase 1's match block (0x00E463AE) and finally prot->world_rights.  Two original quirks preserved and documented: phase 3 reloads only the index from max_index and keeps A0's entry pointer, and the subsys/owner/group/org/world rights are all zero-extended BYTES (clr.w D0w + move.b), so a 16-bit entry rights word can never keep its high half.  22 unit tests in acl/test/test_eval_acl_entries.c, all passing.

title: win: DISK_INIT (0x00e19986) is WIN-internal and has no C file
description:
disk/misc/disk_init.c was removed (bead source-5ky): it was never built, contained an extern FUN_00e190bc reference and a stale EC_$WAIT call, and it does not belong to the disk subsystem.

Evidence: DISK_INIT lives at 0x00e19986, entirely inside the WIN (Winchester driver) code region, and its only callers are WIN_$DINIT (0x00e19d32) and FUN_00e194b4 (0x00e194e0).  Its helper FUN_00e190bc is called from WIN_$ANSI_COMMAND (0x00e1916a), SEEK (0x00e195d8) and DISK_INIT itself.  So the prototype stays in win/win.h; it must NOT move to disk/disk.h.

Work: emit DISK_INIT under win/ (566 bytes, ANSI drive identification for Micropolis 1203 / PRIAM 3450 / PRIAM 7050), identify and rename FUN_00e190bc, and convert its EC_$WAIT call (0xe19..., three eventcounts) to the by-value ec_$wait_ecs_t / ec_$wait_vals_t signature in ec/ec.h.
close_reason: DISK_INIT (0x00E19986, 566 bytes) emitted as win/disk_init.c with win/test/test_disk_init.c (9 tests).  It is WIN-internal: bsr-called with the status in D0 and no Pascal result slot.  Its seven arguments are (unit:w, sub_unit:w, ^total_blocks:long, ^blocks_per_track:word, ^heads:word, ^geometry:word[2], ^drive_id:word); WIN_$DINIT swaps its own first two when it calls it (0x00E19D2C/0x00E19D30).  Ten-attempt retry loop (moveq #9 + dbf, 0x00E199C8/0x00E19AA2), the spin-up branch gated on bit 0 of the general status, and the geometry table for Micropolis 1203 / PRIAM 3450 / PRIAM 7050 including the original's fall-through on an unrecognised id (0x00E19B80 sets the error but still multiplies with D1 holding the drive id, overwriting *total_blocks).  FUN_00e190bc identified and renamed in Ghidra to WAIT_FOR_CONTROLLER: it spins on bit 15 (busy) of the drive status word at regs+6 with a 3-tick TIME_$CLOCKH deadline (status_$disk_controller_busy 0x00080002 on timeout) then maps bit 7 to status_$disk_not_ready; emitted as win/wait_for_controller.c with win/test/test_wait_for_controller.c (5 tests).  The EC_$WAIT at 0x00E19A66 is converted to the by-value ec_$wait_ecs_t / ec_$wait_vals_t form: ecs {&WIN_EC[unit], &TIME_$CLOCKH, NULL}, vals {ec+1, TIME_$CLOCKH+0x78, 0}.  The prototype stayed in win/win.h.

title: SMD: 'pea (d,PC)' constants modelled as variables holding the address
description: Five SMD files declare e.g. 'static const uint32_t cursor_lock_data_1 = 0x00E6E59A;' and then pass its ADDRESS to a callee that dereferences it, so the callee reads 0x00E6E59A's low half instead of the value of the code-region cell.  Affected: add_trk_rects_internal.c:21-22, clr_trk_rect.c:20-21, del_trk_rect.c:20-21, disable_tracking.c:16-17, stop_tp_cursor.c:13-14, set_unit_cursor_pos.c:13-14.  The correct idiom is a named file-static holding the cell's VALUE (see smd/display_logo.c smd_$logo_unit_2, or the shared SMD_ACQ_LOCK_DATA / SMD_SYNC_LOCK_DATA / SMD_ONE_LOCK_DATA in smd_internal.h).  Read each cell with 'gsk read' and give it the right value and type; 0x00E6E458 is a BYTE holding 0xFF, 0x00E6E45A a byte holding 0x00, 0x00E6D92A / 0x00E6DFF8 words holding 1, 0x00E6D92C a word holding 0.
close_reason: All six files fixed.  Cell values read with gsk: 0x00E6E59A = 'ff ff' (the word -1), 0x00E6E458 = 'ff' (boolean true), 0x00E6D92C = 0x0000, 0x00E6DFF8 = 0x0001, 0x00E6D92A = 0x0001, 0x00E6E45A = 0x00.  SHOW_CURSOR dereferences argument 2 as a word (0x00E6E1EA 'move.w (A1),D6w', and 0x00E6E256 'cmpi.w #-0x1,D6w' is what makes -1 mean 'keep the current cursor number') and argument 3 as a byte (0x00E6E1EE 'move.b (A2),D5b').  Resolved 'pea (d,PC)' targets (instruction + 2 + d): add_trk_rects_internal 0x00E6E582 -> 0x00E6E59A and 0x00E6E57E -> 0x00E6E458; clr_trk_rect 0x00E6E74C/0x00E6E748; del_trk_rect 0x00E6E702/0x00E6E6FE; disable_tracking 0x00E6E496 -> 0x00E6D92C and 0x00E6E492 -> 0x00E6E458; stop_tp_cursor 0x00E6EB2E/0x00E6EB2A; set_unit_cursor_pos 0x00E6E7D2/0x00E6E7CE.  Added named cells SMD_MINUS_ONE_DATA / SMD_TRUE_DATA / SMD_FALSE_DATA (const, code segment) to smd_internal.h + smd_data.c beside the existing SMD_ACQ_LOCK_DATA / SMD_SYNC_LOCK_DATA / SMD_ONE_LOCK_DATA, and deleted the six file statics that held the ADDRESSES.  Ghidra: labels SMD_$MINUS_ONE_DATA / SMD_$TRUE_DATA / SMD_$FALSE_DATA / SMD_$ONE_LOCK_DATA / SMD_$ACQ_LOCK_DATA / SMD_$SYNC_LOCK_DATA with short/byte types, plus EOL comments at all twelve pea sites.

title: smd: v3 font header reads +0x34 two contradictory ways
description:
SMD_$WRITE_STRING (00e70390) has two v3 paths that disagree about the character map:
  - draw path 00e70426: `add.l (0x34,A2),D0` then `move.b (0x0,A2,D0*0x1),D1b` -- +0x34 is a LONGWORD byte offset to the map, and 00e70438 `adda.l (0x38,A2),A1` (biased by `lea (-0x8,A2)`) makes +0x38 the glyph-data offset.
  - width-measure path 00e70634: `move.b (0x34,A2,D0w*0x1),D1b\' -- the map is inline at +0x34.
Only one can be right; the other is an original bug (the measure path is the less-exercised one).

smd/smd_internal.h now spells the region as a union so both readings are visible and the proven metrics fit: 0x42 hdm_size (SMD_$LOAD_FONT 00e6dcbe), 0x48 descent (00e704fc), 0x4A ascent (00e7056c), 0x5A char_spacing (00e7060e), 0x6E default_missing (00e7063a).  The previously asserted char_map_offset@0x1A / glyph_data_offset@0x1E were guesses and are now field_1a / field_1e.

Follow-up: decide which reading is correct and collapse the union; smd/write_str_clip.c:173,292 use font_v3->char_map[c] (the inline reading).

title: NET_IO_$CREATE_PORT clears one byte past a ROUTE_$USER_STAT record
description:
The record clear loop at 0x00E5A66C-0x00E5A67E in NET_IO_$CREATE_PORT (0x00E5A4A4) is 'move.w #0x90,D1w / clr.w D0w / movea.l (0x44,A3),A1 / clr.b (0x0,A1,D0w) / addq.w #0x1,D0w / dbf D1w', i.e. 0x91 iterations writing offsets 0x00..0x90.  The ROUTE_$USER_STAT record stride is 0x90 (scan loop at 0x00E5A5CC, index arithmetic at 0x00E5A656-0x00E5A664), so it zeroes the first byte of the following record.  For record 4 that byte is the first byte of ROUTE_$PID (0xE88216), the pid PROC1_$CREATE_P returned in ROUTE_$INIT_ROUTING (0x00E69D60).

Reproduced as written wherever NET_IO_$CREATE_PORT is emitted; documented in route/route_internal.h and pinned by route/test/test_user_stat.c:test_clear_loop_overruns_by_one.  net_io/ is not modelled yet, so nothing in the tree performs the clear.  Close this when net_io/create_port.c is written with the overrun reproduced and commented.

title: xns_$os_send_rec_t: 0x00..0x17 unidentified
description: xns/xns.h's xns_$os_send_rec_t (the 0x48-byte record XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND, 0x00E18256, takes as its second argument) has +0x18..+0x47 recovered but nothing for +0x00..+0x17.  RIP_$SEND, whose copy lives at A6-0x48, never writes that range and XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND never reads it, so it must belong to another caller.  Enumerate the other callers of 0x00E18256 and identify the head.
close_reason: xns_$os_send_rec_t +0x00..0x17 is a destination xns_$net_addr_t followed by a source one. Evidence: XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND's build-header path copies exactly those 24 bytes into the IDP header at +0x06 with 'lea (0x6,A1),A4 / moveq #0x17,D1 / move.b (A3)+,(A4)+ / dbf' (0x00E18336-0x00E1833E), and the connected alternative at 0x00E18318-0x00E18332 fills the SAME 24 header bytes with two three-longword copies from the channel's dest_network (chan+0xA4) and src_network (chan+0xB0) - which is exactly xns_$net_addr_t twice. IDP header +0x06 is dest network/host/socket and +0x12 is source network/host/socket. Confirmed on the caller side: XNS_IDP_$SEND copies 24 bytes from the user's record at 0x00E18B04. The bead's premise held for the other two callers - RIP_$SEND never writes A6-0x48..-0x31 (grep of 0x00E871B6 finds no store in that range) and XNS_ERROR_$SEND writes only +0x18..+0x24 of its static record at 0x00E2B29C - because both build their own IDP header and their channels leave the build-header flag clear.

title: TTY: confirm historical names for char classes 0x05/0x06 (XON vs XOFF)
description: tty/tty.h: class 0x05 (0xE1BA42) sets TTY_STATUS_XON_XOFF and calls the xon/xoff handler with TRUE; class 0x06 (0xE1BA60) clears it, calls with FALSE and advances the output EC.  That reads as 0x05=stop-output(^S) and 0x06=resume(^Q), i.e. the reverse of the current TTY_CHAR_CLASS_XON/XOFF names.  Confirm against TTY_$I_SET_DFL_FUNCS' default table (0xE6720E) before renaming.  TODO comment is in tty/tty.h.
close_reason: Resolved from the two default tables plus the handlers. TTY_$I_INIT (0x00E33284) copies the default function characters from 0x00E351D8 (labelled tty_$i_dfl_func_chars); TTY_$I_SET_DFL_FUNCS (0x00E67274) sets A5=0x00E8242C whose first 18 words are the function-index -> char-class table (tty_$i_dfl_func_classes), with the enable mask 0x0001FFFF at 0x00E82450. Function index 13 = char 0x13 (^S, DC3 = XOFF) -> class 0x05; index 14 = char 0x11 (^Q, DC1 = XON) -> class 0x06. That matches the handlers: class 0x05 (0x00E1BA42) bset.b #2,(0x9,A2) and calls the handler with st (TRUE); class 0x06 (0x00E1BA60) bclr.b #2 and calls with clr.w (FALSE) then advances the output EC. tty_$i_put_chars returns 0 while bit 2 is set (0x00E1B032). So the old names were reversed. Renamed TTY_CHAR_CLASS_XOFF=0x05, TTY_CHAR_CLASS_XON=0x06 and TTY_STATUS_XON_XOFF -> TTY_STATUS_OUTPUT_STOPPED; fixed tty/tty.h, tty/i_rcv.c, tty/i_put_chars.c and both tty tests. Ghidra: labels tty_$i_dfl_func_classes/_chars/_enable_mask, EOL comments at 0x00E1BA42/52/60/6E, 0x00E67284, 0x00E33284.

description: base/base.h:64 has 'typedef long status_$t;'. title: REM_FILE_$SERVER split-reply bulk area at A6+0x60 is unmodelled
description: rem_file/server.c: when reply_len > 0x200 the original loads A4 with 'lea (0x60,A6),A4' (0x00E6417C) - an address ABOVE REM_FILE_$SERVER's own frame, i.e. inside the caller's (0x00E11AC2).  The C re-emission has no portable spelling for that, so the split path currently sends a NULL bulk pointer with the correct length.  Resolving it needs the caller decompiled so the shared buffer becomes an explicit object.
close_reason: The split-reply bulk area is now an explicit object. Derived the geometry from the caller: NETWORK_$REQUEST_SERVER (0x00E118DC) calls REM_FILE_$SERVER with a bare 'jsr' and no arguments at 0x00E11AC2; its 'link.w A6,-0xe0' plus the nine-register movem (0x24 bytes) leave SP at A6_caller-0x104, so A6_callee = A6_caller-0x10C and the 'lea (0x60,A6),A4' at 0x00E6417C addresses A6_caller-0xAC - a longword local NETWORK_$REQUEST_SERVER writes at 0x00E11A68/0x00E11A72. In reply-record terms it is simply reply+0x200 (the reply is based at A6-0x1A0), i.e. the original overrunning its own frame. rem_file_server_frame_t now carries a trailing caller_frame[0x460] so reply+0x200+REM_FILE_BULK_MAX stays inside one object, the _Static_assert on the frame size became an assert on where the frame proper ends, and the send passes RSP_P(&f, 0x60) instead of NULL. Two new tests in rem_file/test/test_server.c prove the pointer is reply+0x200 and that bytes DIR_$SERVER writes there are the bytes sent; 26 tests, 0 failed.

title: TODO: STOP_$WATCH has two unbounded indices (op >= 8 and parent >= 16)
description: stop/watch.c: (1) the operation branch table at 0x00E81854 has entries only for 2..7 but the guard at 0x00E8183E is 'cmp.w #1 / ble' with no upper bound, so op >= 8 jumps into the middle of instructions; the C default: case does nothing. (2) the parent slot index at 0x00E81988 is only checked with 'blt', so a parent >= 16 indexes past STOPWATCH_SLOTS; reproduced as written. Both marked TODO(source-2vy1) in stop/watch.c.
close_reason: Verified and mirrored.  (1) The operation code has NO upper bound (0x00E8183E is 'cmp.w #1,D3 / ble' and nothing else).  The table's island runs 0x00E81858..0x00E81896, and operation 7's entry is a FOUR-byte bsr.w, so ops 8, 9 and 10 land on real instruction boundaries: 8 -> 0x00E81864 'ori.b #0x81,D6' (a register the exit movem restores) then the common exit, 9 -> 0x00E81866 'move.l D1,(A1)', a long poke that MISSES the DISK_$DIAG gate operation 7 goes through, 10 -> 0x00E81868 the exit branch itself.  All three are now emitted (STOP_OP_ORI_D6 / STOP_OP_POKE_LONG_UNGATED / STOP_OP_NOP in stop/stop.h).  Op 11 lands on the gate at 0x00E8186A entered by jmp not bsr, so its rts returns to the caller with the frame still linked and its refusal path pops the caller's return address; 12+ land mid-instruction -- documented, not reproducible.  (2) The parent slot index is guarded only by 'blt' (0x00E81988).  The scaling is 'lsl.w #6' (wraps mod 0x10000) and the base is reached with a sign-extending 'adda.w' (0x00E81990), and 0x40*0x400 == 0x10000, so the slot number is the low ten bits with 0x200..0x3FF coming out NEGATIVE.  stop/watch.c now computes exactly that.  Tests test_op_above_table and test_parent_unbounded in stop/test/test_watch.c cover both; 14 tests, 0 failed.

title: VOLX table base is off by one entry (0xE825E4 vs 0xE82604)
description:
Found during the SR10.2 SAU2 link-map sweep (source-9y3r).

volx/volx_internal.h used to claim that the Ghidra labels VFMT_$FORMATN (0xE825E4) and ERROR_$PRINT (0xE825F4) were 'misidentified labels that actually point into the VOLX table'.  The SAU2 link map disproves that: those two addresses are 0x10-byte data segments VFMT_$FORMATN and VFMT_$WRITEN (the procedure-variable descriptors), and the VOLX table is its own segment:

    D    E825E4  VFMT_$FORMATN     size = 10
    D    E825F4  VFMT_$WRITEN      size = 10
    D    E82604  VOLX_              size = C0
    D    E826C4  DISK_              size = 64

0xC0 = 6 entries of 0x20, so the table is exactly E82604..E826C4 and holds volume indices 1..6.

That exposes an inconsistency in the tree.  volx_internal.h documents the addressing correctly -- 'ptr = base + (vol_idx << 5); dir_uid is at ptr - 0x20' , which puts index 1 at 0xE82604 -- but both VOLX_ENTRY(idx) (= &VOLX_$TABLE_BASE[idx]) and VOLX_DIR_UID_FIELD(idx) (= base + (idx << 5)) omit the -0x20, so with VOLX_$TABLE_BASE = 0xE82604 they address index 1 at 0xE82624 and index 6 at 0xE826E4, i.e. one entry past the end of the segment and into DISK_.

Either VOLX_$TABLE_BASE should be 0xE825E4 (the biased base the code actually holds) or the macros need the -0x20.  Decide from the disassembly which the original does, fix it, and add a _Static_assert / comment citing 'D E82604 VOLX_ size = C0'.  Left alone by source-9y3r because that sweep was renames only.
close_reason: Closed

- the reply goes to header_copy+0x12 (the IDP source address) - 'pea (-0xe,A6)' at 0x00E68BD2 - not to a hand-built address with socket 1.
- RIP_$SEND's five arguments and the five-attempt retry loop at 0x00E68BB8-0x00E68C10, with clock_t {0, 0x61A8} and TIME_$WAIT's delay-type constant now a named file-static cell for 'pea (0x232,PC)' -> 0x00E68E26.
- request arm, internet: 'tst.b (-0x2af,A6)' at 0x00E68C20 is the low byte of PKT_$BRK_INTERNET_HDR's info word 0; info_out[0] = 0x20 at 0x00E68C32; PKT_$SEND_INTERNET's fifteen arguments each mapped to their push (0x00E68C3A-0x00E68C7E), with 'pea (0x1de,PC)' -> 0x00E68E28 = RIP_$ANNOUNCE_EXTRA.
- response arm: D4 is reloaded from header_copy+0x06, the IDP DESTINATION network, at 0x00E68C9E (was header+0x1A); ROUTE_$PORTP is 0-indexed (0x00E68C8A); the protected-port set is 'btst.l D1,#0x38' at 0x00E68CAE; HINT_$ADD_NET takes the longword network by value (0x00E68D0E); the short-circuit routing test at 0x00E68D18-0x00E68D58 is emitted arm for arm including the always-taken 'tst.b D3b / bmi' at 0x00E68D38; the non-XNS source host is '(old & 0xFFF00000) | src_node' on host[2..5] only (0x00E68D78-0x00E68D86); the update loop runs entry_count times, not entry_count-1 - 'subq.w #1,D1w' at 0x00E68D8C feeds a dbf.
- name-register arm: the packet-type check is header_copy+0x05 == 0xBE at 0x00E68DD0.
- RIP_$PROCESS_REQUEST: request entries at request+2+6i (0x00E68904); STD reads routes[1] (+0x27) and clamps the metric UP to 0x10 with an unsigned longword compare (0x00E6893C), internet reads routes[0] (+0x13) and answers 0x11 (0x00E6894E); the full-table scan is 64 slots of stride 0x2C from 0xE263BC with state (flags & 0xC0) >> 6 tested by 'btst.l D1,#6' (0x00E6899C) and capped at 0x5A (0x00E689EE).

Two original defects found and preserved with TODOs -> bead source-u9wy: A6-0x4F0 is written only in the XNS arm (0x00E68A5A) but read on both paths (0x00E688F6), and the name-register node-id mask applies a +6 record accessor to a pointer already four bytes into the record (0x00E68DE0-0x00E68DEE).

title: Recover the 122-byte ring_info_t returned by NETWORK_$RING_INFO
description:
network/network.h now models ring_info_t as the real 122-byte (0x7A) record instead of an opaque uint8_t[122].

The layout comes from the responder, NETWORK_$PROCESS_PAGING_REQUEST case 0x0E (0x00E11246..0x00E112D4), whose reply record base is A2-0x1E8 (+0x00 reply type 0x000F, +0x02 status longword, +0x06 payload), so the ring_info_t base is A0-0x1E2 and an instruction storing at (-0x1E2+N,A0) writes offset N.  It fills exactly 0x7A bytes and nothing beyond, matching NETWORK_$RING_INFO's 30-longs-plus-a-word copy from response+6.  A5 there is the network module base 0x00E248FC (pinned by 'lea (0xe248fc).l,A5' at 0x00E10402).

Layout, with the storing instruction per field:
  0x00 word   _unknown_00  const 3                     0x00E112BC   STILL UNNAMED
  0x02 byte   diskless     NETWORK_$DISKLESS 0xE24C4C  0x00E112C2
  0x03 byte   _unknown_03  never written                            STILL UNNAMED
  0x04 long   mother_node  NETWORK_$MOTHER_NODE 0xE24C0C 0x00E112C8
  0x08 0x3C   stats        RING_$STATS[0] 0xE261E0     0x00E11266 (15 longs)
  0x44 0x10   failure_rec  NETWORK_$FAILURE_REC 0xE24BF4 0x00E11256 (4 longs)
  0x54 0x1E   swdiag       RING_$SWDIAG_DATA 0xE261C2  0x00E11278 (7 longs + 1 word)
       0x56     .rcvcnt    RING_$SWDIAG_RCVCNT 0xE261B4 0x00E1128C (patched over the copy)
       0x6C     .rcvhcsum  swdiag+0x18 (the uniform -0x1A mirror of stats+0x32)
       0x6E     .nodeid    RING_$SWDIAG_NODEID 0xE261AC 0x00E11294 (patched over the copy)
  0x72 word   xmit_biphase RING_$XMIT_BIPHASE 0xE261BC 0x00E1129C
  0x74 word   rcv_biphase  RING_$RCV_BIPHASE 0xE261B8  0x00E112A4
  0x76 word   xmit_esb     RING_$XMIT_ESB 0xE261BE     0x00E112AC
  0x78 word   rcv_esb      RING_$RCV_ESB 0xE261BA      0x00E112B4

The counter names are Apollo's own: /etc/netmain's 'Error counts for <node>' display formats this record and shows 25 counters where ring_$stats_t holds 22.  The extra three -- 'xmit bph', 'rcv bph', 'xmit esb' (and 'rcv esb' on the software-diagnostic line) -- are exactly the four tail words, printed in that order, and the two receive ones are already pinned to 0xE261B8 / 0xE261BA by ring_$validate_receive, which fixes the other two.

The stats half is spelled out field by field rather than embedded as ring_$stats_t because ring/ring.h #includes network/network.h for the status_$network_* codes, so network.h cannot include ring/ring.h back; ring/ring.h stays the authority for those names.  network_$failure_rec_t is in the same header and is embedded by type.

Tests: network/test/test_ring_info.c #includes the real network/ring_info.c (stubbing only network_$do_request) and checks the size, every offset above, the uniform 0x1A stats/swdiag displacement, the 0x0E command word, the copy from response+6 and that an error status leaves the caller's buffer untouched.  9 tests, 0 failed; make test 158 tests, 0 failed.

Ghidra: FUN_00e10628 renamed NETWORK_$PROCESS_PAGING_REQUEST (sr10.4-install/sau7/domain_os.map is the only NETWORK_ entry, 3C414E64 size 0xF32, between REPORT_FAILURE and PAGE_SERVER, and this routine is 0xF02 in exactly that gap); decompiler comments on 0x00E10628, 0x00E11246 and 0x00E1039A; disassembly comments on 0x00E11250/11266/11278/1128C/11294/112BC.

STILL OPEN: two fields.  +0x00 is always the literal 3, but the same slot carries an unrelated value in the dispatcher's other replies (8 at 0x00E10A3C / 0x00E11172 / 0x00E1148C / 0x00E1151E), so it is per-payload and its meaning is not recoverable from the image; netmain's 'v%wd' record-version prints are suggestive but not conclusive.  +0x03 is never written.  Spun off: source-twut (ring_$swdiag_t is 0x1E, not 0x18) and source-oowv (network_$failure_rec_t +0x04/+0x0C named backwards).

title: MSG_$WAIT signature has an extra status_ret parameter
description: msg/wait.c:MSG_$WAIT declares (socket, timeout, status_ret) but the binary at 0x00e59ba4 takes only two arguments: it does link.w A6,-0x8 / pea (-0x4,A6) to allocate the status locally, pushes only (0xc,A6) and (0x8,A6), and returns seq on the local status. It never writes a caller-supplied status. Fix the prototype in msg/msg.h, msg/wait.c and the svc/svc_tables.c entry (0x15). TODO(source-d8t1) marks the spot.
close_reason: MSG_$WAIT re-emitted with the two-argument signature the binary has (0x00E59BA4 'link.w A6,-0x8' / 'pea (-0x4,A6)', args at 0x8 and 0xc only, boolean via 'seq D0b').  msg/msg.h, msg/wait.c and the svc/svc_tables.c TRAP2 entry 0x15 updated; MSG_$WAITI de-magicked onto SOCK_$EVENT_COUNTERS[socket-1] and the new MSG_$SOCK_OWNERS extern.  Ghidra prototypes/comments updated.  New test msg/test/test_wait.c (8 tests) calls the real functions.

title: ast_$allocate_pages had its two word arguments inverted at every call site (fixed)
description: Recorded for the audit trail.  ast_$allocate_pages (0x00E00D46) takes THREE Pascal parameters: the requested count word at (0x8,A6) (read into D2 at 0x00E00D4E and decremented as pages are obtained), a minimum-count word at (0xa,A6) (compared against the running total at 0x00E00E56 to decide whether to wake the purifier and retry), and the array pointer at (0xc,A6) (0x00E00D52).  The C had modelled the two words as one 'count_flags' longword and then read the halves the wrong way round: ast/allocate_pages.c set num_pages = (uint16_t)count_flags, which for the universal caller encoding (count << 16) | 1 requested ONE page instead of count, and set min_count = count.  Fixed: the prototype in ast/ast.h and ast/ast_internal.h is now (int16_t count, int16_t min_count, uint32_t *ppn_array), and all eight call sites were converted -- ast/count_valid_pages.c, ast/copy_area.c, ast/fetch_pmap_page.c, ast/read_area_pages.c, ast/read_area_pages_network.c, ast/touch_area.c (three), wp/calloc.c and wp/calloc_list.c.  ast/test/test_touch_area.c's mock, wp/test/test_calloc.c and wp/test/test_calloc_list.c were updated; the two wp tests now #include the real .c instead of re-implementing it.
close_reason: Audit-trail entries; fixes verified by the wave-7 verification pass and committed (10f8346)

title: Audit: CAL_$WRITE_CALENDAR writes 11 of 13 RTC registers wrong; delay loops elided at -O2
description: cal/write_calendar.c: control byte must be threaded by reference and auto-decremented (*control -= 0x10 at end of cal_$write_calendar_digit; 0xE8173E); cal_$delay non-volatile (also time/read_cal.c:150); signed / and % where divu.w; leap bit +0x50 contradicts read_cal (bit 3 vs 2). See docs/audit-2026-09-06.md.
close_reason: Re-emitted cal/write_calendar.c from the 0xE8167C disassembly: control byte threaded by reference and decremented in cal_$write_calendar_digit (0xE8173E), so all 13 MSM5832 registers (0xC1..0x01, seconds-ones included) now get the right address; delays made non-elidable via the new ARCH_SPIN_TICK() arch macro (used here and in time/read_cal.c); unsigned divu.w semantics; leap bit reconciled against read_cal (write sets D10 bit 3 via +0x50, read uses bit 2 - original discrepancy documented + bead source-tcxm); OKI MSM5832 terminology and the register map moved into cal/cal.h behind CAL_$RTC_* accessors; Ghidra comments added at 0xE8167C/0xE816D6/0xE816EA/0xE8173E/0xE81752/0xE81756 (the delay entries were already named cal_$delay / cal_$delay_40). title: mac_os_$send_pkt_t is 0x40 bytes but the real MAC_OS send record is 0x4C
description: MAC_OS_$SEND's descriptor carries a payload page vector at +0x3C (four longwords) and the frame type at +0x30, so the record runs to 0x4C bytes.  Verified from ROUTE_$PROCESS (0x00E876A4-0x00E876DA) and XNS_IDP_$SEND (0x00E183FC-0x00E1842A), and from MAC_OS_$SEND itself (descriptor chain at +0x1C walked at 0x00E0B62C, 'prebuilt' byte at +0x28 tested at 0x00E0B616, accumulated length stored at +0x38 at 0x00E0B786).  route/route_internal.h currently carries the corrected layout as route_$mac_send_rec_t; fold it back into mac_os/mac_os.h (and reconcile mac/mac.h's mac_$send_pkt_t, whose 0x1C/0x20/0x24 field names describe a {length,address,next} descriptor).
close_reason: mac_os/mac_os.h now carries the real 0x4C-byte mac_os_$send_pkt_t (with mac_os_$link_addr_t and mac_os_$buf_desc_t) and _Static_asserts.  Size confirmed by RING_$SEND_OS's whole-record copy, 0x13 longwords at 0x00E77E76-0x00E77E80; the link address head by MAC_OS_$ARP's third argument (0x00E0C0DE) and RING_$SEND_OS's count check at 0x00E77D7E; the broadcast flag at +0x18 by ARP's fourth argument (0x00E0C112/0x00E0C12A) and 0x00E77DB6; the descriptor at +0x1C by MAC_OS_$SEND's chain walk (0x00E0B62C-0x00E0B660); hdr_prebuilt at +0x28 by 0x00E0B616; frame_type at +0x30 by 0x00E77DEA; data_length at +0x38 by 0x00E77D60; the four payload pages at +0x3C by ROUTE_$PROCESS (0x00E876CC-0x00E876DA) and XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND (0x00E1841C-0x00E18428).  route/route_internal.h's route_$mac_send_rec_t is gone and ROUTE_$PROCESS plus route/test/test_process.c use the shared record; mac/mac.h's mac_$send_pkt_t is now a typedef of it and mac/send.c was corrected against 0x00E0BB88-0x00E0BC18 (it passed NULL for MAC_OS_$ARP's broadcast-flag output, which the callee writes through, and did not clear +0x38/+0x3C).  xns/idp_send.c still builds an invented record - bead source-tvrs.

title: Emit acl_$find_acl_slot (0x00E45E8E), the ACL image cache lookup
description: 234 bytes.  Hashes the ACL UID with UID_$HASH (0x00E45EB0) and walks a chained directory in the ACL module's A5 data (A5+0x800 16-byte slots, A5+0xA70 next links, A5+0xAF0 hash buckets; A5 = 0xE7CF54) to a slot index into ACL_$ACL_CACHE (0xE88834, 31 slots of 0x400).  On a miss it calls FUN_00e45a60 to load the image; on a hit whose flag byte at slot+0x80A is negative it calls ACL_$DEF_ACLDATA and refreshes prot->world_rights / prot->subsys_rights from slot+0x80D / +0x80F.  Also needs FUN_00e44c92 and FUN_00e44c3c (LRU list maintenance).  Prototype and TODO are in acl/acl_internal.h.
close_reason: Emitted acl/find_acl_slot.c plus acl/cache_list.c (the two list primitives at 0x00E44C3C / 0x00E44C92, renamed acl_$cache_list_insert / acl_$cache_list_remove in Ghidra), every basic block of 0x00E45E8E-0x00E45F76 traced.  Recovered the whole A5-relative cache directory and fixed each array's element count from the fact that they are contiguous (A5 = 0xE7CF54): ACL_$CACHE_DIR[31] 16 bytes at A5+0x800 (0xE7D754, uid at +0, flag +0x0A, world_rights +0x0D, subsys_rights +0x0F), ACL_$CACHE_LRU_LINKS[32] {next,prev} at A5+0x9F0, ACL_$CACHE_HASH_LINKS[32] at A5+0xA70, ACL_$CACHE_HASH_BUCKETS[64] at A5+0xAF0, ACL_$CACHE_FREE_HEAD at A5+0xB74 and ACL_$CACHE_LRU_HEAD at A5+0xB76 - the last one shares its address with ACL_$SUPER_COUNT[0], which process numbering (1-based, ACL_$ENTER_SUPER 0x00E46FA8) never uses.  UID_$HASH's modulus is the word 0x003D (61) at 0x00E45E8C, reached by the pea (-0x20,PC) at 0x00E45EAA and now a named file static.  Also pinned: the miss-path status test is the LOW word (tst.w (0x2,A0) at 0x00E45EE2), a hit does remove-then-insert on the LRU while a miss only inserts (0x00E45EF0 skips 0x00E45F48), and the negative flag byte at dir+0x0A triggers ACL_$DEF_ACLDATA followed by restoring prot->world_rights / subsys_rights from dir+0x0D / +0x0F (0x00E45F24).  FUN_00e45a60 renamed acl_$load_acl_image; its body is bead source-3cq1.  15 unit tests in acl/test/test_find_acl_slot.c, all passing.

title: smd_disp_info_result_t: +0x06/+0x08 field names are swapped
description: SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO (0x00E7018A/0x00E70194) stores hw->max_x+1 at result+0x06 and hw->max_y+1 at result+0x08, but smd/smd.h names those fields 'height' and 'width' respectively.  smd/inq_disp_info.c now writes the correct bytes with a TODO comment explaining the mismatch.  Renaming the fields also means fixing tpad/init.c:52-53, which must be checked against TPAD_$INIT's assembly first (tpad is not owned by this pass).
close_reason: smd_disp_info_result_t's +0x06 is now 'width' and +0x08 'height', matching SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO 0x00E7018A (move.w (0x50,A1)=hw->max_x, addq #1, move.w D1w,(0x6,A2)) and 0x00E70194 (hw->max_y+1 -> (0x8,A2)).  smd/inq_disp_info.c writes the same bytes as before and its TODO is gone.  tpad/init.c:52-53 needed no text change - it was written to the semantics, so the rename makes it read the correct offsets: TPAD_$INIT 0x00E335C6 takes the result's +0x08 into config +0x18 (y_max_disp) and 0x00E335D0 the +0x06 into config +0x14 (x_max_disp).  Also renamed +0x02/+0x04 from bits_per_pixel/num_planes to mem_width/mem_height: the jump table at 0x00E701B2 writes 0x04000400 / 0x04000800 / 0x08000400 there, i.e. frame-buffer dimensions of 1024/2048, never the 4 and 8 the old C stored.  _Static_asserts added on all five offsets and on sizeof == 10.  Covered by the new smd/test/test_inq_disp_info.c (9 tests).  A separate finding in TPAD_$INIT (the x_range/x_scale copies) is filed as source-j999.

title: Fix Dir_$OpResponse struct: f18 should be 12 bytes, not 8
description: The Dir_$OpResponse struct in dir_internal.h has f18[8] (8-byte array at offset 8). Assembly analysis confirms it should be f18[12] (12 bytes). With f18[12], the field offsets match the assembly: _20_2_ at 0x14, _22_4_ at 0x16, f1a at 0x1A. Current layout only works on m68k where uint32_t has 2-byte alignment. On x86 hosts, alignment padding makes fields land at wrong offsets. The fix requires auditing all Dir_$OpResponse users (resolve.c, do_op.c, etc.) to verify they use correct byte offsets after the change. See also do_op.c case 0x46 TODO.

title: time_$clock_to_itimer callers pass source/destination in the wrong order
description:
0x00E58C02 (now named time_$clock_to_itimer in Ghidra) writes through the FIRST argument and reads the SECOND:

  00e58c02  link.w A6,-0xc
  00e58c06  movea.l (0xc,A6),A0      | A0 = arg2 = SOURCE
  ...
  00e58c28  movea.l (0x8,A6),A1      | A1 = arg1 = DESTINATION
  00e58c2c  move.l (-0xc,A6),(A1)
  00e58c30  move.w (-0x8,A6),(0x4,A1)

Argument order was confirmed against 0x00E58D14 (time_$set_itimer_internal), whose six parameters run 0x08 which(w), 0x0A value, 0x0E interval, 0x12 ovalue, 0x16 ointerval, 0x1A status - i.e. the first declared parameter sits at (0x8,A6).

time/time_internal.h declares 'void time_$clock_to_itimer(clock_t *clock, uint32_t *itimerval)' and time/get_itimer.c:29,33 calls it as time_$clock_to_itimer(&val_clock, value) - passing the clock_t SOURCE as the destination. The direction is inverted at every call site. The sibling time_$itimer_to_clock (0x00E58C3A) is declared correctly (arg1 = clock_t dest).

Note the two also do nothing but a 48-bit shift by one (left for clock->itimer, right for itimer->clock); get_itimer.c then re-copies value[0]/value[1] by hand, which duplicates what the callee already wrote.
close_reason: time_$clock_to_itimer's prototype now has the destination first (0x00E58C28 movea.l (0x8,A6),A1). Fixed time/time_internal.h, and re-emitted every caller: time/get_itimer.c and time/set_itimer.c now hand the caller's own buffers to the *_internal routines and convert in place through one temporary, as the asm does (0xE58F3C, 0xE58EDE); time/set_cpu_limit.c now converts its limit with time_$itimer_to_clock (0xE58FA0 - it did not before), tests the RAW limit for zero (0xE58FEE), runs SUB48 on a scratch copy of the raw limit (0xE59036) instead of the halved one, and reaches TIME_$VTQ (0xE2A4A0) instead of TIME_$CPU_LIMIT_DB. Added time/clock_to_itimer.c and time/itimer_to_clock.c (they were declared but never defined) and time/test/test_itimer.c, 14 tests.

title: ACL_$RIGHTS' second parameter is a boolean pointer, not an unused void*
description: acl/acl.h declares 'int16_t ACL_$RIGHTS(uid_t *uid, void *unused, uint32_t *required_mask, int16_t *option_flags, status_$t *status)' and every call site passes something arbitrary for the second argument (NULL in some, the address of the rights mask in others). title: PKT_$BLD_INTERNET_HDR is not emitted against pkt_$info_t
description: pkt/bld_internet_hdr.c models its pkt_info argument as 'uint8_t *pkt_info_bytes' plus 'uint32_t *pkt_info_words' and writes the header buffer through byte and word casts of a uint32_t* ('((uint8_t *)&hdr_buf[1])[0] = pkt_info_bytes[1];'). pkt.h now carries the recovered pkt_$info_t (0x20 bytes, +0x00 flags, +0x02 routing_type, +0x04 addr_type, +0x06 protocol, +0x08 retry_limit, +0x0C field_0c, +0x0E addr[16]) and the header record the routine fills in is 0x4C..0x5C bytes and still unnamed. close_reason: Re-emitted the whole 764-byte PKT_$BLD_INTERNET_HDR (0x00E1202C) against pkt_$info_t and a newly recovered pkt_$hdr_t/pkt_$inet_addr_t in pkt/pkt.h. Every basic block traced: the loopback flag (0x00E1204C), the common 0x1E-byte prologue (0x00E1206A-0x00E1208A), the RIP lookup on an uninitialised dest record (0x00E12098-0x00E120C6), all three size-check arms (this node 0x00E120E2, direct port 0x00E120F8, gateway 0x00E12156), the unconditional internet fill at 0x00E1217C, both header extensions (0x00E1221E, 0x00E12240), the type-1 body (0x00E12262), the common tail and both length caps (0x00E122BE, 0x00E122EA). Header record shared with PKT_$BRK_INTERNET_HDR (0x00E12328), which was re-emitted against it in the same pass. Fixed en route: hdr+0x24/0x1E take the LOW word of the destination (0x00E12196 reads (-0x2e,A6)), the template-offset cap is >= not > (0x00E122EA bcs), the error path uses the nexthop node not the destination (0x00E1217C), and ROUTE_$PORTP/ROUTE_$PORT_ARRAY are really indexed instead of the two old TODO stubs. rem_file_internal.h REM_FILE_OP_* opcode table disagrees with the image
description: The REM_FILE_OP_* macros in rem_file/rem_file_internal.h were guessed and at least four are wrong against the binary: REM_FILE_OP_UNLOCK is defined 0x05 but REM_FILE_$UNLOCK writes 0x0C (move.b #0xc,(-0x16d,A6) at 0x00E61D48, and REM_FILE_$SERVER dispatches SERVER_OP_UNLOCK == 0x0C); REM_FILE_OP_SET_DEF_ACL is defined 0x0C but REM_FILE_$SET_DEF_ACL writes 0x18 (0x00E62300); REM_FILE_OP_UNLOCK_ALL is defined 0x04 but rem_file/unlock_all.c uses 0x12; REM_FILE_OP_LOCAL_VERIFY is defined 0x11 but local_verify.c uses 0x1A. The table is inert today because every request builder writes its own literal, so nothing is mis-emitted, but it is a trap. Re-derive all ~28 opcodes from each REM_FILE_$* builder's 'move.b #op,(-0x16d,A6)' and from REM_FILE_$SERVER's dispatch table, then convert the builders to use the macros. Referenced by a TODO at the bottom of rem_file/unlock.c.
close_reason:
REM_FILE_OP_* rebuilt from the image.  Every builder writes 0x80 at request+0x02 and its opcode at request+0x03 (rec based at A6-0x170; CREATE_TYPE and NAME_GET_ENTRYU use A6-0x198, UNLOCK_ALL A6-0xD0, same two offsets into the record), and REM_FILE_$SERVER reads it back at request+0x03 - 'move.b (-0x435,A6),D0b' with the request at A6-0x438.

Derived opcodes, builder store address -> value: TEST clr.b 0x00E62386 = 0x00; SET_ATTRIBUTE 0x00E61A48 = 0x04; TRUNCATE 0x00E61996 = 0x08; LOCK 0x00E61B5E = 0x0A; UNLOCK 0x00E61D48 = 0x0C; NEIGHBORS 0x00E621D0 = 0x10; UNLOCK_ALL 0x00E61C84 = 0x12; PURIFY 0x00E62272 = 0x14; LOCAL_READ_LOCK 0x00E61EB6 = 0x16; SET_DEF_ACL 0x00E62300 = 0x18; LOCAL_VERIFY 0x00E61E38 = 0x1A; NAME_GET_ENTRYU 0x00E620C2 = 0x1C; GET_SEG_MAP 0x00E61F62 = 0x1E; INVALIDATE 0x00E623F8 = 0x20; NAME_ADD_HARD_LINKU 0x00E6250A = 0x22; GENERATE_UID 0x00E61742 / 0x00E6188C / 0x00E62858 = 0x24; CREATE_TYPE_PRESR10 0x00E618E4 = 0x26; DROP_HARD_LINKU 0x00E625AC = 0x28; ACL_IMAGE 0x00E627C0 = 0x64; SET_ACL 0x00E62AC4 = 0x66; ACL_CREATE 0x00E628A2 = 0x68; ACL_SETIDS 0x00E62950 = 0x6A; ACL_CHECK_RIGHTS 0x00E62A10 = 0x6C; RESERVE 0x00E62478 = 0x7C; CREATE_TYPE 0x00E61788 = 0x7E; FILE_SET_PROT 0x00E62B84 = 0x80; FILE_SET_ATTRIB 0x00E62C46 = 0x82; LOCK_EXT 0x00E61AEA = 0x84; CREATE_AREA 0x00E62646 = 0x86; DELETE_AREA 0x00E626E6 = 0x88; GROW_AREA 0x00E62754 = 0x8A.  Cross-checked against REM_FILE_$SERVER's compare chain at 0x00E63A02-0x00E63AD0 and its two forwarding ranges, 0x2A..0x5C -> DIR_$SERVER (0x00E63840) and 0x64..0x77 -> ACL_$SERVER (0x00E6395E).

The bead's four named errors are confirmed and fixed: UNLOCK was 0x05 (is 0x0C), SET_DEF_ACL was 0x0C (is 0x18), UNLOCK_ALL was 0x04 (is 0x12), LOCAL_VERIFY was 0x11 (is 0x1A).  The table was NOT entirely inert: rem_file/purify.c used REM_FILE_OP_PURIFY, which was defined 0x0B and is really 0x14 - a real mis-emission, now correct.  Three builders send two requests (CREATE_TYPE 0x24 then 0x7E, CREATE_TYPE_PRESR10 0x24 then 0x26, ACL_CREATE 0x24 then 0x68); 0x24 is the shared 'ask the remote node for a UID' step, handled by REM_FILE_$SERVER__generate_uid (0x00E632C2), so it is named GENERATE_UID rather than CREATE_TYPE_INIT.  REM_FILE_$LOCK's 0x84/0x0A pair is a real choice on its boolean at (0x14,A6), not a fallback, so both are defined.

All 25 builders now use the macros (24 that wrote literals plus rem_file/unlock.c, whose local REM_FILE_UNLOCK_MAGIC/OPCODE now alias REM_FILE_REQ_MAGIC/REM_FILE_OP_UNLOCK); its trailing TODO is removed.  rem_file/server.c's private SERVER_OP_* duplicate is deleted and its uses point at the shared macros - only the four DIR_$SERVER codes it special-cases for their netbuf (0x3C/0x3E/0x42/0x58) stay local, since no REM_FILE builder produces them.

rem_file builds clean; its three tests pass (19, 26 and 16 assertions, 0 failed).  Ghidra: decompiler comments with the full table on 0x00E63A02 and the record head on 0x00E60FD8; disassembly comments on 0x00E63840, 0x00E6395E and 0x00E637EA (the reply carries opcode+1).

title: win/disk: the per-volume record table at 0x00E7A560 (stride 0x1C) is not modelled
description:
DISK's A5 is 0x00E7A1E8, so its A5+0x378 is 0x00E7A560, and DISK_$WRITE_MULTI addresses a per-volume record there with 'lea (0x0,A5,D0w*0x1),A3' + '(0x378,A3)' / '(0x384,A3)' at 0x00E3CE3E / 0x00E3CE46, D0 = 0x1C * index - i.e. a 0x1C-byte record, entry n at 0x00E7A560 + 0x1C*n.  Other readers: 0x00E3D12E, 0x00E3D320, 0x00E3D43C, 0x00E3D6F4.

Four routines clear ONE byte of it with the same idiom, 'clr.b (-0x4,A1,D1w*0x1)' with A1 = 0x00E7A560 and D1 = 0x1C * (request byte at +0x1E): WIN_$FORMAT_TRACK 0x00E19764, WIN_$DO_IO 0x00E1994A, FLP_FORMAT_TRACK 0x00E3DDB0 and 0x00E3DFBC.  That address is 0x00E7A560 + 0x1C*n - 4, i.e. entry (n-1) + 0x18 - so a request's volume number is 1-BASED against the table while DISK's own index is 0-based.

Nothing in the tree declares the table; win/win_internal.h currently names only the one byte (WIN_VOLUME_MOUNTED).  Recover the 0x1C-byte record from the DISK_$ readers and give it a home in disk/disk.h, then have win/format_track.c and win/do_io.c use it.
close_reason: Recovered the record - and it is not per-volume. DISK_$WRITE_MULTI's A5 is 0xE7A1CC (0xE3CCF6 'lea (0xe7a1cc).l,A5'), not 0xE7A1E8, and its index is PROC1_$CURRENT (0xE3CE2A reads 0xE20608, then id*32-id*4 = id*0x1C), so A5+0x378 is 0x00E7A544 and the 0x1C-byte slot is PER PROCESS. Fields: +0x00 an I/O-completion ec_$eventcount_t whose value 0xE3CE3E reads, +0x0C an error eventcount whose value+1 0xE3CE46/0xE3CE4A forms, +0x18 a pending-I/O boolean 'st' at 0xE3CD3A and 'tst.b (0x390,A0)/bmi' at 0xE3CED2. That agrees with disk/disk_internal.h, which already had DMOD_PER_PROC_IO_EC 0x378 and DMOD_PER_PROC_ERR_EC 0x384 at a 0x1C stride indexed by PROC1_$CURRENT. Same pattern at 0xE3D12E/0xE3D136 in DISK_$READ_MULTI. The array ends at the disk_$error_info_t at A5+0xA94, so it holds 0x41 slots (id 0 plus 64 processes). The bead's '1-based volume table' reading came from taking 0xE7A560 for the base: 0xE7A560-4 is DISK_$PER_PROC + 0x18, so 'clr.b (-0x4,A1,D1w)' with D1 = 0x1C*n is slot n's byte with n 0-BASED, and n is the process id the request carries at +0x1E - which is why win_$request_t's +0x1E is now proc_id, not volume. Added disk_$per_proc_t + DISK_$PER_PROC to disk/disk.h (a type in another agent's public header - reported), replaced win_internal.h's fabricated WIN_VOLUME_TABLE/WIN_VOLUME_MOUNTED with WIN_IO_PENDING(proc_id), and updated win/format_track.c, win/do_io.c and win/test/test_format_track.c (8 tests, 0 failed). Ghidra: DISK_$PER_PROC labelled at 0xE7A544, comments on 0xE3CCEE, 0xE19764 and 0xE1994A.

title: netlog: page_counts[] is Pascal 1-based (elements at 0x70/0x72 only)
description:
NETLOG_$LOG_IT (00e71b9c) reads/writes the page counter at (0x6e,A0) with A0 = A5 + 2*current_buf_index, and NETLOG_$CNTL clears exactly two words at 0x70 and 0x72 (00e719a4/00e719a8).  The array holds two entries at 0x70 and 0x72, addressed 1-based.

netlog/netlog_internal.h now declares uint16_t page_counts[NETLOG_NUM_BUFFERS] at 0x70 (the old [NETLOG_NUM_BUFFERS+1] overlapped current_buf_ptr at 0x74).  The .c bodies still index it 1-based and must be changed to [i - 1]:
  netlog/cntl.c:46,72,73
  netlog/send_page.c:52
close_reason: netlog/cntl.c:54, netlog/log_it.c and netlog/send_page.c:53 now index page_counts with [index - 1], matching (0x6e,A0) with A0 = A5 + index*2 at 0x00E7195C / 0x00E71B9C / 0x00E71C14 / 0x00E71C38 / 0x00E71C98, and the two clear sites use [0]/[1] for 0x70/0x72 (0x00E719A4, 0x00E71AB2). Three further defects found while tracing: NETLOG_ENTRY_ADDR was one record too high (0x00E71BCE..0x00E71C02 write at -0x1A..-0x02 from base + count*26), entry.timestamp is the middle 32 bits of the clock not clock.high (0x00E71BDA reads (-0xe,A6)), and NETLOG_$CNTL's two MST_$WIRE_AREA calls passed VAs and a count by value where all five arguments are by reference - the four range cells and the page limit are now named file-statics matching 0x00E71B24..0x00E71B34, the ranges are NETLOG code 0xE71914..0xE71D7A and NETLOG data 0xE85684..0xE85708 (nothing AUDIT), and the unwire loop now runs forward (0x00E719BC). New test netlog/test/test_log_it.c (6 tests); netlog/test/test_netlog.c rewritten to use the real headers instead of a private struct copy and no longer asserts the wrong entry offset.

description: Six 'TODO: verify' field comments in disk/disk_internal.h disk_$volume_t have no owner; find their uses (gsk xrefs on 0xE7A1CC+N*0x48 accesses) and name them.

title: smd: SMD_$START_SCROLL / SMD_$CONTINUE_SCROLL / SMD_$START_BLT are hand-written asm with register arguments
description:
0x00E272A8 SMD_$START_SCROLL is a two-instruction trampoline ('lea (-0x38a,PC),A0' -> A0 = 0x00E26F20, then 'jmp 0x00E15C68'), and the body at 0x00E15C68 takes its arguments in REGISTERS: 'movea.l A0,A5' then 'movea.l (0x8,SP),A1' / 'movea.l (0xc,SP),A0', and calls the scroll-BLT setup routine through the SAU dispatch table with 'jsr (0x150,A5)' at 0x00E15C8A (A5 + 0x150 = 0x00E27070).  It ends in 'rts' with the BLT control word already written to (A0).

smd/start_scroll.c and smd/continue_scroll.c model this as ordinary C, and smd/smd_internal.h declares smd_$setup_scroll_blt(SMD_HW_REG_PTR, smd_display_hw_t *) as if it were C-callable - it is not; A0/A1 are the arguments.  Per CLAUDE.md these bodies belong in smd/sau2/*.s with the C kept behind '#if !defined(ARCH_M68K)' as a portable model, the way smd/sau2/start_blt.s and lock_display.s already are.

Same treatment is still owed to SMD_$START_BLT's body at 0x00E15D1E (bead source-x81r) and to whatever else the 0x00E15Cxx block holds.  The scroll-BLT setup routine itself is now byte-for-byte in smd/sau2/disp1_int.s (bead source-k6h0).
close_reason: Transcribed both bodies to smd/sau2/scroll.s: SMD_$START_SCROLL (trampoline 0xE272A8, body 0xE15C68..0xE15C9B) and SMD_$CONTINUE_SCROLL (trampoline 0xE272B2, body 0xE15C9C..0xE15CCD). objdump-compared against the image bytes (gsk read 0x00E15C68 104): every instruction matches, including the two 'or.w #-0x7ff0,D0' that had to be emitted as .short 0x807c,0x8010 because gas normalises or.w #imm,%d0 to ORI.W. The only bytes that differ are the ones carrying relocations in the two trampolines. Both trampolines' lea reach the SAME address - 0xE272AA-0x38A and 0xE272B4-0x394 are both 0xE26F20, SMD_$DISP1_INT - which is why A0 is a genuine register argument: the body moves it to A5 and calls smd_$setup_scroll_blt with 'jsr (0x150,A5)', i.e. by jumping to 0xE27070, not through a function pointer. smd/start_scroll.c and smd/continue_scroll.c keep the portable model behind '#if !defined(ARCH_M68K)', the convention smd/start_blt.c already uses, so the two never collide at link time. New smd/test/test_scroll.c #includes both .c files and calls the real entry points: 5 tests, 0 failed. smd_internal.h's note that smd_$setup_scroll_blt is not C-callable already said this and is unchanged. Ghidra: decompiler comments on 0xE272A8 and 0xE272B2. SMD_$START_BLT was already done under source-x81r.

title: svc/sau2: PC16 lea to SVC_$TRAPn_TABLE overflows at link (11 sites)
description: The image reaches every dispatch table with lea (d16,PC): 0xE7B04C -> SVC_$TRAP0_TABLE 0xE7B2DE, and the same at 0xE7B064/0xE7B09C/0xE7B0E0/0xE7B128/0xE7B184/0xE7B1E0, plus 0xE7B240/0xE7B27C/0xE7B28E/0xE7B2CC in trap8.  trap0..trap7 now emit that form (bead source-avfg, byte fidelity), so 11 R_68K_PC16 relocations against the tables exist.  In the image the tables sit 0x290..0xC08 bytes past the code; in our sau2.ld layout .data lands ~0x11000 past .text, so all 11 overflow at link time.  GNU ld prints only the first 10 relocation overflows tree-wide and then says 'additional relocation overflows omitted', so most are invisible.  Three of these (trap8's) predate source-avfg.  Same root cause as the PROC1_$DISPATCH_INT / ADVANCE_INT / SIO2681_$PTRS / SMD_DISPLAY_INFO overflows: the link script does not reproduce the image's code/data adjacency.  Fix belongs in sau2.ld (place the SVC tables, or all of .data, next to .text), not in the .s files.

title: svc/sau2/trap0-7.s: cmp.w #imm,%dn assembles as CMPI, image uses CMP

- 0x08-0x34: saved D2-D7, A2-A6, A7 registers

title: sock.h: SOCK_$PUT's pkt_ptr is a sock_$pkt_info_t*, not a void**
description: sock/sock.h declares 'int8_t SOCK_$PUT(uint16_t, void **pkt_ptr, ...)' and sock/put.c's SOCK_$PUT_INT_INT does 'sock_$pkt_info_t *pkt_info = (sock_$pkt_info_t *)*pkt_ptr;', i.e. one dereference too many. The assembly passes the pointer straight through by value (SOCK_$PUT 0x00E16164 'move.l (0xa,A6),-(SP)') and SOCK_$PUT_INT_INT uses it AS the record: 0x00E16206 'movea.l (0xc,A6),A2' then 0x00E1623C 'move.w (0x2a,A2),D1w' reads sock_$pkt_info_t.data_len at +0x2A and 0x00E16266 'move.l (A2),D6' reads .hdr at +0x00. Retype the parameter to sock_$pkt_info_t* in sock.h, drop the extra deref in put.c, and remove the '(void **)&local_pkt' cast msg/send.c currently needs at its SOCK_$PUT call. Found while closing source-o80r.

title: ring: RING_$SENDP's poll loop and force-start arm are still a sketch
description:
While closing source-11rf the transmit-statistics half of RING_$SENDP (0x00E75916) was traced instruction by instruction and the counter/flag stores were corrected.  The rest of the 1226-byte function was NOT re-emitted and still diverges:

1. The normal-mode polling loop (ring/sendp.c, 'do { ... TIME_$ABS_CLOCK(&timeout); /* Check if deadline passed - simplified */ break; } while (1);') has no deadline comparison at all.  The image spins at 0x00E75A78-0x00E75AA2: 'movea.l A0,A0' / 'cmp.l (0x10,A1),D7' / 'ble 0x00E75C18', then TIME_$ABS_CLOCK into A6-0x18, SUB48(A6-0x20, A6-0x18) at 0x00E75A98 and 'tst.b D0b / bpl 0x00E75A78' - i.e. it loops until the 48-bit deadline in A6-0x20 (seeded from A6-0x28 plus RING_$DATA+0x590 at 0x00E75A66) goes negative.
2. The three TIME_$WAIT2 calls at 0x00E75AE0, 0x00E75B62 and 0x00E75B9A each take a 'pea (d16,PC)' constant cell as their first argument (0x00E75ADC 'pea (0x302,PC)' -> 0x00E75DE0, 0x00E75B5E 'pea (0x282,PC)' -> 0x00E75DE2, 0x00E75B96 'pea (0x24a,PC)' -> 0x00E75DE2) and the timeouts come from A5-relative cells at +0x578, +0x580, +0x590 and +0x598.  The C passes a shared 'delay_type' local and names the timeouts loosely.
3. The 0x00E75AF0-0x00E75B22 arm (deadline plus '(A6-0x26) & 7') has no C counterpart; the C falls straight through to the second TIME_$WAIT2.
4. hw_regs is 'int16_t *' indexed 0 and 3; the image uses (A4) and (0x6,A4) so those two happen to agree, but a byte-offset volatile view would be safer and would match ring/rcv.c.

Retrace 0x00E75916-0x00E75DDE block by block.  TODO marker is in ring/sendp.c at the poll loop.
close_reason: Re-emitted RING_$SENDP (0xE75916) block by block, 0xE75916-0xE75DDE. (1) The poll loop is now the real one: deadline = attempt_start + RING_$DATA.poll_timeout (ADD48 at 0xE75A6E), then spin at 0xE75A78 testing the eventcount and SUB48(&now, &deadline) at 0xE75A98 with 'bpl' looping while the deadline is ahead. (2) The three TIME_$WAIT2 setups that share the jsr at 0xE75B62 are all present with their own delay and delay-type: 0xE75ADC and 0xE75B1E take the ABSOLUTE cell 0xE75DE0 (=1) with the deadline, 0xE75B5E takes the RELATIVE cell 0xE75DE2 (=0) with RING_$DATA.xmit_timeout1, 0xE75B96 the same cell with xmit_timeout2 and 0xE75DB0 with the local retry delay; both cells are named file-static constants (gsk read 0x00E75DDE: 4e 75 00 01 00 00). (3) The 0xE75AF0 arm is emitted - deadline reseeded from attempt_start plus (attempt_start_low32 & 7) added to its HIGH longword. (4) hw_regs is the typed volatile ring_hw_regs_t*, so the 0x00 CSR and the 0x06 mode register are distinct fields. Also corrected from the listing: the argument list is TEN, not eight (0x14 hdr_len whose ADDRESS goes to HDR_CHKSUM, 0x16 a 16-byte descriptor, 0x1A never read, 0x20 an option word); 0xE75D5A reads the HEADER's msg_type, not send_flags; 0xE75D9C tests the header flags bit 1, not a byte of send_flags; SIO-style straddling longword writes at 0xE75D42/0xE75D76 go through the clock fields. New ring/test/test_sendp.c #includes the real .c: 28 tests, 0 failed. Ghidra: prototype, decompiler comment, five disassembly comments, two constant labels.

title: SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY and SMD_$BIT_SET are hand-written asm; move to smd/sau2/
description: SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY (0x00E15CCE, 68 bytes) has no link/unlk, takes its arguments straight off the stack via (0x4,SP)/(0x8,SP), and brackets its body with ori #0x700,SR / andi #0xf8ff,SR (a forced IPL 0, not an SR restore).  SMD_$BIT_SET (0x00E15D12, 12 bytes) is a three-instruction bset+seq thunk.  Per CLAUDE.md both belong in smd/sau2/*.s rather than C.  smd/lock_display.c currently models the forced-IPL-0 exits with ENABLE_INTERRUPTS(sr); the missing restore on the state-0 path was added during the 2026-09-06 fidelity pass.
close_reason: Both routines moved to smd/sau2/.  smd/sau2/lock_display.s is an instruction-for-instruction transcription of 0x00E15CCE-0x00E15D10; m68k-elf-gcc -c + m68k-elf-objdump -d gives 0x44 = 68 bytes, the original's size, and every byte matches the image read with gsk except the two compares, where the original uses CMP.W #imm,D0 (0xB07C) and GNU as normalises 'cmp.w #imm,%d0' to CMPI.W (0x0C40) - same length, same flags.  smd/sau2/bit_set.s transcribes 0x00E15D12-0x00E15D1C and assembles to 20 6f 00 04 08 d0 00 07 57 c0 4e 75, byte-identical to the image.  The forced IPL 0 (ori #0x700,SR / andi #0xf8ff,SR) is now real rather than modelled as an SR restore.  smd/lock_display.c and smd/bit_set.c keep portable models behind '#if !defined(ARCH_M68K)' so the m68k build links the assembly and the host test build keeps working; both files document where the model diverges (ENABLE_INTERRUPTS restores instead of forcing IPL 0; the C bit_set is not atomic - source-ssma).  Both prototypes changed from int16_t to int8_t: the originals only ever write the low byte of D0 (clr.b/st, seq).  smd/test/test_show_cursor.c's stub was updated to match and still passes.  Follow-up source-x81r covers SMD_$START_BLT (0x00E15D1E), which has the same hand-written shape.

title: app_$receive_rec_t.reply/.data are void* but hold target VAs, so the record is 8 bytes too long on a 64-bit host
description:
app/app.h declares 'void *reply' at 0x00 and 'void *data' at 0x04.  APP_$RECEIVE (0x00E00800) stores target virtual addresses there (0x00E008A8 'moveq #0x1e,D0 / add.l (-0x40,A6),D0 / move.l D0,(A2)'), and every consumer converts back with ARCH_PTR_TO_VA before masking to the 1KB netbuf page (pkt/likely_to_answer.c:207, pkt/ping_server.c:148, msg/rcv_internal.c, msg/rcv_contig.c).

On a 64-bit host the two pointers make sizeof(app_$receive_rec_t) 0x34 instead of 0x2C and shift data_pages/hdr_f06/hdr_f12/src_addr/src_port/flags_hi/flags_lo by 8, which is why app.h's _Static_asserts are wrapped in '#if defined(ARCH_M68K)'.  Retyping both to uint32_t (as sock_$pkt_info_t.hdr now is, bead source-bpz8) would let the asserts run unguarded; it touches pkt/likely_to_answer.c, pkt/ping_server.c, msg/rcv_internal.c, msg/rcv_contig.c and the pkt tests.
close_reason: app_$receive_rec_t.reply and .data are now uint32_t target VAs. APP_$RECEIVE stores an address it computes from sock_$pkt_info_t.hdr, itself a VA (0xE008A8 'moveq #0x1e,D0 / add.l (-0x40,A6),D0 / move.l D0,(A2)'; 0xE008B0 and 0xE0093C for .data), so nothing was ever a C pointer. sizeof is 0x2C on the host too, and all nine of app/app.h's _Static_asserts moved out of the '#if defined(ARCH_M68K)' guard. Use sites converted with ARCH_VA_TO_PTR / ARCH_PTR_TO_VA, and the ARCH_PTR_TO_VA(rec.data) calls before the 1KB netbuf-page mask are now plain reads: msg/rcv_internal.c (0xE59584/0xE59588/0xE59618/0xE59642), msg/rcv_contig.c (0xE5981C/0xE59820/0xE59930), pkt/likely_to_answer.c (0xE12B08), pkt/ping_server.c, asknode/who_remote.c, asknode/who_notopo.c and asknode/server.c - the last three also stop casting &rcv.data to uint32_t* for NETBUF_$RTN_HDR, since the field is now exactly that. Tests updated to round-trip through ARCH_HOST_VA_BASE (msg/test/test_rcv 10/0, pkt/test/test_likely_to_answer 13/0, asknode/test/test_server 17/0), and test_server's note that the record 'carries two real pointers' is replaced by the layout it now really has. This bead is inherently cross-subsystem: msg/, pkt/ and asknode/ belong to other agents in the 2026-09-07 split and are edited here only at the sites the retype forces.

title: ASKNODE_$WHO_NOTOPO reads the responding node id after returning the header buffer
description: asknode/who_notopo.c takes node_list[*count] from pkt_data+0x0E after NETBUF_$RTN_HDR has already returned the buffer, and then passes pkt_data+0x1C to PKT_$DUMP_DATA.  The original reads the node id from the packet BEFORE returning it ('move.l (0xe,A0),(0x0,A1,D7w)' at 0x00E6626A, with the RTN_HDR at 0x00E6629E) and hands PKT_$DUMP_DATA the APP_$RECEIVE record's own page vector at A6-0x28, not an offset into the freed buffer.

It reads the payload byte count, the responding node id, the reply length and the reply id from the reply record BEFORE NETBUF_$RTN_HDR, in the original's order (0x00E66258-0x00E66284 then 0x00E6629A), copies from the record's DATA pointer at +0x04 rather than reply+0x10 (0x00E6628C), and passes PKT_$DUMP_DATA the record's own page vector at +0x08 (0x00E662AC).
