title: ring: move ring_mac_pkt_info_t to mac_os/mac_os.h
description: ring/receive_packet.c defines the 0x40-byte record it builds for MAC_OS_$DEMUX (0x00E0B816) locally. Once MAC_OS_$DEMUX is decompiled the record belongs in mac_os/mac_os.h with the remaining fields named.
close_reason: The 0x40-byte record is now mac_os_$rcv_pkt_t in mac_os/mac_os.h with _Static_asserts, and ring/receive_packet.c uses it.  MAC_OS_$DEMUX (0x00E0B816) was decompiled to confirm the layout and mac_os/demux.c corrected against it: the port table stride is 0xF4 and the port index is a word read through the second argument (0x00E0B83E); MAC_OS_$FIND_PACKET_TYPE takes the frame type from record +0x30 (0x00E0B852); the channel entry is at MAC_OS_$CHANNEL_TABLE + index*0x14 and its callback is the field the tst.l at 0x00E0B882 checks; the arrival time from TIME_$ABS_CLOCK is stored as a longword at +0x2A and a word at +0x2E (0x00E0B890/0x00E0B896); and +0x34 gets the ADDRESS of the channel entry (0x00E0B89C).  The names now used for the fields the ring driver fills come from ring_$receive_packet 0x00E76528-0x00E7656A; route_info at +0x30 is renamed frame_type to match what MAC_OS_$DEMUX does with it.

title: fp/fp_internal.h FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE 0x00E21928 points into FIM_$BUS_ERR code
description: FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE is defined as 0x00E21928, but that address is inside FIM_$BUS_ERR: it is the extension words of the 'cmpi.b #0xA0,(0x22,%sp)' at 0x00E21926 that distinguishes a 68020 format A frame from a format B one.  It cannot be an FP save area.  The macro is currently unreferenced, so nothing is broken today, but it should be corrected or removed - FIM_$FSAVE (0x00E21C34) and FIM_$FRESTORE (0x00E21CD4) are where the real base can be recovered.
close_reason: FP_SAVE_AREA_BASE removed; the real base recovered. FP_$SAVEP (0x00E218D0) is not a save-pending flag but a LONGWORD POINTER to the per-address-space save-area table: fp_$switch_owner_d2 loads it with movea.l (-0x24c,PC),A1 at 0x00E21B1A (0x00E21B1C-0x24C = 0xE218D0) and fp_$check_owner with movea.l (-0x4ac,PC),A1 at 0x00E21D7A; fp_$save_state (0x00E21B5C) and fp_$restore_state (0x00E21B30) then address a slot as (-0x4,A1,asid*0x14A). The table is allocated at boot by PEB_$LOAD_WCS (move.l A0,(0x00e218d0).l at 0x00E3207C, A0 from the allocator at 0x00E43982) and cleared by OS_$SHUTDOWN (0x00E6D52E); it is 0 in the image, which is what the tst.l in FIM_$FP_ABORT (0x00E21B80) and FIM_$FP_INIT (0x00E21BB0) tests. Confirmed 0x00E21928 is inside FIM_$BUS_ERR. fp_save_area_t re-laid out from the assembly as a packed 0x14A-byte slot whose LAST longword is the frame pointer, with the frame written DOWNWARD (fsave -(A0), then FP0-7 / FPCR-FPSR-FPIAR / the 0xFFFF marker), and given unconditional _Static_asserts; the 326 available bytes are exactly 2+12+96 plus the 216-byte maximum 68882 FSAVE frame. Also re-emitted the whole FP cluster: fp/sau2/fp_context.s replaced the fabricated '68010 has no FPU' stubs with the real code for fp_$switch_owner (0x00E21B10), fp_$switch_owner_d2 (0x00E21B16), fp_$restore_state, fp_$save_state, FP_$GET_FP (0x00E21D48), fp_$check_owner (0x00E21D70) and FP_$PUT_FP (0x00E21D94) - every instruction encoding matches the image bytes read with gsk read (206f/7000/323c, f320/f218 9c00/f218 d0ff/f358/f220 e0ff/f220 bc00/f23c 9000 0000 f400, 2031 28fc, 41f1 08fc, 2388 08fc, 48e7 3000, 4cdf 000c), using the gas (sym:w,%pc) form to reproduce the 4-byte 303a/227a/487a PC-relative operands. fp/get_fp.c and fp/put_fp.c deleted: both omitted the fp_$restore_state / fp_$save_state calls entirely, and neither could express the A1-survives-between-calls contract that makes FP_$GET_FP / FP_$PUT_FP assembly. fp.h and fp_data.c retyped FP_$SAVEP as m68k_ptr_t with the correct description; fim/sau2/fim.s's 'non-zero if FPU hardware is present' comment corrected in place. New fp/test/test_save_area.c (5 tests) checks the 0x14A slot, the state cell at 0x146, the frame budget, the slot arithmetic against the record, the asid-0 skip, and the exact save/restore frame shape. Ghidra: disassembly comments at 0x00E218D0 and 0x00E21928, decompiler comments at 0x00E21B30 and 0x00E21B5C.

PROC2_$SET_PGROUP compares two entries' copies as a session test (0x00E4xxx), which is what the current name came from and which the self-index reading contradicts. title: TODO: OS_$INIT - vtoce_$result_t size vs the buffer OS_$INIT provides
description: os/init.c declares os_$init_vtoce_t (0x90 bytes) for the VTOCE_$READ result buffer at A6-0x128, because OS_$INIT clears exactly 36 longwords there (0x00E34018) and its frame (link.w A6,-0x1fc) has no room for the 0x150 bytes vtoc/vtoc.h gives vtoce_$result_t. Either vtoce_$result_t's size is wrong or OS_$INIT under-provides. Marked TODO(source-6y3f) in os/init.c.
close_reason: vtoce_$result_t is 0x90 bytes, not 0x150; OS_$INIT was right.  Every routine that moves a VTOCE across the caller boundary moves exactly 36 longwords: VTOCE_$READ 0x00E395B0, VTOCE_$WRITE 0x00E3977A, VTOC_$ALLOCATE 0x00E38C26.  The two converters agree: VTOCE_$OLD_TO_NEW's highest destination store is the longword at +0x8C (0x00E19F32) after clearing 31 longwords from +0x14 (0x00E19E72), and VTOCE_$NEW_TO_OLD's highest source load is +0x88 (0x00E38556).  0x150 is the on-disk entry stride inside a VTOCE block, not the record size.  vtoc/vtoc.h now declares 0x90 with a _Static_assert and documents the known field offsets; os/init.c's local os_$init_vtoce_t asserts it equals sizeof(vtoce_$result_t) and os/test/test_init.c checks it at runtime.

title: msg_$data_t layout and its dead inline accessors
description: msg/msg_internal.h's msg_$data_t puts depth[224] at 0x1E, which ends at 0x1DE, yet the ownership bitmaps start at 0x1D8 (0x00E59BFC 'lea (0x1D8,A1),A1') - the depth table cannot be 224 entries at that offset.  Recover the real layout from MSG_$OPENI/MSG_$ALLOCATEI.  Also msg_$check_ownership / msg_$set_ownership / msg_$clear_ownership / msg_$get_depth / msg_$set_depth are unused, ARCH_M68K-only and now duplicate the MSG_$SOCK_OWNERS extern added for MSG_$WAITI; fold or delete them.
close_reason: msg_$data_t recovered from MSG_$OPENI (0x00E591B4), MSG_$ALLOCATEI (0x00E592E6), MSG_$CLOSEI (0x00E593E4) and MSG_$WAITI (0x00E59BC0). The apparent overlap was a one-based array: the ownership base 0x1D8 is the address of slot ZERO of an array indexed by the socket number ('lsl.w #0x3,D2w / lea (0x0,A5,D2w),A0 / lea (0x1d8,A0),A1' at 0x00E59202-0x00E5920A), and socket 0 is impossible - MSG_$OPENI rejects <= 0 at 0x00E591CE and MSG_$CLOSEI at 0x00E593FA - so the lowest bitmap any caller can reach is socket 1 at +0x1E0. The depth table at 0x1E+socket*2 (0x00E59276, 0x00E5936C) therefore ends exactly at 0x1E0. Layout is now reserved_00[0x1E] / depth[0xE1] at 0x1E / ownership[0xE0][8] at 0x1E0 (indexed socket-1) / open_count at 0x8E0 (0x00E5927A, 0x00E5949E), sizeof 0x8E2, with _Static_asserts. depth is sized for 0xE1 entries because MSG_$CLOSEI and MSG_$WAITI accept socket 0xE0 ('cmpi.w #0xe0,D0w / ble' at 0x00E593FE and 0x00E59BDA) while MSG_$OPENI stops at 0xDF ('blt' at 0x00E591D6). The five dead inline accessors (msg_$check_ownership / set_ownership / clear_ownership / get_depth / set_depth) are deleted; MSG_$SOCK_OWNERS is now a macro over the record, so it and MSG_$DATA->ownership[n-1] are provably the same storage, and msg/open.c, allocate.c and close.c reach depth/open_count/NETWORK_$USER_SOCK_OPEN through it instead of raw address arithmetic. Host storage added in msg/msg_data.c. Tests: msg/test/test_data_layout.c (5 tests) and the existing msg/test/test_wait.c (8 tests), 0 failed.

description: ml/lock.c models the helper at 0x00E20AE8 as a file-static ml_$prepare_lock, described as a nested Pascal procedure. title: SMD: display info table indexing is 1-based; several files use [unit]
description: The 0x00E27376 table is addressed as base + unit*0x60 - 0x60 (smd_$validate_unit 0x00E6D722 'tst.w (-0x60,A0,D1*0x1)', SMD_$INQ_DISP_TYPE 0x00E6DE4C, SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO 0x00E70172, SMD_$INQ_KBD_CURSOR 0x00E6E112/0x00E6E116).  smd_internal.h now exports smd_$unit_info(unit) = &SMD_DISPLAY_INFO[unit-1] and inq_disp_info.c / invert_s.c / reset_display_globals.c use it, but inq_disp_type.c:55,86, write_string.c:70, set_clip_window.c:58-59, send_response.c:75-81 and inq_kbd_cursor.c:66-75 still index with the raw unit number or with hand-rolled byte arithmetic.  Convert each after checking its own assembly.
close_reason: All six files converted, and the underlying struct was wrong too.  Every accessor computes base + unit*0x60 and then reaches back by a negative displacement, so the table is 1-based: smd_$validate_unit 0x00E6D722 'tst.w (-0x60,A0,D1*0x1)', SMD_$INQ_DISP_TYPE 0x00E6DE4C 'move.w (-0x60,A0,D0*0x1),D0w', SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO 0x00E70172, SMD_$INQ_KBD_CURSOR 0x00E6E10A/-0x2E/-0x28, smd_$reset_display_globals 0x00E6D80E/0x00E6D812/0x00E6D816, SMD_$SET_CLIP_WINDOW 0x00E6FE70 (-0x12..-0x04), SMD_$WRITE_STRING 0x00E6FF08 (-0x12/-0x0A), SMD_$SEND_RESPONSE 0x00E6F4EC (-0x20).  Converting them exposed that the old smd_display_info_t put the clip window at +0x0C..+0x1B, which no instruction agrees with: SMD_$SET_CLIP_WINDOW clamps +0x56/+0x58 against +0x4E/+0x50 and +0x5A/+0x5C against +0x52/+0x54, and smd_$write_str_clip_impl tests the X coordinate against +0x56/+0x58 (0x00E70402, 0x00E7045E, 0x00E70466) and the Y coordinate against +0x5A/+0x5C (0x00E7040E, 0x00E704E6, 0x00E704EE).  Those are exactly smd_display_hw_t's min_x/max_x/min_y/max_y and clip_x1/clip_x2/clip_y1/clip_y2, because the 'display info entry' and the per-display hardware record are ONE object: SMD_$INIT stores the literal 0x00E27376 into unit 1's hw pointer (0x00E34D92 'move.l #0xe27376,(0x18,A0)') and then writes +0x50/+0x54 through A4 = rec->hw (0x00E34E00-0x00E34E18); Ghidra even labels 0x00E27376 SMD_$DISPLAY_COM.  smd_display_info_t is now a typedef alias of smd_display_hw_t and the old struct is gone.  Consequences: SMD_$SET_CLIP_WINDOW's argument is {x1,x2,y1,y2} (two move.l stores at 0x00E6FE76/0x00E6FE7A), not {x1,y1,x2,y2}; SMD_$SEND_RESPONSE advances hw->cursor_ec at +0x40 (the same eventcount SMD_$BORROW_DISPLAY waits on, 0x00E6F60E/0x00E6F63A); SMD_$INQ_KBD_CURSOR returns hw->cursor_visible (+0x38) and hw->cursor_pos (+0x32); inq_disp_type.c's private smd_validate_unit stub (which guessed units 0..3) is deleted in favour of the real 0x00E6D700 routine, which accepts only unit 1.  New _Static_asserts pin +0x02, +0x04, +0x10, +0x1C, +0x22 and +0x40.  Ghidra: decompiler comment on 0x00E27376 with the full field list, EOL comments at 0x00E6FE70, 0x00E6FF08, 0x00E6F500, 0x00E6F4FC, 0x00E6E10A and 0x00E6DE4C.

title: Complete network_$set_service (route port structure, service notification)
close_reason: NETWORK_$SET_SERVICE (0x00E0F45E) re-emitted against the disassembly.  The service flags are the HIGH word of the NETWORK_$ALLOWED_SERVICE longword at 0xE24C3E -- every access is move.w (0x342,A5) or btst.b #n,(0x343,A5) with A5 = 0xE248FC -- so the old '(x & 0xFFFF0000) | new' store was inverted, and so was the operand half: ops 0..2 read the argument's high word (move.w (-0x98,A6)), op 3 its low word (move.w (-0x96,A6) at 0x00E0F518). title: time: time_$set_itimer_internal (0xE58D14) and time_$get_itimer_internal (0xE58C74) are declared but never decompiled
description:
time/time_internal.h declares both, TIME_$SET_ITIMER (time/set_itimer.c) and TIME_$GET_ITIMER (time/get_itimer.c) call them, and nothing in the tree defines them - the m68k link has two unresolved symbols and time/test/test_itimer.c has to mock them.

0x00E58C74 time_$get_itimer_internal, 160 bytes: (which word, value clock_t*, interval clock_t*), a Pascal function (callers reserve a 2-byte result slot at 0xE58F1A and pop 0xC).
0x00E58D14 time_$set_itimer_internal, 324 bytes: six parameters at 0x08 which(w), 0x0A value, 0x0E interval, 0x12 ovalue, 0x16 ointerval, 0x1A status, also a Pascal function (0xE58E70 subq.l #2,SP, 0xE58ECE lea (0x18,SP),SP).

Both work on TIME_$ITIMER_DB at 0xE297F0 (58 entries of 0x1C bytes, plus the virtual half at +0x658) and install TIME_$SET_ITIMER_REAL_CALLBACK (0xE58A38) / TIME_$SET_ITIMER_VIRT_CALLBACK (0xE58A98), whose element-address arithmetic is already recovered in time/set_itimer_real_callback.c.
close_reason: Emitted time/get_itimer_internal.c (0xE58C74) and time/set_itimer_internal.c (0xE58D14), traced block by block. Entry address arithmetic 0xE58C8A-0xE58CA8 / 0xE58DA8-0xE58DC8 is now time_$itimer_entry() in time_internal.h with ITIMER_DB_WHICH_STRIDE 0x658. Recovered the field roles: elem+0x14 is it_interval (0xE58E28 pushes it as TIME_$Q_ADD_CALLBACK's interval), elem+0x0C is the absolute expiry / it_value (0xE58DD8 zero-test disarms; 0xE58CEA SUB48 turns it into remaining time). That means the arguments are in struct-itimerval order, so TIME_$SET_ITIMER / TIME_$GET_ITIMER parameter names were swapped and are now corrected in time.h, get_itimer.c and set_itimer.c. Added status_$time_relative_time_is_too_large 0x000D000E (0xE58D88) plus 0x000D000C/0x000D000D. time/test/test_itimer.c now #includes both new .c files and drives them against a real 2*0x658 arena; 23 tests, 0 failed. title: PROC2_$FORK: MST_$ALLOC_ASID failure path returns an uninitialised status
description: proc2/fork.c: at 0x00E72CC6 the error is written to *status_ret, then the jump to 0x00E73240 exits via 0x00E732D6 which overwrites *status_ret with the A6-0x2C local, never written on that path. Reproduced faithfully; confirm against a second Domain/OS build whether this is a genuine original bug.
close_reason: CONFIRMED an original bug; reproduced, not repaired. Traced every reference to A6-0x2C in the 1814-byte PROC2_$FORK: writes come only from callees handed 'pea (-0x2c,A6)' at 0x00E72D02 (PROC1_$ALLOC_STACK), 0x00E72D46 (PROC1_$BIND), 0x00E72E60 (EC2_$REGISTER_EC1), 0x00E72EA6 (ACL_$ALLOC_ASID), 0x00E72EB6 (AUDIT_$INHERIT_AUDIT), 0x00E72F0E (FILE_$FORK_LOCK), 0x00E72F4A (MST_$FORK), 0x00E72F6E and 0x00E72FA0 (MST_$GET_VA_INFO), 0x00E730FE (PROC1_$RESUME), plus 'bset.b #0x7,(-0x2c,A6)' at 0x00E731B8; reads are at 0x00E73114 (CRASH_SYSTEM) and 0x00E732D6. The MST_$ALLOC_ASID failure branch is taken at 0x00E72CC6, sets bit 31 of the CALLER's status at 0x00E72CC8, then 'bra.w 0x00E73240' at 0x00E72CCC. Every store listed above lies strictly between 0x00E72CCC and 0x00E73240; the range 0x00E73240..0x00E732D4 contains no reference to A6-0x2C at all; and nothing before 0x00E72CCC touches it (the only frame store in 0x00E72BCE..0x00E72CCC is (-0x20,A6) for TIME_$CLOCK). So 0x00E732D6 'move.l (-0x2c,A6),(A2)' hands the caller the previous frame's leftover and discards the real error. That the author knew the difference is visible at 0x00E72C2E, where the 'table full' exit branches to 0x00E732DA, deliberately past that store. No second Domain/OS build to diff against, so the conclusion is documented in proc2/fork.c (a 30-line note on the 'status' declaration plus a note at the branch), in Ghidra (EOL comments at 0x00E72CCC and 0x00E732D6, decompiler comment at 0x00E72CC6), and covered by proc2/test/test_fork.c::test_alloc_asid_failure_goes_to_entry_teardown, which asserts the branch reaches cleanup_entry (0x00E73240) and not cleanup_locked (0x00E73146) and does not assert the indeterminate status.

title: DISK_$GET_QBLKS out-params typed int32_t*/uint32_t* while disk/io.c passes disk_io_req_t**
description: disk/get_qblks.c declares its two out-parameters as int32_t * and uint32_t * but disk/io.c (around line 203) passes disk_io_req_t ** into the same slots and dereferences the result as a pointer.  Identical on m68k (32-bit cells), divergent on a 64-bit host: the callee stores 4 bytes where the caller reads 8.  Same class as source-xuue/source-csok; fix with uint32_t VA cells plus ARCH_VA_TO_PTR at the boundary, or give the callee the real pointer type after checking the store width in the assembly.  Noted by the source-xuue pass.

title: sio2681: SIO2681_$CHANNELS/$CHIPS/$INT_VECTORS are fabricated; the image has one 1-based SIO2681_$PTRS table
description:
SIO2681_$INIT (0x00E333DC) writes a single 16-byte-stride table: 'move.l A3,(-0x8,A4,D0w*0x1)' 0x00E33428, 'move.l (0x10,A6),(-0x10,A4,D0w*0x1)' 0x00E3342C, 'move.l (0x1c,A6),(-0xc,A3,D0w*0x1)' 0x00E3346E, with A3 = A4 = 0x00E2DF80 (Ghidra label SIO2681_$PTRS) and D0 = chip_num*0x10.  Entry layout is {chan_a:+0x00, chan_b:+0x04, chip:+0x08, unused:+0x0C} and the table is 1-BASED (entry 1 is the label itself): TERM_$INIT passes the constant word 1 at 0x00E33220 as chip_num ('pea (0x5a,PC)' at 0x00E331C4).  Only two entries fit, 0x00E2DF80..0x00E2DF9F, before SIO2681_$INT1_RTE at 0x00E2DFA0 - so SIO2681_MAX_CHIPS is 2, not 4.

sio2681/sio2681_data.c instead defines SIO2681_$CHANNELS at a claimed 0x00E2DF70 and SIO2681_$CHIPS at a claimed 0x00E2DF78; they overlap each other and both land inside SIO2681_$DATA's storage (SIO2681_$DATA + 0xB8 / +0xC0).  sio2681/init.c:78-98 indexes them.

SIO2681_$INT_VECTORS is the same story: 0x00E334F0 'move.l (-0x4,A5,D0w*0x1)' with A5 = 0x00E351EC and D0 = chip_num*4 reads a 2-entry 1-based table at 0x00E351EC whose image contents are 0x00E2DFA0 and 0x00E2DFB0 - the two rte stubs SIO2681_$INT1_RTE and SIO2681_$INT2_RTE, which are hand-written assembly and belong in sio2681/sau2/.  The .c declares it as a 4-entry all-NULL array at 0x00E351E8 (0x00E351E8 is the tail of tty_$i_dfl_func_chars).

Also unidentified: the eight longwords 0,2,4,6,1,5,3,0 at 0x00E2DF60..0x00E2DF7F, which nothing in the image references.  TODO marker is at sio2681/init.c:78.
close_reason: Recovered the real objects. SIO2681_$CHANNELS / SIO2681_$CHIPS / SIO2681_$INT_VECTORS(4) are gone from sio2681_data.c and sio2681_internal.h and replaced by: (1) sio2681_ptrs_entry_t SIO2681_$PTRS[2] - the one 16-byte-stride 1-based table at 0xE2DF80 that 0xE33428 'move.l A3,(-0x8,A4,D0w)', 0xE3342C '(-0x10,A4,D0w)' and 0xE3346E '(-0xc,A3,D0w)' write with D0 = chip_num*0x10; the fourth field is not unused - the interrupt stubs store the interrupted PC there at 0xE2DFBC 'move.l (0x12,SP),(0xc,A0)'. (2) SIO2681_MAX_CHIPS is 2, since SIO2681_$INT1_RTE starts at 0xE2DFA0. (3) SIO2681_$INT_VECTORS is the 1-based 2-entry table at 0xE351EC holding 0xE2DFA0/0xE2DFB0, and the vector store at 0xE334F0 targets exception vector (vec-1) off 0x64. (4) The two rte stubs are transcribed to sio2681/sau2/int_rte.s and objdump-compared: 0x38 bytes, identical instruction encodings and identical INT2/common offsets (0x10/0x1C). (5) The eight longwords at 0xE2DF60 are SIO2681_$DATA + 0xA8, read by SIO6509_$RCV at 0xE1D56A with ((status>>4)&7)*4; they are now the sio6509_rcv_flags field with a layout assert. Also corrected while tracing: chan A's 0xE33440 writes 2 to +0x18 and 0xE33446 clears +0x12 (the C had 2 on the +0x10 flags field), and the register base now goes through ARCH_VA_TO_PTR. New sio2681/test/test_init.c #includes the real init.c: 8 tests, 0 failed. Ghidra: SIO2681_$INT_VECTORS and SIO2681_$DATA_SIO6509_RCV_FLAGS labelled, comments on 0xE333DC/0xE33428/0xE334B4/0xE334F0/0xE1D56A.

title: smd_$disp1_setup_blt (0x00E27036) and its twin at 0x00E27070 are not emitted byte-for-byte
description: smd/sau2/disp1_int.s now defines the label smd_$disp1_setup_blt at exactly the offset the image puts it (0x00E27036, right after the four status constants), so SMD_$DISP1_INT's 'jsr (0xa8,PC)' at 0x00E26F8C keeps its original displacement - but the body (0x00E27036..0x00E2720D) is not transcribed. title: FILE_$SET_PROT called with NULL prot_type in dir/set_protection.c
description: FILE_$SET_PROT (0x00E5DF3A) dereferences its 2nd argument immediately ('move.w (A4),D2w' at 0x00E5DF56), so NULL is not possible.  dir/set_protection.c:108 passes NULL - find the constant word cell DIR_$SET_PROTECTION actually pea's and name it, the way dir/do_op_set_prot.c and dir/add_bak_default_prot.c already do.
close_reason: FILE_$SET_PROT's prot_type is the constant word cell at 0xE52392, reached by 'pea (0x40,PC)' at 0x00E52350 (0x00E52350 + 2 + 0x40); the image holds 0x0006, and FILE_$SET_PROT dereferences it at 0x00E5DF56 ('move.w (A4),D2w').  dir/set_protection.c now names it dir_$set_protection_prot_type, the way dir/do_op_set_prot.c passes &prot_type.  The same function had a second NULL of exactly this kind: FILE_$PRIV_LOCK's acl_ctx argument is 'pea (-0x6fe0,PC)' at 0x00E5231A = 0xE4B33C, a constant NIL pointer cell that FILE_$PRIV_LOCK loads at 0x00E5EDDE; it is now dir_$set_protection_acl_ctx.  Re-deriving the frame while there fixed three more things: the request record's opcode byte is at request+0x03 ('move.b #0x52,(-0xe5,A6)' with the record at A6-0xE8), so the record is now a 0xC4-byte packed type with layout asserts; the temp ACL UID is a separate local at A6-0x08, not a field 8 bytes into the response, and the response itself is a Dir_$OpResponse at A6-0x20 whose status is at +0x04 ('move.l (-0x1c,A6),D0'); and the 9ACL test at 0x00E522CC-0x00E522DA reads the WORD at acl_uid+0x04 (the high half of uid.low) and tests bit 8 of it, where the old code tested bit 8 of the whole low longword.  DIR_$DO_OP's fifth argument is 'pea (-0x100,A6)', 0x18 bytes below the request, so it is modelled as its own local; bead source-32ld tracks what it is for.

title: ec/sau2: EC_$ADVANCE / EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH emit bsr.b to ADVANCE_INT as a literal .short
description:
The image's short branches to ADVANCE_INT (0xE2072C) are

  0xE206F6  61 34   (EC_$ADVANCE, 0xE206EE)
  0xE20722  61 08   (EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH, 0xE20718)

gas does keep the two-byte form for 'bsr.b ADVANCE_INT' (it emits 61 00 plus an
R_68K_PC8 fixup on the displacement byte), but the link cannot resolve it.
ADVANCE_INT is the C routine ec/advance_int.c; sau2.ld's '*/ec/*.o(.text)'
gather takes objects in Makefile order, so every ec/*.c object precedes the
ec/sau2/*.s objects and ADVANCE_INT lands ~0xDD0 bytes ahead of the branch -
far outside the +/-127 byte reach of a byte displacement:

  m68k-elf-ld: (.text+0x9):  relocation truncated to fit: R_68K_PC8 against `ADVANCE_INT'
  m68k-elf-ld: (.text+0xb):  relocation truncated to fit: R_68K_PC8 against `ADVANCE_INT'

Byte fidelity wins for now (source-p49c), so both sites emit the image encoding
literally as '.short 0x6134' / '.short 0x6108' with no relocation.  The branch
targets are therefore wrong in the linked image and the symbolic dependency on
ADVANCE_INT is lost.

Real fix is a sau2.ld / Makefile change (not owned by source-p49c): place
ec/advance_int.o and ec/advance_all_int.o immediately after the ec/sau2 objects,
in image order (ADVANCE begins at 0xE20728, right after
EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH ends at 0xE20727), and then restore 'bsr.b'.
close_reason:
Fixed: sau2.ld now spells out the head of the ec/proc1 run object by object, in the SAU2 map's PROC1_ASM order (PROC1_ASM 0xE1EAC8+0x24A4):

     E20610 EC_$WAIT / E2063E EC_$WAITN / E206D2 PROC1_$REMOVE_READY /
     E206EE EC_$ADVANCE / E20702 EC_$ADVANCE_ALL /
     E20718 EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH / E20728 ADVANCE / E207C6 ADVANCE_ALL_INT

so ec/advance_int.o (ADVANCE_INT) directly follows the three ec/sau2 objects
instead of preceding all of them.  The map's interleaving is honoured too -
PROC1_$REMOVE_READY comes from proc1/remove_ready.o and sits between waitn.o
and advance.o.  The catch-all '*/ec/*.o' and '*/proc1/*.o' gathers stay after
the explicit list and pick up the rest.  No Makefile change was needed.

ec/sau2/advance.s and ec/sau2/advance_without_dispatch.s now write
'bsr.b ADVANCE_INT' again; both .short literals are gone.  Object bytes
(objcopy -O binary -j .text) vs 'gsk read':

  advance.o                 00 7c 07 00 20 6f 00 04 61 00 61 00 00 00 02 7c f8 ff 4e 75
  image 0xE206EE            00 7c 07 00 20 6f 00 04 61 34 61 00 03 26 02 7c f8 ff 4e 75
  advance_without_dispatch.o 40 e7 00 7c 07 00 20 6f 00 06 61 00 46 df 4e 75
  image 0xE20718             40 e7 00 7c 07 00 20 6f 00 06 61 08 46 df 4e 75

Every byte matches except the two relocated displacements, and the .text sizes
(0x14 and 0x10) are exactly the image's 0xE206EE..0xE20701 and
0xE20718..0xE20727 - the branch is the image's 2-byte form again, so nothing
after it is displaced.

Remaining, in the LINKED image only (both filed as source-0ke7): the
displacements come out 61 32 / 61 04 rather than 61 34 / 61 08.
  -4  ADVANCE (0xE20728, '20 6f 00 04', the C-callable entry that falls
      through into ADVANCE_INT at 0xE2072C) is not in the tree; ec/advance_int.o
      starts directly at ADVANCE_INT.
  +2  gas gives every .s .text section 2**2 alignment, so a 2-byte pad follows
      advance_all.o (image size 0x16, ending 2-mod-4).
Both .s files carry a TODO(source-0ke7, 0xE20728) saying so.

source-0i3's docs/design-per-process-data.md is not pre-empted: this change
only reorders .text INPUT statements inside the existing .text output section
and touches no data cell, while that design adds separate '.moddata.<name>'
OUTPUT sections at fixed A5 addresses.

Gates: make clean && make -k -j8 -> no error:/warning: lines, 0 relocation
truncations, link reaches ld and fails only on the pre-existing undefined
references; make test -> 180 tests, 0 failed; duplicate-global scan (nm
--defined-only over all 1416 objects, sort|uniq -d) empty.

title: xns_$copy_header is a dead duplicate of xns_$copy_error_header; neither body matches 0x00E17876
description:
xns/xns_internal.h:221 declares 'uint8_t xns_$copy_header(void *packet_info)' with 'Original address: 0x00E17876'. Nothing in the tree defines it. xns/error_send.c:79 defines a file-static 'xns_$copy_error_header' at the SAME address. Two names, one address, one of them dead.

Call-order evidence picks error_send.c's name: XNS_ERROR_$SEND (0x00E17A2E) calls 0x00E17876 at 0x00E17B14 and 0x00E17960 at 0x00E17B1E, matching error_send.c:188-189. Ghidra is now xns_$copy_error_header / xns_$setup_error_header.

Separately, NEITHER C body reproduces the machine code. 0x00E17876 is 50 bytes:

  00e17876  link.w A6,-0x10
  00e1787a  movea.l (0x8,A6),A0
  00e1787e  st D0b
  00e17880  lea (0x18,A0),A0
  00e17884  bra.b 0x00e178a0
  00e17888  move.l (0x4,A0),D1
  00e1788c  cmp.l (0x70,A5),D1
  00e17890  blt.b 0x00e17898      | D1 <  A5+0x70 -> false
  00e17892  cmp.l (0x6c,A5),D1
  00e17896  blt.b 0x00e1789c      | D1 <  A5+0x6C -> next node
  00e17898  clr.b D0b             | otherwise false
  ...
  00e1789c  movea.l (0x8,A0),A0   | next
  00e178a0  cmpa.w #0x0,A0
  00e178a4  bne.b 0x00e17888

It walks the chain starting at arg1+0x18 (link at +0x08) and returns TRUE (0xFF) only if every node's longword at +0x04 lies in [A5+0x70, A5+0x6C). It copies nothing. The tree's version returns pkt[0x2D]. 0x00E17960 (204 bytes, a nested procedure reading the parent frame via A6) is an empty stub in the tree. Both need re-emission.
close_reason: Closed

title: SMD_$ subsystem analysis and implementation
description:
# SMD_$ Subsystem Analysis and Implementation

## Overview
SMD = Screen Management Display - manages display hardware, cursors, fonts, and screen operations for Domain/OS.

## Analysis Complete
- **75+ functions identified** in the SMD_$ namespace
- **Key data structures mapped**:
  - `smd_globals_t` at 0x00E82B8C - global state including ASID-to-unit mapping, blanking state
  - `smd_display_unit_t` at 0x00E2E3FC - per-display unit state (0x10C bytes each)
  - `smd_display_hw_t` - hardware info pointed from unit (display type, dimensions, lock state, etc.)
  - `smd_display_info_t` at 0x00E27376 - display configuration (0x60 bytes each)

## Files Created
- `smd/smd.h` - Public API (50+ function prototypes)
- `smd/smd_internal.h` - Internal structures and helpers
- `smd/smd_data.c` - Global variable definitions
- `smd/cold_init.c` - SMD_$COLD_INIT (no-op stub)
- `smd/unblank.c` - SMD_$UNBLANK implementation
- `smd/inq_disp_type.c` - SMD_$INQ_DISP_TYPE implementation
- `smd/inq_disp_info.c` - SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO implementation
- `smd/video_ctl.c` - SMD_$VIDEO_CTL implementation
- `smd/assoc.c` - SMD_$ASSOC implementation
- `smd/sau2/lock_display.s` - SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY assembly (uses SR manipulation)
- `tpad/tpad.h` - Stub header for trackpad subsystem

## Build Status
- Makefile updated to include smd/*.c and smd/sau2/*.s
- Build blocked by pre-existing issues in ast/allocate_aste.c (CRASH_SYSTEM signature mismatch)
- Once ast issue fixed, SMD files should compile

## Key Functions Analyzed
- SMD_$INIT (0x00E34D2C) - Main initialization, has jump table complexity
- SMD_$ASSOC (0x00E6D882) - Associates display with process ASID
- SMD_$INQ_DISP_INFO (0x00E70124) - Returns display type, dimensions, bit depth
- SMD_$VIDEO_CTL (0x00E6F838) - Enable/disable video output
- SMD_$UNBLANK (0x00E6EFB4) - Restore blanked display
- SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY (0x00E15CCE) - Low-level lock with interrupt disable

## Display Types Identified
- 1, 2: Mono landscape/portrait (1024x800 / 800x1024)
- 3, 4: Color 1024x2048
- 5, 9: Hi-res 2048x1024
- 6, 8, 10, 11: Mono 1024x1024 variants

## Remaining Work
- Fix pre-existing build issues in ast/ subsystem
- Implement remaining SMD functions (BLT, scroll, cursor, font, tracking)
- Add unit tests for non-hardware-dependent functions
- Complete SMD_$INIT (complex jump table decompilation)

## Dependencies
- ec/ec.h - Event counts for synchronization
- proc1/proc1.h - PROC1_$AS_ID for current process
- time/time.h - TIME_$CLOCKH for blanking timestamps
- term/term.h - TERM_$SET_REAL_LINE_DISCIPLINE
- tpad/tpad.h - TPAD_$SET_UNIT (stub created)

title: Name the memory error source register at 0xFFB40A
description: FIM_$BUS_ERR (fim/sau2/bus_err.s) reads bits 5 and 4 of the byte at 0xFFB40A to choose between status 0x00070004 / 0x00070005 / 0x00070006 before calling CRASH_SYSTEM, then writes 0x4000 to the word to acknowledge.  It is the only code in the image that touches the register (gsk xrefs to 0x00FFB40A shows exactly the three accesses at 0x00E21A34, 0x00E21A42, 0x00E21A5A), so its real name and bit layout are unconfirmed.  bus_err.s calls it MMU_ERR_SRC_REG with a TODO; mmu/mmu.h documents only 0xFFB400..0xFFB409 and should grow an entry once the name is known.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: toshok
comments.text:
RESOLVED: the register at 0xFFB40A is Apollo's *MMU Parity Register* [800A-800B].

Citation: Domain Engineering Handbook 002398-04 Rev4 (Jan87), DN3xx chapter, p.7-27 (~/src/domainos-archeology/docs/apollo-docs/002398-04_Domain_Engineering_Handbook_Rev4_Jan87.pdf).  SAU2 = DN300/DN320/DN330 (docs/saus.md).  Word layout:
  bit 15 Write Wrong MMU Parity (both PFT and PTT)  [R/W]
  bit 14 MMU Parity Fault Enable (MMU PFE)          [R/W]
  bit 13 PTT Parity Error                            [CLR]
  bit 12 PFT Parity Error                            [CLR]
  bits 11..0 PFTX, the PFT index of the failing entry [R/O]
Handbook note: 'Bus error occurs on parity operation if MMU PFE is set, and bits 12 and 13 were clear.'

This matches the code exactly.  m68k is big-endian, so the byte at 0xFFB40A is word bits 15..8: btst #5 (0x00E21A34) = word bit 13 = PTT parity -> status 0x00070004 'ptt parity error'; btst #4 (0x00E21A42) = word bit 12 = PFT parity -> status 0x00070005 'pft parity error'; neither -> 0x00070006 'mmu timeout'.  The move.w #0x4000 (0x00E21A5A) sets PFE, clears write-wrong-parity, and writes 0 into the two CLR bits, i.e. acknowledges the latched error and re-arms parity faults.

The same page also confirms the neighbours bus_err.s already used: 0xFFB402 is the FPU Owner Register (write-only ASID) and 0xFFB403 is the DN330 MMU Status Register, whose bit 0 is '0 -> Stingray 020 board' (so 1 = DN300/320, which has no parity register), bit 3 'MMU Error (timeout or parity), valid only if bit 5 set', bit 5 'Bus/MMU timeout or MMU Parity Error'.

Searched and did NOT find the name: sau2-maps/domain_os.10.2.map and .10.3.map name only the FFB400 page as 'MMU' (IODEFS section), no per-register absolute symbols; sr10.4-install and the other SAU maps were not needed once the handbook settled it.

Changes: mmu/mmu.h grows MMU_PARITY_REG plus MMU_PARITY_{PFTX_MASK,PFT_ERR,PTT_ERR,PFE,WRITE_WRONG,ACK} and the three status_$mmu_* codes, with the full citation; fim/sau2/bus_err.s renames MMU_ERR_SRC_REG -> MMU_PARITY_REG and drops the TODO.  Ghidra: label MMU_PARITY_REG at 0x00FFB40A, disassembly comments at 0x00E21A34/0x00E21A42/0x00E21A5A.

title: DIR_$DO_OP remote path: wrong status width and a dropped DIR_$UPDATE_HINT argument
description:
Found while auditing Dir_$OpResponse (source-6ci); these are not offset problems so they were left for a separate pass.

1. dir/do_op.c passes (int16_t)resp->status to DIR_$IS_RETRYABLE_STATUS; 0xE4C150 pushes the full longword (move.l D1,-(SP)).
2. The DIR_$UPDATE_HINT call after a redirect passes 0 as its last argument, but the assembly pushes a longword out of the reply: (0x30,A3) on the path from 0xE4C1E2 and (0x1e,A3) on the path from 0xE4C222, then pea (0x16,A3) at 0xE4C226 and bsr 0xE4BC76.
3. The case 0x58 (RESOLVE) handler argument order in dir/do_op.c does not match the push order at 0xE4C896-0xE4C8CE (0x4, 0x2e, 0x2c, 0x2a, 0x28, 0x26, 0x15, 0x14, 0x1e, 0x30, 0x16); worth re-deriving dir_$do_op_resolve's signature from the callee at 0xE4D0E2.
close_reason:
All three items fixed in dir/do_op.c and covered by the new dir/test/test_do_op.c (16 tests, 0 failed).
1. DIR_$IS_RETRYABLE_STATUS now gets resp->status whole; 0x00E4C150 is 'move.l D1,-(SP)' and the callee at 0x00E4BC26 compares five longwords and also tests byte (0x9,A6).
2. DIR_$UPDATE_HINT's last argument is (0x30,A3) on the RESOLVE path from 0x00E4C1E2 and (0x1e,A3) on the GET_ENTRYU path from 0x00E4C222 - never 0. Its two hint arguments also go by value (0x00E4C230/0x00E4C234) and index hints[k], the pair the request was sent to, not k+1; HINT_$ADDI had the same off-by-one at 0x00E4C1A6 and 0x00E4C9A8. Added Dir_$OpResponse.resolve.redirect at +0x30.
3. dir_$do_op_resolve's fourteen arguments re-derived from the callee frame at 0x00E4D0E2 (0x08 path, 0x0C len, 0x0E &r16, 0x12 &r30, 0x16 &r1e, 0x1A &r14, 0x1E &r15, 0x22 &r26, 0x26 &r28, 0x2A &r2a, 0x2E &r2c, 0x32 req+0xAC, 0x36 &r2e, 0x3A &status); the call site was shifted by one from argument 4 on and passed reply+0x0A where the assembly pushes request+0xAC.
Also proven from the same basic blocks and fixed: the reply-version test at 0x00E4C174-0x00E4C18C (it read reply+0x08 twice and inverted the second comparison), the post-switch fallback at 0x00E4C99C-0x00E4C9D4 (it neither advanced the hint index nor honoured the server-process check the way 'tst.b D4b; bmi' does), the case-0x32 call to dir_$do_op_cname (packed word pairs; the callee frame at 0x00E518BC has a seventh slot at A6+0x0C fed from request+0x0E), and the per-operation parameter table at 0x00E7FB9C is now typed as DIR_$OP_PARAMS instead of two scalar DAT_ externs indexed by pointer arithmetic.

title: network_$failure_rec_t: +0x04 and +0x0C are named backwards
description:
network/network.h names network_$failure_rec_t+0x04 'error_info' and +0x0C 'node_id'.  Both writers say the opposite:

NETWORK_$REPORT_FAILURE (0x00E103FA), with A5 = 0x00E248FC and the record at A5+0x2F8:
  0x00E10408  move.l (0x00e2b0d4).l,(0x300,A5)   +0x08 <- TIME_$CLOCKH
  0x00E10410  st (0x2fa,A5)                      +0x02 <- 0xFF
  0x00E10414  move.l (0x00e245a4).l,(0x2fc,A5)   +0x04 <- NODE_$ME
  0x00E1042E  move.l D0,(0x304,A5)               +0x0C <- 1 or 3 (from bit 5 of the argument)

ASKNODE_$SERVER request 0x0E (0x00E65D04):
  0x00E65D0E  move.l D6,(0x4,A0)                 +0x04 <- requesting node
  0x00E65D12  move.l (0x00e2b0e4).l,(0x8,A0)     +0x08 <- TIME_$CURRENT_CLOCKH
  0x00E65D1A  move.l (-0x264,A6),(0xc,A0)        +0x0C <- request word

So +0x04 is the reporting node and +0x0C is the failure type.  /etc/netmain's hardware-failure display agrees: it prints 'v<n>  Failure type = <lh>' and 'reported by <node> at <time>'.  Rename +0x04 to node_id and +0x0C to failure_type, and check the ~few readers.

title: chksum: emit CHKSUM_$GET_CHKSUM (0x00E0A314) as chksum/sau2/get_chksum.s
description: chksum/chksum.h currently only declares it.  CHKSUM_$GET_CHKSUM is hand-written assembly: no link/unlk, it reads its argument at (0x4,SP) and returns the 16-bit sum of 512 words in D0 (movea.l (0x4,SP),A0 / moveq #0 / move.w #0xff,D1 / two add.w (A0)+,D0w / dbf).  Per CLAUDE.md it belongs in chksum/sau2/get_chksum.s with a C-ABI wrapper, and the chksum directory then needs adding to SUBSYSTEMS in the Makefile.  Referenced by TODO(source-cm2w) in chksum/chksum.h -- retarget that TODO at the new bead.
close_reason: CHKSUM_$GET_CHKSUM (0x00E0A314, 20 bytes) emitted as chksum/sau2/get_chksum.s and verified byte-for-byte: m68k-elf-objcopy -O binary gives 206f00047000323c00ffd058d05851c9fffa4e75, identical to the image bytes from gsk read 0x00E0A314 20. It is hand-written asm (no link/unlk, argument read at (0x4,SP), result left in D0). chksum/chksum_internal.h added with CHKSUM_LOOP_COUNT (0xFF, so the dbf body runs 256 times) and CHKSUM_WORDS_PER_ITER; chksum/chksum.h gained CHKSUM_PAGE_WORDS/CHKSUM_PAGE_SIZE and lost its TODO. chksum/get_chksum.c is the !ARCH_M68K model: it assembles each word from its two bytes so the big-endian sum survives on a little-endian host, and keeps the modulo-2^16 wrap that add.w gives. chksum added to SUBSYSTEMS in the Makefile (between cal and dbuf); the m68k build produces an empty chksum/get_chksum.o and the symbol from chksum/sau2/get_chksum.o, and disk/chksum_page.c's reference now resolves. chksum/test/test_get_chksum.c #includes the .c and calls the real function: 6 tests covering the zero page, the 512-word count, reading exactly 1024 bytes (guard bytes past the page ignored, first and last words counted), big-endian word assembly, the add.w wrap (0x8000+0x8000, 0xFFFF+0x0002, 512*0xFFFF), and order independence. Ghidra: decompiler comment at 0x00E0A314. TODO(source-cm2w) in chksum.h retired along with the rest of that header text.

title: ec/sau2: EC_$ADVANCE and EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH use bsr.w where the image has bsr.b
description:
Byte-fidelity drift found while fixing source-uwxz (no bytes changed there).

The image branches to ADVANCE_INT (0xE2072C) with the 2-byte short form:
  0xE206F6  61 34   bsr.b  ->  0xE206F8 + 0x34 = 0xE2072C   (EC_$ADVANCE, 0xE206EE)
  0xE20722  61 08   bsr.b  ->  0xE20724 + 0x08 = 0xE2072C   (EC_$ADVANCE_WITHOUT_DISPATCH, 0xE20718)

ec/sau2/advance.s:21 and ec/sau2/advance_without_dispatch.s both write 'bsr.w ADVANCE_INT', which gas assembles as 61 00 xx xx - two bytes too long, so every following instruction in those routines is displaced relative to the image.  The neighbours are already right: advance.s's second branch (bsr.w PROC1_$DISPATCH_INT, image 61 00 03 26) and advance_all.s's two bsr.w are genuinely long form, and proc1/sau2/dispatch.s already uses bsr.s for the image's 61 06 at 0xE20A18.

Now that sau2.ld emits ec/ and proc1/ as one contiguous run (source-uwxz), the short form is in range, so the fix is just s/bsr.w/bsr.b/ at those two sites plus an objcopy-vs-'gsk read' byte check of 0xE206EE..0xE20701 and 0xE20718..0xE20727.
close_reason: Closed

title: Identify the AST common-attributes word at +0x14 that FILE_$PRIV_UNLOCK gates its read-lock probe on
description: file/priv_unlock.c reads AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES' output word at +0x14 (0x00E60240 'tst.w (-0x2c,A6)' with the buffer at A6-0x40) and only asks the lock holder for a read lock (REM_FILE_$LOCAL_READ_LOCK) when it is zero. AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES (0x00E04A00) fills it at 0x00E04A46 from the full attribute record's +0x74. The field's meaning is unidentified, so the accessor is spelled FILE_CATTR_W14 in file/priv_unlock.c. Identifying it should also produce a proper struct for the common-attributes record, which several file/ and dir/ call sites currently treat as a raw byte buffer.
close_reason: The word at ast_$common_attr_t+0x14 is the object's REFERENCE COUNT (aote+0x80). Derivation: AST_$GET_COMMON_ATTRIBUTES (0x00E04A00) has 'link.w A6,-0x90' and the whole frame is the full attribute record, so 'move.w (-0x1c,A6),(0x14,A2)' at 0x00E04A46 reads record+0x74 (-0x1C + 0x90); AST_$GET_ATTRIBUTES fills that record verbatim from aote+0x0C ('lea (0xc,A2),A0' + moveq #0x23 + 36 long moves at 0x00E049A2), so record+0x74 = aote+0x80, which is the word AST_$SET_ATTR_DISPATCH's attributes 6/7/8 increment ('addq.w #0x1,(0x80,A2)' at 0x00E04CEE) and decrement (0x00E04D52), both guarded by 'cmpi.w #-0xb' = 0xFFF5 and status_$ast_refcount_underflow. FILE_$PRIV_UNLOCK therefore only asks the lock holder for a read lock when the object has no references left. Produced the struct the bead asked for: ast_$common_attr_t in ast/ast.h (0x18 bytes, offsets asserted) with obj_type/sub_type/attr_flags_hi/attr_flags_lo at 0x00..0x03, length at 0x04 (record+0x14 = aote+0x20), mod_time at 0x08, blocks at 0x10, refcount at 0x14, access_flags at 0x16. Fixed ast/get_common_attributes.c, whose two source offsets were wrong (it read record+0x1C instead of +0x74 for the refcount and record+0x25 instead of +0x65 for the access flags - the A6 displacements had not been rebased by 0x90). Converted every call site off the raw byte buffer: file/priv_unlock.c (now attrs.cattr.refcount / .obj_type), file/set_prot.c, dir/validate_handle.c, dir/do_op_add_mount.c, dir/do_op_create_dir.c, dir/old_set_default_acl.c, dir/do_op_add_bak.c, dir/do_op_add_link.c and log/init.c. Six of those were writing 0x18 bytes into buffers of 1, 4 or 8 bytes; four were reading the wrong offset (add_mount read +0x03 instead of the sub_type at +0x01, add_bak and create_dir read +0x04, log/init read +0x00 instead of the length at +0x04); five were passing a bare uid_t where the callee needs a 0x20-byte file_$obj_loc_t with the UID at +0x08; and dir/do_op_add_bak.c had the sub-type test inverted (0x00E50B24-0x00E50B3C ORs three seq results and 'bmi' takes the DELETE path when one matched, so only sub-types 0/4/5 may be replaced). dir/validate_handle.c's attribute block is now fully wired from the record instead of seven uninitialised locals, including the type-9-process OS-only check at 0x00E4B4B6-0x00E4B4D8 that was missing. Ghidra: prototype and comments set on 0x00E04A00, 0x00E04A30, 0x00E04A46, 0x00E04A4C, 0x00E60240, 0x00E4B4B6.

title: SMD_BLINK_FUNC_PTABLE overlaps smd_globals_t's tail at SMD_GLOBALS+0x1DA0
description: SMD_$BLINK_CURSOR_CALLBACK loads the per-unit blink routine with 'lea (0x0,A5,D0*0x1),A0' / 'movea.l (0x1da0,A0),A1' (0x00E6FF84/0x00E6FF88) where A5 = 0x00E82B8C = &SMD_GLOBALS and D0 = default_unit*4, i.e. the table base is SMD_GLOBALS + 0x1DA0 = 0x00E8492C and the index is the unit number itself, NOT unit-1.  But smd_internal.h already names 0x1DA0 'last_idm_button' (a word, SMD_$GET_IDM_EVENT 0x00E6EE7C) and 0x1DA2 'power_off_reported', and sizeof(smd_globals_t) is asserted to be 0x1DA4 - so unit 1's entry (0x00E84930) starts one byte past the end of the record.  smd_internal.h declares 'extern smd_blink_func_t SMD_BLINK_FUNC_PTABLE[SMD_MAX_DISPLAY_UNITS]' as a separate object that nothing defines (it is in the link's undefined list), so today the C model has two different names for overlapping storage.  Per the 'second global at address X' rule (compute X - 0x00E82B8C first), decide which reading is right: either smd_globals_t is short and 0x1DA0.. is really the pointer table, or the table starts elsewhere.  Read 0x00E84924..0x00E84940 in the image and check every writer of the table (SMD_$INIT / SMD_$WS_INIT) before choosing.

title: dir_insert_ctx_t.handle is a 32-bit pointer; not dereferenceable on 64-bit hosts
description: dir/insert_entry.c dereferences the directory handle directly: *(int8_t *)((char *)(uintptr_t)ctx->handle + 0x0E) in the simple insertion path (0xE4FD3E) and again for the volatile-directory check. ctx->handle is uint32_t because m68k pointers are 32 bits, so on a 64-bit host the cast produces an invalid pointer and the simple path cannot be unit tested (dir/test/test_insert_entry.c works around it by failing dir_$alloc_split_page first). Options: type dir_insert_ctx_t.handle as void* (it is a reconstruction of the parent frame, not an on-disk record), or route it through an arch handle-conversion helper like the NAME_$HANDLE_TO_PTR pair now in name/name_internal.h.
close_reason: dir_insert_ctx_t.handle stays a uint32_t (it is the 32-bit kernel virtual address dir_$add_entry receives at A6+0x08), but every dereference in dir/ now goes through NAME_$HANDLE_TO_PTR / NAME_$PTR_TO_HANDLE: insert_entry.c, add_entry.c, alloc_split_page.c, finalize_split.c, purify_split_pages.c. title: Revisit CPU architecture vs SAU vs feature-level code organization
description:
The current code organization uses SAU (System Architecture Unit) numbers for platform-specific code splits (e.g., ec/sau2/advance.s). However, this conflates several different concerns:

1. **CPU architecture** (m68k vs x86 vs ARM) - instruction set, calling conventions, register usage
2. **SAU variants** (sau1, sau2, etc.) - Apollo-specific hardware configurations
3. **Feature-level differences** - e.g., MMU type, peripheral support

The ec/sau2/*.s files contain m68k assembly for SR (Status Register) manipulation to disable/enable interrupts. This is fundamentally a CPU architecture concern, not an SAU-level concern - the same code would work on any m68k-based SAU.

Consider reorganizing to something like:
- `ec/arch/m68k/` for m68k-specific assembly
- `ec/arch/x86/` for x86 equivalents (when porting)
- Keep SAU-level splits only for actual hardware variant differences

This would make the retargetability goal clearer and avoid confusion about what each directory level represents.
close_reason: Closed

    00e27060  4e b9 00 e2 07 28   jsr (0x00e20728).l

routine with %a0 unset.

The image's other two ADVANCE callers, 0xE14760 and 0xE7566E, are not in the
tree yet - check them when those functions land.  Owner: smd.

title: xns: xns_$pkt_desc_t and xns_$sock_pkt_t are not host-faithful (header is a C pointer)
description:
xns_$pkt_desc_t declares 'xns_$idp_header_t *header' at +0x1C and xns_$sock_pkt_t declares one at +0x00.  On a 64-bit host those are 8 bytes, so sizeof(xns_$pkt_desc_t) is 96 rather than 0x48, iov lands at 0x28 rather than 0x20 and every field after it shifts; the layout _Static_asserts only hold because they sit under '#if defined(ARCH_M68K)'.

Consequences: no host test can alias the record, and the descriptor chain that starts at packet record +0x18 ({data_len, header, iov} = a mac_os_$buf_desc_t) cannot be walked as one.  xns/error_send.c works around it with xns_$pkt_head_desc(), which lifts the three fields out by name.

The fix is the one route/rip already use: declare the field 'uint32_t header' (a target VA) and go through ARCH_VA_TO_PTR / ARCH_PTR_TO_VA at the seven use sites in xns/idp_demux.c (lines 110, 137, 219, 282, 391 plus the two header_len reads), then move the asserts out of the ARCH_M68K guard so the host build checks them too.  Same for xns_$sock_pkt_t.header and xns/test/test_idp_demux.c.
close_reason: xns_$pkt_desc_t.header (+0x1C), xns_$pkt_desc_t.channel (+0x30) and xns_$sock_pkt_t.header (+0x00) are now uint32_t target VAs instead of C pointers, and both records are __attribute__((packed)) because mac_src_hi/+0x26 and mac_src_lo/+0x2A sit two bytes off a longword boundary (m68k aligns 32-bit fields to two, a 64-bit host to four; packing changes no m68k layout). sizeof(xns_$pkt_desc_t) is 0x48 and sizeof(xns_$sock_pkt_t) is 0x40 on both, so all their _Static_asserts plus the xns_$mac_rcv_t ones moved OUT of the '#if defined(ARCH_M68K)' guard and now run in the host build. Converted at the seven use sites in xns/idp_demux.c with ARCH_VA_TO_PTR / ARCH_PTR_TO_VA (0xE184CC, 0xE1861A, 0xE186C8, 0xE18BA8, 0xE18BEE, 0xE18C12). xns/error_send.c's xns_$pkt_head_desc no longer needs ARCH_PTR_TO_VA - the field is already a VA - and the file now carries three asserts proving {data_len, header, iov} at +0x18 lines up field for field with mac_os_$buf_desc_t {length, address, next}, which is what 0xE17880 'lea (0x18,A0),A0' and 0xE17978 assume; the head is still returned by value because taking the address of a packed member trips -Werror=address-of-packed-member. Tests updated to round-trip through ARCH_HOST_VA_BASE: test_error_send 10/0, test_idp_demux 21/0, test_idp_send 29/0.

There is no FIM_$FAULT in the image or in the SR10.4 maps.  Ghidra names 0x00E21828 FIM_$FAULT_RETURN, and all six sr10.4-install/sau*/domain_os.map files list exactly one symbol there (FIM_$FAULT_RETURN, e.g. 3C42C2D6 in sau7) and no FIM_$FAULT at all.  fim/fim.h already declares only FIM_$FAULT_RETURN, so the FIM side is consistent; trap8.s is the odd one out.

trap8.s currently does 'jsr FIM_$FAULT / unlk %a6 / jmp FIM_$FAULT_RETURN', i.e. it names two distinct callees.  Re-derive the real callee of that jsr from the image (0x00E7B240 is not yet turned into a function in Ghidra, so 'gsk analyze' returns nothing there) and rename it to whatever it actually is.

Owner: svc.  Raised while closing source-refr / source-zsgb from fim/.

title: SMD_$BIT_SET's portable model is not atomic
description: smd/bit_set.c (built only for !ARCH_M68K) does a plain read-modify-write where the original relies on the m68k bset being an indivisible bus cycle (0x00E15D16).  A real non-m68k port needs the host's atomic test-and-set.  The m68k build uses smd/sau2/bit_set.s and is unaffected.  A TODO marks the spot.
close_reason: smd/bit_set.c now does the read-modify-write atomically: 'old_value = (uint8_t)__atomic_fetch_or(byte_ptr, 0x80u, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);' followed by the same 'was the old bit 7 clear' test.  That matches what the original relies on - 0x00E15D16 'bset.b #0x7,(A0)' is a single indivisible read-modify-write bus cycle and 0x00E15D1A 'seq D0b' turns the *previous* state of the bit into the Domain boolean - and both gcc and clang lower __atomic_fetch_or on a byte to one atomic RMW instruction/sequence, with no library call and no header dependency (important here because the tree builds -ffreestanding).  The file is still compiled only when ARCH_M68K is undefined; the m68k build links smd/sau2/bit_set.s and is unaffected.  The TODO(source-ssma) marker is removed and the header comment now records why the atomic is required rather than warning that it is missing.

title: ast_$force_activate_segment's second parameter is a longword the callee never reads
description:
SETTLED, and the bead's premise was wrong: ast_$force_activate_segment (0x00E020FA) DOES read A6+0x0C -- nine times.  The "dead parameter" reading came from the decompiler; the disassembly shows:
  0x00E02194  move.l (0xc,A6),(0x8,A3)   aote+0x08 := the argument
  0x00E021B2  tst.w  (0xc,A6) / smi      bit 31 -> aote+0xB9 remote flag
  0x00E021CC  tst.w  (0xc,A6) / bmi      local vs remote branch
  0x00E021D8  and.l  #0x7fffffff         low byte -> aote+0xB8 volume index
  0x00E021E6  and.l  #0xfffff            node id  -> aote+0xB0 (obj_loc.node)
  0x00E021FA  move.l (0xc,A6),-(SP)      NETWORK_$GET_NET(loc, &aote+0xAC, st)
  0x00E02228  and.l  #0x7fffffff / bne   zero selects the hint search
  0x00E02244  pea    (0xc,A6)            &loc to AST_$LOOKUP_WITH_HINTS, which
                                         writes the resolved network/node back
                                         through it (0x00E01D08, 0x00E01D2A)
  0x00E02260  move.l (0xc,A6),(0x8,A3)   re-store after that resolution

It is a LONGWORD (all move.l/and.l; the tst.w tests the high word, which on this big-endian machine is the sign of the whole longword), named "location".  Encoding: bit 31 = remote, bits 0..19 node id, bits 20..30 network number; bit 31 clear = local with the logical volume index in the low byte; 0 = "location unknown".  It is the same word AST_$GET_LOCATION returns to its caller (move.l (0x8,A0),(A1) at 0x00E04766), and the same word ast/load_aote.c:117 and ast/activate_aote_canned.c:47 rebuild as (x & 0xFFF00000) | node.

AST_$GET_ATTRIBUTES's A6-0x14 holds a plain longword ZERO: clr.l (-0x14,A6) at 0x00E04822, never stored to again, pushed at 0x00E04832.  It is one of eleven callers that pass zero; the two that do not are AST_$MSTE_ACTIVATE_AND_WIRE (mste+0x0C, 0x00E02F64) and AST_$GET_DTV (its own second argument, 0x00E054C6).  The SR10.4 map has no entry for the callee (it is module-local), so no name came from there.

Renamed: the parameter, and mste_t.vol_uid -> mste_t.location, AST_$GET_DTV's "unused" -> "location", AST_$GET_LOCATION's "vol_uid_out" -> "location_out", plus Ghidra prototypes at 0x00E020FA / 0x00E05476 / 0x00E046C8.  aote_t.vol_uid keeps its name for now -- mmap/ also spells it that way; tracked as source-thsz.

Fixed in ast/force_activate_segment.c while documenting it (all fidelity bugs about this argument): the sign test was (int16_t)location, i.e. the LOW word; NETWORK_$GET_NET was passed (aote + 0xAC) with aote_t pointer arithmetic instead of (char*)aote + 0xAC; AST_$LOOKUP_WITH_HINTS was passed aote+0x0C instead of &location as its second argument; the aote+0xB9 update dropped the preserved low bits and the unconditional bclr #6 at 0x00E021C6; and the post-lookup control flow now follows the branches at 0x00E02266/0x00E02286/0x00E022A8/0x00E022AE/0x00E022B4 instead of a flattened if-chain.

title: CAL_$WRITE_CALENDAR writes the MSM5832 leap bit at D10 bit 3, TIME_$READ_CAL uses bit 2
description: cal/write_calendar.c 0x00E816D6 does 'add.w #0x50,D1w' on the day before splitting it into tens/ones, which sets bit 3 of the D10 (date tens) register.  TIME_$READ_CAL sets the leap flag with 'bset.l #2' (0x00E2AE78) and masks the date tens with 3 (0x00E2AEC8), i.e. bit 2 - which is where the MSM5832 datasheet puts the leap-year bit.  The 0x50 looks like the 24-hour-select idiom used for the hour (0x00E816EA, H10 bit 3) applied to the wrong register.  Both sides are reproduced faithfully in C with a TODO comment in cal/write_calendar.c; this bead tracks confirming the hardware behaviour (MSM5832 datasheet / a second SAU image) before deciding whether it is an original bug.
close_reason: Confirmed an original bug in the writer; both sides left reproduced as found. MSM5832 D10 (address 8) is {D0,D1 = date tens, D2 = leap year, D3 = unused}; H10 (address 5) is {D0,D1 = hour tens, D2 = PM, D3 = 24-hour select}. Both routines compute the SAME leap predicate -- (year mod 100 + (month > 2)) mod 4 == 0 (writer 0x00E816C0..0x00E816D4; reader 0x00E2AE60..0x00E2AE72, where the -0x51/+0x64 and the +1 cancel the 80) -- but deposit it in different bits. TIME_$READ_CAL uses bset.l #2 (0x00E2AE78) = D10 bit 2 and masks the date tens with 3 (0x00E2AEC8), which is correct. CAL_$WRITE_CALENDAR does add.w #0x50,D1w (0x00E816D6) before the /10 split; since (v+80)/10 == v/10 + 8 and (v+80)%10 == v%10, that lands in D10 bit 3, the unused bit, so the chip's leap counter is never programmed. The identical add.w #0x50 on the hour (0x00E816EA) IS correct because H10 bit 3 is the 24-hour select -- the idiom was copied onto the wrong register. The correct constant for the date would have been 0x28. Benign in practice: the reader masks D10 with 3 and the chip ignores D3, and TIME_$READ_CAL rewrites D10 with bit 2 set on every read taken in a leap year. Documented in cal/cal.h (resolved note + MSM5832_D10_UNUSED), cal/write_calendar.c and time/read_cal.c; cal/test/test_write_calendar.c now asserts D10 bit 3 set and bit 2 clear. Ghidra EOL comments at 0x00E816D6, 0x00E816EA, 0x00E2AE78, 0x00E2AEC8 and a decompiler comment at 0x00E8167C.

title: aote+0x20 vs the 48-bit length at aote+0x28
description:
SETTLED: aote+0x20 is the object's current LENGTH IN BYTES (32-bit), and there is no 48-bit length in the AOTE at all -- the pair at 0x28/0x2C that this bead called a 48-bit length is a 48-bit CLOCK (see source-xk18).

Complete reader/writer set, from disassembling all 1871 functions and keeping every (0x20,An) in a function that also touches the AOTE-only offsets 0x9C/0xB9/0xBF:
  writers  0x00E02AB6 ast_$setup_page_read (len := last_page_byte_offset + 0x400)
           0x00E02EBE ast_$read_area_pages_network (same idiom, test at 0x00E02E9A)
           0x00E04918 AST_$GET_ATTRIBUTES (max(cached, record+0x14))
           0x00E06098 AST_$TRUNCATE (len := the new-length argument)
  readers  0x00E03258/5E AST_$TOUCH, 0x00E05A78 AST_$PURIFY,
           0x00E066C0/C6/DE AST_$INVALIDATE, 0x00E06BF4 AST_$GET_SEG_MAP,
           0x00E13074/8E/94 pmap_$write_page,
           ast_$get_common_attributes 0x00E04A30 (as record+0x14 -> common+0x04).
  NOT this field: AST_$SET_ATTR_DISPATCH 0x00E04E78/0x00E04FAA are attribute-record+0x20 (owner1_ext); PMAP_$PURIFIER_L 0x00E13EB4/0x00E13F1E walk a 0x24-byte record.

Unit: BYTES over 1KB pages everywhere -- every reader either does (len-1)>>10 to get a page index or compares against page_index*0x400.  Not pages, not segments, not blocks.  It is not a monotone high-water mark either: AST_$TRUNCATE lowers it.  The max() at 0x00E048F0 is narrower than that -- it only keeps a refresh from pulling the length back below what the local pager already grew, which is why the field looked monotone.

Written up on aote_t.length in ast/ast.h (renamed from unknown_20); Ghidra comments at the addresses above; ast/test/test_aote_length_and_location.c pins the arithmetic.
close_reason: Closed

title: xns/idp_send.c does not use mac_os_$send_pkt_t
description: XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND (0x00E18256) builds the 0x4C-byte MAC send record at A6-0x88: frame type 0x600 at +0x30 (0x00E183FC), the three-longword header descriptor at +0x1C from the caller's record+0x18 (0x00E18408-0x00E18414), hdr_prebuilt at +0x28 from record+0x24 (0x00E18416), and data_length plus all four payload pages at +0x38 in one five-longword loop from record+0x34 (0x00E1841C-0x00E18428); MAC_OS_$ARP gets it as its third argument with the broadcast flag at +0x18 (0x00E183C0-0x00E183CC).  xns/idp_send.c instead invents a local anonymous struct 'mac_send_params' with fields ethertype/header_len/header_ptr/iov/flags/extra[0x14] that does not lay out to any of that, and passes 'mac_info' (a different object) to MAC_OS_$SEND.  Re-emit XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND against the assembly and build a mac_os_$send_pkt_t (mac_os/mac_os.h).
close_reason: Re-emitted XNS_IDP_$OS_SEND and XNS_IDP_$SEND (xns/idp_send.c) against 0x00E18256 and 0x00E18A66, tracing every basic block. The MAC record is now mac_os_$send_pkt_t built at A6-0x88: frame_type 0x600 at +0x30 (0x00E183FC), hdr_desc at +0x1C from rec+0x18 (0x00E18408-0x00E18414), hdr_prebuilt at +0x28 from rec+0x24 (0x00E18416), data_length plus all four pages at +0x38 from rec+0x34 in the five-longword loop (0x00E1841C-0x00E18428); MAC_OS_$ARP gets &record.link_addr and &record.is_broadcast (0x00E183C0/0x00E183C4). Other defects fixed in the same pass: the checksum test was inverted (0x00E1842E 'cmpi.w #-1,(A3) / beq' skips the computation); MAC_OS_$SEND's first argument is &state->ports[port].mac_socket, not ROUTE_$PORTP[port]+0x48 (0x00E18474 'pea (0x48,A5,D1)' with D1 = port*12); the third argument is the length MAC_OS_$SEND reports, not a checksum (0x00E18268 / 0x00E18460); the connect and build-header flags are word bits 13 and 11, not 0x20/0x08, because 0x00E182A4/0x00E182AC btst the high byte of the flags word; RIP_$FIND_NEXTHOP's boolean is pushed by value with 'st' (0x00E1837C). XNS_ERROR_$SEND's static record at 0x00E2B29C is now the same xns_$os_send_rec_t. 29 new tests in xns/test/test_idp_send.c call the real functions.

title: ring_$swdiag_t is 0x1E bytes, not 0x18: add rcvhcsum at +0x18
description:
ring/ring.h declares ring_$swdiag_t as 0x18 bytes (_r00.._r04 plus ten receive words ending at rcvxerr +0x16).  NETWORK_$PROCESS_PAGING_REQUEST case 0x0E copies 0x1E bytes out of it -- "movea.l #0xe261c2,A1 / lea (-0x18e,A0),A4 / moveq #0x6 / move.l (A1)+,(A4)+ / dbf / move.w (A1)+,(A4)+" at 0x00E11278..0x00E1128A, i.e. 0x00E261C2..0x00E261DF, which runs up to but not into RING_$STATS[0] at 0x00E261E0.  So the block is 0x1E bytes.

+0x18 is rcvhcsum: every swdiag mirror sits a uniform 0x1A below its ring_$stats_t counter and rcvhcsum is stats+0x32; /etc/netmain's software-diagnostic display prints "rcvxerr <n>  rcvhcsum <n>" as its own line.  +0x1A..0x1D is a longword slot the responder immediately overwrites from RING_$SWDIAG_NODEID (0x00E261AC, 0x00E11294), and +0x02..0x05 is likewise overwritten from RING_$SWDIAG_RCVCNT (0x00E261B4, 0x00E1128C) -- so the two live values are held in the standalone globals and those two slots in the block are stale.

Extend ring_$swdiag_t to 0x1E with rcvhcsum at +0x18 and two unnamed bytes... a word pair at +0x1A, and add a sizeof static assert.  ring_info_t in network/network.h already models the copy field by field (bead source-4omb).
close_reason: Closed

title: mac_os_$send_pkt_t bytes 0x08..0x17: the 24-byte block MAC_$SEND copies whole
description:
SETTLED (2026-09-07).  mac_os_$send_pkt_t bytes 0x00..0x17 are ONE variable-length link-address record: a word count followed by up to 11 address words (24 bytes).  mac_os/mac_os.h now models it as mac_os_$link_addr_t {uint16_t n_words; uint16_t addr[11];} and mac_os_$rcv_pkt_t's head is the same record (the old net_type/src_id/_r06 names are kept as a union arm so ring/receive_packet.c still builds).

Shape - two count-driven copy loops:
  MAC_$DEMUX   0x00E0BC82 move.w (A2),(-0x2e,A6); 0x00E0BC86 move.w (A2),D0w/subq.w #1/bmi; 0x00E0BC90 move.w (0x2,A1),(-0x2c,A0)/addq #2/addq #2/dbf
  MAC_$RECEIVE 0x00E0BE52 the same loop the other way; 0x00E0BE60 move.w (-0x2c,A0),(0x2,A1)
Neither loop bounds the count, so a count above 11 overruns the record - original behaviour.

Extent = 24 bytes => 11 words:
  - driver record: the next field is the boolean at +0x18 (0x00E0BC68 tst.b (0x18,A2); 0x00E0BE4E move.b D1b,(0x18,A3)), and MAC_$SEND moves 0x00..0x17 as one record assignment (0x00E0BBC2 moveq #0x5 + move.l (A0)+,(A1)+/dbf) before filling +0x18/+0x1C/+0x28/+0x30/+0x38/+0x3C field by field at 0x00E0BBCE..0x00E0BBF0
  - MAC_$DEMUX staging record: count at A6-0x2E, words from A6-0x2C, next field written is the word at A6-0x16 (0x00E0BCBC) => 0x16 bytes = 11 words

Counts stored anywhere in this image:
  2  MAC_OS_$ARP net_type 0 and 3 - the 20-bit Apollo ring node id, (ip>>16)&0x000F and ip&0xFFFF (0x00E0C1A4..0x00E0C1B2); broadcast arm writes the count alone (0x00E0C14E)
  3  MAC_OS_$ARP net_type 4 and 5 - a 6-byte IEEE 802 address copied from the caller record (0x00E0C1FC..0x00E0C210) or FF-FF-FF-FF-FF-FF for broadcast (0x00E0C156..0x00E0C164)
  2  ring_$receive_packet - 0x00E76528 move.w #0x2,(-0x50,A6) then the two words of the source node id at 0x00E7652E..0x00E7653E
Only length check in the image: RING_$SEND_OS refuses anything but 2 (0x00E77D7E cmpi.w #0x2 -> status 0x00310012), then copies two words from +0x02 (0x00E77D86..0x00E77D96).

NOT established (and not claimed in the header): what the remaining eight words are for.  The 802.5-routing-information-field motivation is unattested here - no token-ring or ethernet driver exists in this image (ETHERNET_$INIT 0x00E78004 is a stub returning status_$io_controller_not_in_system, and there is no 802/TR/FDDI namespace), and the SR10.4 user-space /sys/ins tree ships no mac.ins.pas naming the record.

Also recovered: mac_os_$rcv_pkt_t and mac_os_$send_pkt_t are the SAME Pascal record - link address 0x00..0x17, boolean 0x18, buffer chain 0x1C, frame type 0x30, payload length 0x38, payload pages 0x3C.  RING_$SEND_OS's loopback path relies on that, copying the caller's send record whole into the DEMUX receive record (0x00E77E76 moveq #0x12 + move.l (A1)+,(A4)+/dbf = 0x4C bytes).
close_reason: Closed

title: CRASH_SYSTEM status constants should be per-module pea(d,PC) cells, not shared globals
description: misc/crash_system.c defines ~22 'status_$t X = 0x...;' globals (Lock_ordering_violation, MMAP_*, Disk_*, ...) that ~70 .c files take the address of and hand to CRASH_SYSTEM.  In the image no such globals exist: every caller does 'pea (d,PC)' to a constant longword inside its own module (see the domain-pascal-codegen-conventions note).  Each constant should become a file-static 'static const status_$t <name>_00eXXXXX = 0x...;' next to its single caller, with the cell address in a comment, and misc/crash_system.h should stop exporting them.  Two entries were only ever inferred rather than read out of the image (Lock_ordering_violation = 0x000A0001 used by ml/lock.c; Disk_Driver_Logic_Err, a duplicate of Disk_driver_logic_err used by disk/dismount.c which also declares it as 'void *').  Lock_order_violation_err was invented and unused and has already been removed.
close_reason: All 22 invented status_$t globals removed from misc/crash_system.c and misc/crash_system.h (and the commented-out block in misc/misc.h, plus the dead externs in ml/ml_internal.h, mst/mst_internal.h, mmap/mmap_internal.h, proc1/proc1_internal.h, ast/ast.h, os/os_internal.h). Every CRASH_SYSTEM call site now has a file-static 'static const status_$t <name>_00eXXXXX' with the cell address in the name; names come from the SR10.4 database (~/src/domainos-archeology/stcodes). 19 distinct cells recovered from the pea (d,PC) at each call: 0x00E20DE4=0x000A0002 proc1_$illegal_lock (ml, shared tail 0x00E20B56); 0x00E30B0C=0x0004000E (mst/init); 0x00E0E1B8=0x00040005 (mst/find); 0x00E3C9FA=0x0008002E (disk/add_que); 0x00E6D130=0x00080022 (disk/dismount); 0x00E1940C=0x00080004 and 0x00E19410=0x00080022 (win); 0x00E0D1C4=0x0006000A, 0x00E0C9E0=0x00060009, 0x00E0D270=0x0006000B, 0x00E0CFF4=0x00060008, 0x00E0CD18=0x00060006, 0x00E0CCB8=0x00060004, 0x00E0D9E6=0x0006000D, 0x00E31B80=0x00060007 (mmap); 0x00E152E0=0x000A0001 (proc1); 0x00E01F18=0x80030003, 0x00E00EAC=0x00050003, 0x00E03544=0x0006000C (ast). The two never-read entries are now read: Lock_ordering_violation was NOT a separate 0x000A0001 -- ML_$LOCK's ordering test (bls.b 0x00E20B56 at 0x00E20AF8) and ML_$UNLOCK's not-locked test (beq.b 0x00E20B56 at 0x00E20BA4) branch into the SAME crash tail, so both use 0x00E20DE4 = 0x000A0002 'illegal lock'; and Disk_Driver_Logic_Err is a genuinely distinct cell at 0x00E6D130 in the disk module (0x00080022), separate from win's 0x00E19410 of the same value. proc1's cell is 0x00E152E0, not the mmap cell the old file claimed. The stale 'void *' / array-typed declarations and the test-local definitions in ml/test/test_exclusion.c and disk/test/test_io.c are gone. All 19 cells labelled in Ghidra, with an EOL comment on the shared ML tail at 0x00E20B56.

title: smd/sau2/start_blt.s trampoline lea cannot reproduce its displacement until SMD_$DISP1_INT is emitted
description: SMD_$START_BLT's entry trampoline is 'lea (-0x39e,PC),A0' at 0x00E272BC, i.e. A0 = 0x00E272BE - 0x39E = 0x00E26F20 = SMD_$DISP1_INT, followed by 'jmp 0x00e15d1e.l'.  SMD_$DISP1_INT is not emitted anywhere yet, so smd/sau2/start_blt.s loads the body label instead and the two-byte displacement differs from the original (everything else, including the whole 108-byte body, is byte for byte identical - verified with m68k-elf-objdump).  A0 is dead (0x00E15D22 overwrites it with the first argument before any use), so this is cosmetic, but once SMD_$DISP1_INT exists as a symbol the lea should name it.  A TODO marks the spot.

title: rip: RIP_$SERVER's two original defects on the Domain-internet / name-register paths
description:
Both found while re-emitting the dispatch arms for source-4nvz (rip/server.c); both are preserved in the C with TODO comments.

1. RIP_$SERVER's frame slot A6-0x4F0 (payload_va) is written ONLY at 0x00E68A5A, inside the 'tst.b D3b / bpl 0x00E68A8E' XNS arm.  On the Domain-internet path (the RIP_$PROCESS_REQUEST(false) call at 0x00E68C2C) the nested procedure still loads it - 'movea.l (-0x4f0,A0),A1' at 0x00E688F6 - and reads the requested networks through it, so an internet-borne RIP request with entry_count > 0 dereferences whatever the previous stack frame left there.  PKT_$BRK_INTERNET_HDR copies the payload to A6-0x4D0 instead, which is where the response arm reads it from (0x00E68DAC), so the intended pointer was almost certainly &(-0x4d0,A6).

2. The name-register arm's node-id extraction at 0x00E68DE0-0x00E68DEE does 'lea (-0xa,A6),A2' (the IDP SOURCE HOST, header+0x16) then 'and.l (0x6,A2),D1'.  The +6 accessor belongs to the 10-byte { network:4, host_hi:2, host_lo:4 } record (rip_$nexthop_t), so it should have been applied to the record base at header+0x12, not to the host field.  As written it masks src_socket (header+0x1C) plus the two frame bytes between the 30-byte header copy and A6 - neither of which the copy at 0x00E68A62 ever writes.

No fix is possible without changing behaviour; these are notes for anyone reading rip/server.c.

title: sau2.ld: 8 remaining R_68K_PC16 overflows in ec/proc1/sio2681/smd
description:
Follow-up to source-a5t8, which fixed only the 11 SVC sites (sau2.ld now emits svc/sau2/trap*.o(.text) followed by .text.svc_tables; svc overflow count 11 -> 0).  8 R_68K_PC16 overflows remain, same root cause - the link script does not reproduce the image's code/data adjacency:

  ec (2)       build/sau2/ec/sau2/advance.o(.text+0xe), advance_all.o(.text+0xe)
               -> PROC1_$DISPATCH_INT
  proc1 (3)    proc1/sau2/init_stack.o(.text+0x36) -> PROC1_$CURRENT (0xE2611E)
               proc1/sau2/int_handler.o(.text+0x6, +0x6c) -> ADVANCE_INT
  sio2681 (2)  sio2681/sau2/int_rte.o(.text+0xa, +0x1a) -> SIO2681_$PTRS (+0, +10)
  smd (1)      smd/sau2/disp1_int.o(.text+0x10) -> SMD_DISPLAY_INFO

Recipe (see the SVC_CATCHER block comment in domain_os/sau2.ld): give each
image-adjacent table a dedicated section at its definition site and name that
section in sau2.ld immediately after the code that reaches it PC-relative.
svc uses SVC_TABLE_SECTION (svc/svc_internal.h) -> .text.svc_tables.  Where the
target is a Pascal module data block pinned at an A5 address, prefer
source-0i3's .moddata.<name> scheme instead.  Note GNU ld prints at most 10
relocation overflows tree-wide, so re-check the count after each subsystem.

Owners: ec, proc1, sio2681, smd (sau2.ld itself is shared).
TODO in domain_os/sau2.ld cites source-a5t8; retarget it to this bead.
close_reason:
All 8 R_68K_PC16 overflows resolved; 'make' now links with zero relocation truncations.

Every one of the 8 sites was confirmed genuinely PC-relative in the image (gsk read), so no .s instruction byte was changed:
  0xE206F8 61 00 03 26 bsr.w  -> 0xE20A20 PROC1_$DISPATCH_INT   (ec/sau2/advance.s)
  0xE2070E 61 00 03 10 bsr.w  -> 0xE20A20 PROC1_$DISPATCH_INT   (ec/sau2/advance_all.s)
  0xE208FA 61 00 fe 30 bsr.w  -> 0xE2072C ADVANCE_INT            (proc1/sau2/int_handler.s)
  0xE20960 61 00 fd ca bsr.w  -> 0xE2072C ADVANCE_INT            (proc1/sau2/int_handler.s)
  0xE20AD8 3f 3a fb 2e move.w (-0x4d2,PC) -> 0xE20608 PROC1_$CURRENT (proc1/sau2/init_stack.s)
  0xE2DFA8 41 fa ff d6 lea    (-0x2a,PC)  -> 0xE2DF80 SIO2681_$PTRS
  0xE2DFB8 41 fa ff d6 lea    (-0x2a,PC)  -> 0xE2DF90 SIO2681_$PTRS+0x10
  0xE26F2E 43 fa 04 46 lea    (0x446,PC)  -> 0xE27376 SMD_$DISPLAY_COM (SMD_DISPLAY_INFO)

None of the three data cells is a Pascal A5 module block: the SAU2 map places all three INSIDE a code segment (PROC1_$CURRENT 0xE20608 in PROC1_ASM 0xE1EAC8+0x24A4; SIO2681_$PTRS 0xE2DF80 opens SIO_INT 0x8C; SMD_$DISPLAY_COM 0xE27376 closes SMD_WIRED 0xE26F20+0x5E0).  So they take source-a5t8's '.text.<name>' technique and do NOT pre-empt source-0i3's '.moddata.<name>' scheme; each header says so.

  proc1/proc1_internal.h  PROC1_ASM_DATA_SECTION  -> .text.proc1_asm_data
  sio2681/sio2681_internal.h SIO2681_PTRS_SECTION -> .text.sio2681_ptrs
  smd/smd_internal.h      SMD_DISPLAY_INFO_SECTION -> .text.smd_display_info

sau2.ld now emits three image-ordered runs ahead of the '*(.text .text.*)' gather: .text.proc1_asm_data + */ec/*.o + */proc1/*.o; .text.sio2681_ptrs + int_rte.o; and the SMD_WIRED run disp1_int/cursor_thunks/blink_cursor_1/interrupt_init/scroll/start_blt + .text.smd_display_info.  Whole subsystems (ec, proc1) and the whole SMD_WIRED run are listed rather than the referencing objects alone: an intermediate attempt that pulled only smd/sau2/disp1_int.o out of the gather stranded SMD_$XOR_CURSOR/$OR_CURSOR/$START_SCROLL/$CONTINUE_SCROLL/$START_BLT, whose own 'lea (SMD_$DISP1_INT:w,PC),A0' then overflowed (5 new errors).

Link map spot check: SIO2681_$PTRS 0xE03464 -> SIO2681_$INT1_RTE 0xE03484 reproduces the image's 0x20 gap exactly.

Gates: make clean && make -k -j8 -> no error:/warning: lines, 0 relocation truncations; make test -> 175 tests, 0 failed; duplicate-global scan unchanged from baseline (9 pre-existing file/ and static-local names, none of them touched here).

Byte-fidelity drift found but not fixed here (out of scope, filed as source-p49c): ec/sau2/advance.s and advance_without_dispatch.s use bsr.w where the image has the 2-byte bsr.b (0x61 0x34 at 0xE206F6, 0x61 0x08 at 0xE20722).

title: proc1: TIMESLICE_TABLE is the map's PROC1_$TSVV (0xE205D2) and must live in the PROC1_ASM code segment
description:
SAU2 map domain_os.10.2.map, PROC1_ASM:

     E205D2  PROC1_$TSVV
     E205F6  PROC1_$SUSPEND_EC

so the object is 0xE205D2..0xE205F5, 0x24 bytes = 18 word entries - exactly
the 0x12 bound ADVANCE_INT enforces with 'cmp.l #0x11,%d0' at 0xE20766.

ADVANCE_INT reaches it PC-relatively:

    0xE2078C  41 fa fe 44   lea (-0x1bc,%pc),%a0     -> 0xE205D2
    0xE20790  3f 30 00 fe   move.w (-2,%a0,%d0.w),-(%sp)

i.e. a 1-based word table indexed by the newly computed priority, whose entry
is passed as PROC1_$SET_TS's second argument.

The tree carries this cell as proc1/proc1_data.c's

    int16_t TIMESLICE_TABLE[PROC1_MAX_STATES] = { 0 };   /* 0xE205D2 */

which (a) is not the map's name and (b) lands in .bss, ~0x11000 bytes from the
lea, so an R_68K_PC16 to it would be truncated.  ec/sau2/advance_int.s
therefore writes 'lea (PROC1_$TSVV:w,%pc),%a0' and the link reports one
undefined reference to PROC1_$TSVV.

Fix (proc1-owned): rename TIMESLICE_TABLE to PROC1_$TSVV, give it
PROC1_ASM_DATA_SECTION (proc1/proc1_internal.h) so sau2.ld's
'*(.text.proc1_asm_data)' picks it up at the head of the PROC1_ASM run, and
_Static_assert its size at 0x24.  Ghidra already has the label
(gsk label add 0x00E205D2 'PROC1_$TSVV').

TODO cited in ec/sau2/advance_int.s.
close_reason: Fixed in wave 17 (commit after 517acdc): RING_$DATA public in ring/ring.h and used by asknode; PROC1_$TSVV renamed, sized 18, placed in .text.proc1_asm_data; disp1_int.s jsr ADVANCE

title: Emit smd_$init_display_state (0x00E6F514) - declared but has no .c
description:
smd/smd_internal.h declares smd_$init_display_state(int8_t options, status_$t *status_ret) for 0x00E6F514 and two call sites use it (SMD_$INIT_STATE 0x00E6F818 and SMD_$BORROW_DISPLAY 0x00E6F69C), but no smd/init_display_state.c exists, so the symbol is unresolved at link time.

Runs on the caller's A5.

title: DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK packed flags param does not match assembly
description: dxm/add_callback.c models the 4th/5th Pascal parameters as one packed uint32 'flags'. The binary (0x00E16FF6 move.w (0x14,A6),D4w; 0x00E16FFA move.b (0x16,A6),D2b) has a word data_size and a separate byte boolean check_dup. Splitting the C signature touches callers in kbd/rcv.c, tty/i_signal.c, ast/save_clobbered_uid.c and suma/rcv.c. Referenced by TODO in dxm/add_signal.c.
close_reason: Split DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK's 4th/5th Pascal parameters into a uint16_t data_size (0x00E16FF6 move.w (0x14,A6),D4w) and a boolean check_dup (0x00E16FFA move.b (0x16,A6),D2b), verified against all six call sites (each cleans up 20 bytes = 4+4+4+2+2+4). Fixed the pushes in kbd/rcv.c (4,true @0x00E1CDF2/F4), tty/i_signal.c (12,true @0x00E1B872/74), ast/save_clobbered_uid.c (8,true @0x00E07248/4A), suma/rcv.c (4,true @0x00E1AE7E/80) and dxm/add_signal.c (10,check_dup @0x00E172A2/A6); all four had been decoding the old packed longword incorrectly in both fields. Also turned the two pea (d,PC) cells into file-statics (0x00E17164 = status 0x00170002 'datum too large for deferred execution', previously mismodelled as a string; 0x00E17154 = the crash string '(DXM) No room%'), fixed the scan-vs-insert index scaling (lsl.l at 0x00E17060 vs lsl.w at 0x00E17102), and added dxm/test/test_add_callback.c (10 cases, includes the real .c). Ghidra: prototype set on 0x00E16FE0, label DXM_No_room_msg at 0x00E17154, 0x00E17164 typed dword, EOL comments at the parameter reads and both pea sites.
