title: pkt_$data_t initialisers disagree with the 0x00E24C9C image
description: gsk read 0x00E24CF0 shows the loaded image: visibility_seq(0x54)=1, n_missing(0x58)=0, ping_req_hdr(0x5A)=1, short_id(0x5C)=0, long_id(0x60)=0, default_flags(0x64)=0, and PKT_$PING_TEMPLATE (0x68) = 0x0010 0x0002 0x0002 0x8031 0xFFFF 0x0000 0xFFFF 0x0000.  pkt/pkt_data.c's host initialisers say short_id=1, long_id=1, visibility_seq=0 and a ping_template of {type=2,length=0,...}.  Note the template's retry-count word at +8 is 0xFFFF, which PKT_$SEND_INTERNET's 'tst.w (0x8,A4) / ble' (0x00E126A0) treats as 'no limit', and pkt_$request_template_t.retry_count should therefore be int16_t.  Also: bytes 0x76-0x87 of pkt_$data_t are still unidentified (reserved_76).
close_reason: pkt/pkt_data.c's initialisers now match the image read with 'gsk read 0x00E24C9C 0x100': visibility_seq(0x54)=1, n_missing(0x58)=0, ping_req_hdr(0x5A)=1, short_id(0x5C)=0, long_id(0x60)=0, default_flags(0x64)=0 (they said short_id=1, long_id=1, visibility_seq=0). The 0x76-0x87 'reserved_76' hole is identified: 0x68 and 0x88 hold TWO copies of one 0x20-byte record, byte-identical apart from their first word (0x0010 vs 0x0020), and both are pushed as PKT_$SEND_INTERNET's pkt_info argument - 0x00E12AA0 'pea (0x68,A5)' from PKT_$LIKELY_TO_ANSWER and 0x00E12D0A 'pea (0x88,A5)' from PKT_$PING_SERVER. The record is now pkt_$info_t in pkt/pkt.h, recovered from PKT_$BLD_INTERNET_HDR (its only full reader): +0x00 flags (byte at +0x01 read at 0x00E1206A/0x00E12298, word written at 0x00E12CE6), +0x02 routing_type (0x00E1208E 'cmpi.w #0x2', 0x00E12262 'cmpi.w #0x1'), +0x04 addr_type (0x00E1221E), +0x06 protocol=0x8031 (0x00E12230), +0x08 retry_limit, +0x0A field_0a, +0x0C field_0c (0x00E121A0), +0x0E addr[16] (copied at 0x00E12248-0x00E12256). pkt_$data_t is therefore 0xA8 bytes with _Static_asserts on every offset. Correction to the bead text: 0x00E126A0 is 'tst.w (0x8,A4) / bne', not 'ble' - 0 means 'take the builder's hint', and the image's 0xFFFF also ends up taking the hint via the 'cmpi.w #-0x1,D4w' at 0x00E1271E, so retry_limit stays unsigned. Tests: pkt/test/test_pkt_data.c, 4 tests, 0 failed.

title: dxm_entry_t is 24 bytes on the host build, 16 in the image
description: dxm/dxm.h models dxm_entry_t.callback as a native function pointer, so on a 64-bit host the record is 24 bytes and data moves from +0x04 to +0x08.  The image entry is 16 bytes (DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK scales indices with lsl #4 at 0x00E17060 and 0x00E17102, DXM_$SCAN_QUEUE at 0x00E17176), so the _Static_asserts in dxm/dxm.h are ARCH_M68K-only and dxm/test/test_add_callback.c has to lay its entry array out with an explicit 16-byte stride.  Fixing it means making the field a 4-byte cell (m68k_ptr_t) everywhere and unifying the callback cells, which are currently modelled three different ways: m68k_ptr_t in tty/tty_internal.h, void* in term/term.h and ast/ast_internal.h, and a function pointer in suma/suma_internal.h and dxm/dxm_internal.h.  Referenced by a TODO in dxm/dxm.h.
close_reason: dxm_entry_t is now 16 bytes on every target and its _Static_asserts are unconditional. dxm/dxm.h gained dxm_$callback_t (= m68k_ptr_t, the 4-byte code address the image stores at entry+0x00, proved by lsl.l #0x4,D0 at 0x00E17060, lsl.w #0x4,D1w at 0x00E17102 and lsl.w #4,D0w at 0x00E17176), plus dxm_$callback_fn_t, DXM_$CALLBACK_CELL, dxm_$callback_fn and DXM_$DEFINE_CALLBACK_CELL. On m68k those are plain casts; on a 64-bit host DXM_$DEFINE_CALLBACK_CELL registers the function in a table in dxm/dxm_data.c through a constructor (a truncated function address is not a constant expression, confirmed: 'initializer element is not a compile-time constant') and dxm_$callback_fn maps a cell back to a callable pointer. All five cells unified on that type: PTR_TTY_$I_DXM_SIGNAL (tty/tty_internal.h + tty_data.c), PTR_TERM_$ENQUEUE_TPAD_00e1ce90 (term/term.h + term_data.c), PTR_AST_$SET_TROUBLE_00e07272 (ast/ast_internal.h), PTR_TERM_$ENQUEUE_TPAD_00e1aecc (suma/suma_internal.h), PTR_DXM_$ADD_SIGNAL_CALLBACK (dxm/dxm_internal.h + dxm_data.c); tty/term/ast gained the dxm/dxm.h include, and the two stale (void **) casts on the callback argument (dxm/add_signal.c, suma/rcv.c) were dropped. DXM_$ADD_CALLBACK's callback parameter is now const dxm_$callback_t *; add_callback.c and scan_queue.c updated. dxm/test/test_add_callback.c dropped its explicit 16-byte-stride byte block and its two slots of slack for a plain dxm_entry_t[8], and uses literal code addresses for the callbacks (the function only compares and stores the cell). New dxm/test/test_scan_queue.c #includes dxm/dxm_data.c and dxm/scan_queue.c and drives the real DXM_$SCAN_QUEUE: 5 tests covering the 16-byte record, the host registry round trip, the empty queue, draining in head order with the head advanced and the lock dropped before each callback, and the masked head wrap. Ghidra: disassembly comments at 0x00E17060 and 0x00E17176. Follow-up source-f4qo filed for the two cells that still have no definition anywhere.

title: disk_io_req_t declares its chain links as host pointers, so its host layout diverges from the target past +0x04
description: disk/disk_internal.h declares disk_io_req_t.next (0x00) and .free_next (0x08) as 'struct disk_io_req_t *'.  On m68k that is exact; on a 64-bit host build (make test) both grow to 8 bytes, so daddr (0x04), status (0x0c), ppn (0x14), flags (0x1c), owner (0x1e), op_flags (0x1f) and header[] (0x20) all slide.  The _Static_asserts that would catch it are guarded by #if defined(ARCH_M68K), so the host build never checks.  Nothing is broken today because disk/io.c and disk/test/test_io.c use the struct fields consistently, but any test that mixes a struct field with a raw DISK_QBLK_* byte offset silently disagrees -- test_get_qblks_internal.c hit exactly that while covering source-jr1c.  Fix by holding the two links as uint32_t VA cells (as disk_$get_qblks_internal and disk_$rtn_qblks_internal already do for DMOD_FREE_HEAD / DISK_QBLK_FREE_NEXT) and converting with ARCH_VA_TO_PTR, then dropping the ARCH_M68K guard on the asserts.  Record at 0x00E3BE8A / DISK_IO 0x00E3D50E.

title: AST_$GET_ATTRIBUTES arg1 is a 0x20-byte location record, not a uid_t
description: 0x00E047D2 reads the caller's UID from +0x08 of a 0x20-byte object-location record and 0x00E0492C overwrites all 32 bytes from aote+0x9C. The four callers named in the bead were re-derived from their own frames: file/get_attributes.c (0x00E5D984, size check moved after the dispatch per 0x00E5D9F2, 0x20-byte writeback at 0x00E5DA30), file/get_attr_info.c (0x00E5D7F4, new 0x7A-byte file_$attr_info_t recovered store by store from 0x00E5D8B0-0x00E5D978, writeback at 0x00E5D88E), file/attributes.c (0x00E5DA4C) and file/act_attributes.c (0x00E5DAB0) - the last two also stopped passing NULL for VTOCE_$NEW_TO_OLD's boolean, which is the constant 0xFF cell at 0xE5DAAE (pea (0x18,PC) at 0x00E5DA94, pea (-0x4c,PC) at 0x00E5DAF8).  The request word is now read as a word, not as byte[1], because 'btst.b #n,(0x1,A0)' addresses a big-endian word's LOW byte.  file/priv_create.c passed &parent_loc.uid where 0x00E5D3F8 pea's the record base.  Casts removed at the other twelve call sites in ast/, file/, dir/, log/ and rem_file/, and dir/do_op_dir_readu.c's 60-byte attribute buffer widened to 0x90 (0x00E5DA20 always writes 36 longwords). title: ring/sendp.c: result flags accessed through a byte view (19 sites); model as word masks
description: uint8_t *result_bytes = (uint8_t *)result_flags; result_bytes[1] |= 0x10 etc. are correct only on big-endian. Rewrite every site as *result_flags word ops (bset.b #n on the odd byte = bit n of the word).
close_reason: All 19 byte-view sites in ring/sendp.c are now word masks with named constants (RING_SENDP_RES_*). The rule is stated once in the file header: 'bset.b #n,(A3)' addresses the EVEN byte of the word at (A3), which on m68k is the high half, so it is bit n+8; 'bset.b #n,(0x1,A3)' is bit n. Concretely 0xE75960/0xE759A0 #4,(0x1,A3)=0x0010, 0xE75BF4 #3,(A3)=0x0800, 0xE75C3E/0xE75D2E #7,(A3)=0x8000, 0xE75C6A #5,(0x1,A3)=0x0020, 0xE75C7C #2,(0x1,A3)=0x0004, 0xE75CC4 #7,(0x1,A3)=0x0080, 0xE75CD8 #0,(A3)=0x0100, 0xE75CEC #2,(A3)=0x0400, 0xE75CFC/0xE75D1C/0xE75D8A #6,(0x1,A3)=0x0040, 0xE75D3A #6,(A3)=0x4000, 0xE75D52 #5,(A3)=0x2000, 0xE75DCA #1,(A3)=0x0200, and 0xE75958 'clr.w (A3)' clears the whole word. The uint8_t* alias is gone, so the file is host-endian-clean; ring/test/test_sendp.c asserts on the word values (e.g. overrun is 0x0100, not 0x0001).

title: acl/free_asid.c: verify the ASID vs PID index base for the per-process ACL tables
description: ACL_$FREE_ASID (0x00E74C6A) indexes ACL_$CURRENT_SIDS / ACL_$ORIGINAL_SIDS / ACL_$SAVED_SIDS with asid*0x24 and ACL_$PROJ_UIDS with asid*0x40, but the two bitmaps with (asid-1)>>3.  acl_$eval_rights and ACL_$RIGHTS use PROC1_$CURRENT for the same tables with the same 1-based bitmap arithmetic, so ASID and PID appear to be the same number here.  Confirm from ACL_$ALLOC_ASID (0x00E73BB8) and PROC1_$SET_ASID, and note it in acl/acl_internal.h.
close_reason: Confirmed: ASID and PID are the same number for every ACL per-process table, and the note is now in acl/acl_internal.h next to the bitmap macros.  Proof is ACL_$ALLOC_ASID (0x00E73BB8), which copies row PROC1_$CURRENT (the word at 0xE20608) into row new_asid (its A6+0x08 word) using identical bases, biases and strides for all six arrays off 0xE97294 - -0x6E84/0x24 ORIGINAL_SIDS, -0x6584/0x24 CURRENT_SIDS, -0x5C84/0x24 SAVED_SIDS (0x00E73BCC-0x00E73C1E), -0x4D98/0x40 PROJ_UIDS (0x00E73C22-0x00E73C4E), -0x536C/0x0C SAVED_PROJ and -0x506C/0x0C PROJ_LISTS (0x00E73C52-0x00E73C98) - and then applies the same (n-1)>>3 / 7-((n-1)&7) bitmap arithmetic to PROC1_$CURRENT's low byte against ACL_$ASID_FREE_BITMAP at -0x4D60 (0x00E73C9A-0x00E73CBA).  ACL_$FREE_ASID (0x00E74C6A) uses exactly those bases with its asid argument (0x00E74C7C-0x00E74D1E).  If the two were separate numbering spaces the row ALLOC_ASID writes would never be the row acl_$eval_rights and ACL_$RIGHTS read, so acl/free_asid.c's mixed asid*0x24 / (asid-1)>>3 indexing is correct as it stands.  0xE20608 (PROC1_$CURRENT) and 0xE2060A (PROC1_$AS_ID) remain distinct cells; only the ACL tables treat their contents interchangeably.

title: SMD_$START_BLT is hand-written assembly; move to smd/sau2/
description: SMD_$START_BLT's implementation at 0x00E15D1E has the same shape as SMD_$LOCK_DISPLAY: no link/unlk, a movem thunk, arguments read straight off the stack at (0x8,SP)/(0xc,SP)/(0x10,SP), register-passed dispatch base in A0, and a trampoline at 0x00E272BC (lea (-0x39e,PC),A0 / jmp).  Per CLAUDE.md it belongs in smd/sau2/start_blt.s with a portable C model under !ARCH_M68K, the way smd/sau2/lock_display.s and smd/sau2/bit_set.s were done under source-c3ap.  smd/start_blt.c is still plain C.
close_reason: Transcribed to smd/sau2/start_blt.s.  Confirmed hand-written: the entry at 0x00E272BC is 'lea (-0x39e,PC),A0' + 'jmp 0x00e15d1e.l', and the body at 0x00E15D1E has no link/unlk, saves exactly one register with 'movem.l {A2},-(SP)', reads its three arguments at (0x8,SP)/(0xc,SP)/(0x10,SP) with the movem push folded into the displacements by hand, and ends in a spin on a memory-mapped register ('tst.w (A1)' / 'bmi.b' at 0x00E15D80/0x00E15D82).  Behaviour: seven parameter words copied in the order 1,3,2,4,5,6,7 (0x00E15D2E-0x00E15D52); the control word is params[0] & 0xFFDE | hw->video_flags (0x00E15D58-0x00E15D5E); if bit 4 is set it presets hw->lock_state = 1, clears the whole word at hw+0x20 and copies hw->op_ec.value into hw->field_1c (0x00E15D68-0x00E15D72) and returns after starting the BLT, otherwise it spins.  Verified with m68k-elf-gcc -c + m68k-elf-objdump -d: the 108-byte body is byte for byte identical to 0x00E15D1E..0x00E15D89 - the one instruction GNU as would have normalised, 'and.w #-0x22,%d0' (0xC07C vs ANDI's 0x0240), is emitted with .short so nothing differs.  The trampoline keeps the original's shape and length (0x41FA + 0x4EF9, 10 bytes) but its lea displacement cannot be reproduced until SMD_$DISP1_INT (0x00E26F20) is emitted - filed as source-tzn8 with a TODO in the file; A0 is dead anyway, overwritten at 0x00E15D22.  smd/start_blt.c is kept as a portable model behind '#if !defined(ARCH_M68K)', the same convention as bit_set.c and lock_display.c.  Ghidra: decompiler comment at 0x00E15D1E.

title: file/check_prot.c and file/export_lk.c claim LOT_DATA_BASE 0xE935BC, which is the ACL locksmith-override bitmap
description: 0xE935BC is ACL_$LOCKSMITH_OVERRIDE_BITMAP (8 bytes, written by ACL_$OVERRIDE_LOCAL_LOCKSMITH at 0x00E492BC, read by acl_$eval_rights at 0x00E4657C and ACL_$SET_ACL_CHECK at 0x00E473A4) and 0xE935C4 is ACL_$ASID_SUSER_BITMAP (acl_$check_suser_pid 0x00E4648A).  FILE_$PRIV_LOCK_$ALLOC_ENTRY addresses the lock table through 'movea.l #0xe935cc,A2' with a 0x1C stride (0x00E5EBCA), i.e. the LOT starts at 0xE935CC, 0x10 bytes above the constant file/check_prot.c:44 and file/export_lk.c:37 use.  Recheck the per-entry field offsets in both files against 0x00E5EBB4-0x00E5EC0A.
close_reason: Fixed.  0xE935CC confirmed as the lock-object table base from three sites: FILE_$PRIV_LOCK_$ALLOC_ENTRY (movea.l #0xe935cc,A2 at 0x00E5EBCA, writing -0x1C..-0x01 off the entry END at 0x00E5EC06-0x00E5ECBE), FILE_$CHECK_PROT (0x00E5D1C8, UID at -0x10, rights byte at -0x2) and FILE_$EXPORT_LK (0x00E74186, refcount at -0x4, UID at -0x10).  Both files rewritten against file_lock_entry_detail_t and the existing FILE_$LOT_ENTRY / FILE_$PROC_LOT_SLOT / FILE_$PROC_LOT_COUNT accessors, which already carry the right layout; the bogus LOT_DATA_BASE 0xE935BC constants and the M68K_TARGET #ifdefs that made check_prot's whole cache path dead on the host are gone. title: aote_t 0x28/0x2C and 0x30/0x38/0x40 clock fields are misnamed (len_high/len_low)
description: ast/ast.h calls aote+0x28/0x2C 'len_high'/'len_low', but the pair is a 48-bit Apollo clock, not a length. The whole DT* run is therefore shifted by one slot: 0x28=DTM, 0x30=DTU, 0x38=DTV (AST_$GET_DTV reads it at 0x00E054F4), 0x40=DTA.  Renaming needs mmap/release_pages.c, mmap/internal.c, mmap/ws_scan.c, pmap/purifier_l.c and their tests changed in the same pass.  Found while settling source-traa (aote+0x20 is the only length in the AOTE).

title: fim: one image object, two definitions - FIM_CLEANUP_STACK vs fim.s cleanup_stack_table
description:
The cleanup-handler stack head table at 0x00E216B2 is defined twice:

  fim/fim_data.c   void *FIM_CLEANUP_STACK[PROC1_MAX_PROCESSES];   (C-visible symbol)
  fim/sau2/fim.s   cleanup_stack_table: .space 260, 0              (private label)

Both are now sized 65 * 4 = 260 bytes (source-zsgb derived the count from the extent 0x00E216B2..0x00E217B6 and from the three PROC1_$CURRENT*4 index sites at 0x00E21640 / 0x00E21668 / 0x00E21692), so they agree, but they are two objects for one image object: FIM_$CLEANUP, FIM_$RLS_CLEANUP and FIM_$SIGNAL in fim.s push and pop the .s copy while any C code that touched FIM_CLEANUP_STACK would see the other.

The .s reservation cannot simply be deleted: fim/sau2/fim.s deliberately keeps image spacing between FIM_$SIGNAL and FIM_$PROC2_STARTUP.  Options are to make the .s label the definition of the global (and drop it from fim_data.c, the way FIM_$TRACE_BIT was handled in source-refr), or to keep the C definition and have the three lea sites reach it as an .extern by absolute long.

Nothing in C references FIM_CLEANUP_STACK today, so this is latent, not a live bug.

The three lea sites use (FIM_$CLEANUP_STACK:w,%pc) so they keep the original 41fa 0070 / 0048 / 001e encodings; objdump -t shows every offset in fim.o unchanged and the 260 bytes assemble to zero, byte-identical to gsk read 0x00E216B2 260. title: rem_file/unlock.c request record layout does not match the 0x22-byte image
description: REM_FILE_$UNLOCK (0x00E61D1C) builds its request at A6-0x170 with: +0x00 msg_type word, +0x02 magic 0x80, +0x03 opcode 0x0C, +0x04 uid (8), +0x0C lock_key, +0x10 remote_node, +0x14 unlock_mode word, +0x18 flags word 3, +0x1A admin byte, +0x1C lock_seq word, +0x20 release byte; the length pushed to REM_FILE_$SEND_REQUEST is 0x22 (move.w #0x22,-(SP) at 0x00E61DB4). The C struct rem_file_unlock_req_t in rem_file/unlock.c lays flags at +0x16, admin at +0x18, wait_flag at +0x1A and release at +0x1C (sizeof 0x1E), so every field from +0x16 on goes out in the wrong place. Also the response is read via a pointer computed as &response[BUFSZ - sizeof(resp_t)] which has no basis in the assembly (0x00E61DC8 reads (-0x17c,A6) and the callee writes into (-0xc0,A6)). Needs REM_FILE_$UNLOCK re-emitted from 0x00E61D1C. Found while fixing source-fi9u.
close_reason: REM_FILE_$UNLOCK re-emitted from 0x00E61D1C. Request record corrected to the image: version word 3 at +0x18 (move.w #0x3,(-0x158,A6) at 0x00E61D6A), super-mode boolean at +0x1A (sgt at 0x00E61D82 -> move.b at 0x00E61D84), lock_key word at +0x1C (0x00E61D62), release boolean at +0x20 (0x00E61D88); sizeof 0x22 matches the 'move.w #0x22,-(SP)' at 0x00E61DB4 and REM_FILE_$SERVER's own request+0x14/+0x1C/+0x0C/+0x10 unpack. Response is now read at offset 0 of the 0xBE-byte buffer (A6-0xC0) instead of the invented 'bufsize - sizeof(resp)' pointer: dtv +0x08 (tst.l (-0xb8,A6) 0x00E61DD4), result +0x0E (0x00E61E0E), attrs_valid +0x0F (0x00E61DE0), dtu +0x10 (0x00E61DFA). Also: one shared zero word for extra_data/bulk_data/bulk_len (clr.w (-0x178,A6) 0x00E61D8C), signed reply-length compares, AST_$SET_DTS status into a dead local. Public prototype retyped to file_$obj_loc_t* with the arguments renamed rem_key/lock_key/rem_node; file_$obj_loc_t moved from file/file_internal.h to file/file.h since rem_file now needs it. file/verify_lock_holder.c's remote branch rewritten - it passed an 8-byte scratch buffer as the location block (0x00E607C8-0x00E607F8 build a real descriptor at A6-0x30). New rem_file/test/test_unlock.c includes the real .c: 16 tests, 0 failed.

title: disk_$volume_t.lv_shift (+0xa2): what does the LV label's +0x40 word mean?
description: disk/disk_internal.h names disk_$volume_t +0xa2 lv_shift.  Provenance is proven: DISK_$LV_MOUNT stores the logical-volume label word at +0x40 into the new LV descriptor (0x00E6CBEA) and mirrors it into the backing physical volume's descriptor (0x00E6CBF4); DISK_$GET_MNT_INFO is the only reader and reports it at info+0x0c (0x00E6BF04).  No code in the kernel does arithmetic with it, so its meaning is unproven -- disk/lv_mount.c calls the label word a 'shift value'.  Needs a look at invol / the LV label format, or at a Domain/OS user-space consumer of DISK_$GET_MNT_INFO's info+0x0c.  Referenced by TODO(source-9tbm) in disk/disk_internal.h -- retarget that TODO at the new bead.
close_reason: Settled: disk_$volume_t +0xA2 is the BAT step, not a shift; field renamed lv_shift -> bat_step and the TODO(source-9tbm)/TODO(source-zot4) comment in disk/disk_internal.h replaced by the citation.  Three independent sources agree: (1) AEGIS Internals and Data Structures (Jan 1986) 4.3.3 lists the BAT header's fields in exactly the label's order and ends with 'the BAT step to use on this volume', with the glossary 'a bat step of 2 tells the BAT manager to allocate the next block at block n+2.  Users set the bat step, via INVOL, to optimize disk seeks'; (2) this tree's own bat/bat_internal.h already names label +0x40 bat_step -- BAT_$MOUNT defaults it to 3 (bat/mount.c:105), BAT_$DISMOUNT writes it back and BAT_$GET_BAT_STEP returns it, so the BAT manager is the real consumer and the DISK copy exists only for mount info; (3) sr10.4-install sys/help/invol.hlp option 10 'Display/change sector interleave factor for a logical volume ... Note: Option 10 is not supported at SR10.4', with the SR10.2 invol binary still carrying the dialogue ('Current interleave factor is %ld', 'Interval must be 1 on logically addressed disks') and reading it through disk_$get_mnt_info -- which explains why nothing in SR10.4 writes it.  Corroborating arithmetic: DISK_$LV_MOUNT at 0xE6CBC8 adds the label longwords at +0x2C and +0x38 to form the volume end (+0x88), matching the manual's field order for the two BAT-header neighbours.  The word reads 1 in sr103.awd and all three disk-images/harddrive SR10.4 images.  Ghidra annotated at 0xE6CBEA (local label LV_LABEL_BAT_STEP), 0xE6CBF4 and 0xE6BF04.  Follow-up filed: the LV label record is defined twice (disk/lv_mount.c offsets vs bat/bat_internal.h).  Gates: make -k -j8 error/warning grep empty; make test 164 tests, 0 failed.

title: Name 0x00E0AAA6 FIM_$GET_USER_PC (22 bytes, next FIM_ map entry) and emit it; size FIM_CLEANUP_STACK from the image
description: SR10.4 map order for FIM_: ... INIT_PID, FREE_PID, GET_USER_PC.  In SAU2 0x00E0AAA6 (22 bytes) directly follows FIM_$FREE_PID (0x00E0AA6C, 58 bytes) and is still unnamed; rename with gsk and emit fim/get_user_pc.c with a test.  Also: FIM_CLEANUP_STACK in fim/fim_data.c is still a guessed 64 entries; its base 0x00E216B2 does not fit the 58-per-AS chain (0x00E216B2 + 57*4 = 0x00E217B6 = FIM_$PROC2_STARTUP), so derive its real element size/count from the accessing code.  Noted by the source-82nx pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: name/test_lock_dir and vtoc/test_allocate compare status_$t against 64-bit literals
description: base/base.h now has 'typedef int32_t status_$t', so a status with bit 31 set is a NEGATIVE int32.  name/test/test_lock_dir.c:326 and :371 and vtoc/test/test_allocate.c:591 assert against 0x80000007 / 0x800f0002 / 0x80020002 promoted to a wider unsigned type, so they see 0xffffffff80000007 etc. and fail.  3 failures total; the stale binaries built against the older 'typedef long' passed, so this only shows after a clean 'make test'.  Neither subsystem is affected in the .c under test - only the test assertions need to compare as (uint32_t) (or the expected values need to be spelled (int32_t)0x80000007).  Found while closing source-tzmw; name/ and vtoc/ were not touched by that work.
close_reason: test_lock_dir passes after a clean rebuild; test_allocate compares status as uint32_t; Makefile test rule now depends on headers so stale binaries don't recur
